articles.headline: U.S. court sentences Indian national Nikhil Gupta to 235 months in jail
articles.title: U.S. court sentences Indian national Nikhil Gupta to 235 months in jail in Pannun murder plot
articles.summary: A U.S. federal judge sentenced Indian national Nikhil Gupta to 235 months in prison on November 20, 2026. The 55-year-old pleaded guilty to murder-for-hire and money laundering charges related to a plot against Sikh separatist Gurpatwant Singh Pannun in New York. The verdict was delivered by Judge Victor Marrero in the Southern District of New York.
articles.description: Nikhil Gupta pleaded guilty earlier this year to charges of murder-for-hire, conspiracy to commit murder-for-hire, and conspiracy to commit money laundering, in connection with his efforts to murder Khalistani separatist Gurpatwant Singh Pannun in New York

articles.headline: Russian missile violates Polish airspace during military exercises
articles.title: Russian missile hits Poland as Ukraine's allies hold military exercise, says Tusk
articles.summary: Poland reported that a Russian cruise missile was among three objects that breached its airspace on Friday during major aerial attacks on Ukraine. Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk described the incursion as a provocation coinciding with Western military exercises. Nato Secretary General Mark Rutte condemned the grave violations, confirming that alliance jets were scrambled in response to the ongoing regional conflict.
articles.description: Nobody was hurt and no damage has been reported, but Warsaw described the incident as a "provocation" from Moscow.

articles.headline: Ukraine strikes Kerch Bridge and oil facilities as Putin and Trump meet in Shenzhen
articles.title: Ukraine strikes Kerch Bridge as Putin ally declares ‘no one needs Europe’
articles.summary: Ukrainian forces launched a multi-day operation targeting the Kerch Bridge, damaging its road and rail sections, while also striking oil depots and the Rostov-Crimea highway to disrupt Russian supply lines. Meanwhile, Russian President Vladimir Putin and US President Donald Trump met with Chinese leader Xi Jinping in Shenzhen on November 19, discussing peace proposals regarding Ukraine and European security architecture.
articles.description: Russia-Europe tensions rise as Ukraine uses its own weapons and communications tech to hit the Kerch Bridge.

articles.headline: Poland hit by at least one Russian missile, says Polish govt
articles.title: Poland hit by at least one Russian missile, says Polish govt
articles.description: Poland hit by at least one Russian missile, says Polish govt

articles.headline: Russian missile strikes target Kyiv bridges and kill six people
articles.title: Russia targets Kyiv crossings days after Ukraine hits Crimean Bridge
articles.summary: Russia launched nearly one hundred missiles and four hundred drones targeting Ukrainian infrastructure, hitting three Dnipro River bridges in Kyiv and killing six individuals. Additional strikes in Lviv claimed two lives at a railway station, while Polish forces investigated a projectile landing near the border. Officials reported widespread injuries, power disruptions, and ongoing air raid sirens across nine regions.
articles.description: Russia launched one of its biggest air attacks yet as it rejected the prospect of security guarantees for Ukraine.

articles.headline: Russia targets Ukrainian infrastructure and bridges in retaliatory air attacks
articles.title: Russia unleashes retaliatory barrage on Kyiv bridges
articles.summary: Russian air attacks killed eight people and struck transport bridges and energy infrastructure across Ukraine. Prime Minister Sergii Koretskyi reported 28 injuries following the overnight strikes. President Vladimir Putin ordered the retaliation after a bridge linking Russia to Crimea was targeted. Meanwhile, US-led ceasefire efforts continue as officials discuss security guarantees and NATO positions.
articles.description: The attack follows Putin's pledge of 'painful' response to Ukraine's attack on symbolic Crimean bridge.

articles.headline: Russia’s day-long attack on Kyiv damages embassies
articles.title: Russia’s day-long attack on Kyiv damages embassies
articles.description: Russia’s day-long attack on Kyiv damages embassies

articles.headline: Trump, Xi and Putin hold trilateral summit in Shenzhen
articles.title: U.S., China, Russia hold historic summit in Shenzhen
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping, and Russian President Vladimir Putin met in Shenzhen on November 19, 2026, for their first trilateral summit. The three leaders discussed strategic stability, international security, and nuclear risk reduction. According to Mr. Xi, major powers must take legitimate security concerns seriously and resolve differences through dialogue, while emphasizing cooperation to confront global security challenges.
articles.description: The three heads of state — Xi Jinping, Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump — had an in-depth exchange of views on the current international situation and committed to maintaining strategic stability and international security

articles.headline: Anthropic shares soar on Nasdaq debut following record initial public offering
articles.title: Anthropic shares close 17% higher on first day of trading
articles.summary: Artificial intelligence firm Anthropic saw its shares surge thirty four percent during its Nasdaq debut on November nineteen, twenty twenty six, after raising a record eighty one billion dollars. Chief executive Dario Amodei spoke in New York about the company's financial position, while protesters gathered outside and analysts debated market valuations and computing costs.
articles.description: The shares ended the session at around $97, up from an IPO price of $83, after opening at $111.50 and briefly valuing the maker of the Claude chatbot at about $2 trillion

articles.headline: Anthropic prices initial public offering at eighty three dollars per share
articles.title: Anthropic raises $81 billion in IPO amid AI market volatility
articles.summary: Artificial intelligence chatbot Claude developer Anthropic priced its initial public offering at eighty three dollars per share on November eighteen, twenty twenty six, aiming to raise approximately eighty one billion dollars. The listing on the Nasdaq Global Select Market occurs amid broader market volatility and investor scrutiny regarding artificial intelligence infrastructure spending.
articles.description: The Claude maker priced its shares at $83 apiece, implying an equity valuation of about $1.03 trillion based on outstanding shares, with trading scheduled to begin on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT on November 19

articles.headline: European leaders state readiness for peace talks with Russia
articles.title: Europe ready for talks with Russia on ending war in Ukraine, leaders say
articles.summary: European leaders declared their readiness for negotiations with Russia to end the war in Ukraine during a summit in Berlin. US President Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner stated that Russia was comfortable with Ukraine receiving security guarantees, though Russian President Vladimir Putin expressed skepticism and reported attacks on Kyiv and the Crimean Bridge, underscoring ongoing conflict alongside diplomatic discussions.
articles.description: European allies of Ukraine say they have a "united" negotiating position at a summit in Berlin.

articles.headline: Artificial intelligence firm Anthropic achieves $1.76 trillion valuation in stock market debut
articles.title: Anthropic becomes one of world's most valuable public companies in stock market debut
articles.summary: Artificial intelligence enterprise Anthropic reached a valuation of approximately $1.76 trillion following its public stock market debut on the Nasdaq exchange on Thursday. Shares opened at $111.50 before closing at $97, outperforming its allocation price of $83. The milestone occurred amid broader tech sector declines, with executives highlighting safety considerations and upcoming regulatory scrutiny.
articles.description: Anthropic is the first purely AI company to be publicly listed, creating a test for the entire industry.

articles.headline: Jerusalem Daily: Israel launches ground offensive in Gaza
articles.title: Jerusalem Daily: Israel launches ground offensive in Gaza
articles.description: Israel launches its first major ground offensive in central Gaza, pushing beyond the ‘Yellow Line’ it controls

articles.headline: United Nations court rules Myanmar committed genocide against Rohingya minority population
articles.title: Myanmar committed genocide against Rohingya minority, top UN court rules
articles.summary: The International Court of Justice ruled on Thursday that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya minority during a twenty seventeen military crackdown. Court president Yuji Iwasawa cited evidence of intent to destroy the population, marking the first time an international court has found a sovereign state guilty of genocide.
articles.description: The unprecedented International Court of Justice verdict concerns a 2017 military crackdown that killed thousands.

articles.headline: European leaders gather in Berlin to affirm support for Ukraine
articles.title: Kushner says Russia ‘comfortable’ with NATO-like guarantees for Ukraine
articles.summary: European leaders gathered in Berlin for talks on Ukraine following a summit in Shenzhen between Donald Trump, Xi Jinping, and Vladimir Putin. German Chancellor Friedrich Merz and British Prime Minister Andy Burnham stressed Europe must be involved in peace negotiations. French President Emmanuel Macron urged allies to increase military aid and reconsider NATO accession for Ukraine, while Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy called for sustained international pressure on Russia.
articles.description: European leaders meet in Berlin after Trump summit with Putin and Xi. Putin vows to retaliate for Kerch Bridge strikes.

articles.headline: Pakistan climate minister arrives in Delhi for SCO forum
articles.title: Pakistan Climate Minister arrives in Delhi to attend SCO Civilisations Dialogue Forum
articles.summary: Pakistan's Federal Minister for Climate Change and Environmental Coordination, Dr. Musadik Masood Malik, arrived in Delhi on November 20, 2026, to attend the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Civilisational Dialogue Forum. Representing the current CHS chair nation, Mr. Malik joined the cultural meeting inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi at the historic Purana Quila.
articles.description: Pakistan is the current chair of the SCO Council of Heads of State (CHS) (SCO_CHS) for the period of 2026-27; the event, which will be inaugurated by PM Modi, will be held at Delhi’s iconic Purana Quila (Old Fort), a 16th Century fort built by Emperor Humayun

articles.headline: Trump-Xi-Putin summit: Five things you need to know
articles.title: Trump-Xi-Putin summit: Five things you need to know
articles.description: Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin held their first trilateral summit in China.

articles.headline: Spurious liquor consumption kills eleven people in Manipur
articles.title: At least 13 dead after consuming spurious liquor, over 300 hospitalised in Manipur
articles.summary: At least eleven people have died and over three hundred have been hospitalized following the consumption of suspected toxic alcohol in Manipur's Chandel district. Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh visited affected patients at hospitals in Imphal on Friday, November 20, 2026. Authorities deployed medical teams to the area and announced an official inquiry into the incident involving methanol poisoning.
articles.description: Joint managing director of Shija Hospitals, Chetan K, told reporters that the patients admitted to the hospital reported symptoms of dizziness, stomach pain and other complications

articles.headline: China’s Xi urges US and Russia to join forces to safeguard world peace
articles.title: China’s Xi urges US and Russia to join forces to safeguard world peace
articles.description: Chinese President Xi urged US President Trump and Russian President Putin to work with China to safeguard world peace.

articles.headline: Leaders issue joint peace declaration after historic trilateral talks in China
articles.title: Trump, Putin and Xi release 'peace declaration' after historic meeting
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin, and Chinese President Xi Jinping issued a joint peace declaration on Thursday following their first trilateral talks in Shenzhen, China. The ninety minute meeting addressed nuclear proliferation, petroleum production, and the war in Ukraine, drawing mixed reactions from international observers and lawmakers.
articles.description: While the presidents have previously met for one-on-one meetings, this is their first trilateral discussion.

articles.headline: Human and AI solutions for Riemann hypothesis emerge on same day
articles.title: ‘All human, no AI’ Riemann hypothesis proof out on same day as Claude’s claim
articles.summary: On November 20, two proposed solutions to the Riemann hypothesis emerged within hours of each other, highlighting a debate over artificial intelligence in mathematics. Levent Alpöge at Anthropic announced a proof with the AI model Claude, while American Mathematical Society president Ravi Vakil shared a human-only manuscript by Alessandro Maria Masullo from Stanford University.
articles.description: ‘We are still here. We are very much alive. We are not going anywhere,’ mathematician Alessandro Masullo wrote in his paper detailing his efforts to crack mathematics’s greatest unsolved problem

articles.headline: BBC correspondents discuss what Trump, Xi and Putin got out of historic talks
articles.title: BBC correspondents discuss what Trump, Xi and Putin got out of historic talks
articles.description: Trump, Putin and Xi have issued a "joint declaration of peace" after historical trilateral talks, but what did they get out of meeting?

articles.headline: Zelensky labels Putin a killer following Trump remarks
articles.title: Zelensky says Putin is a 'killer' after Trump calls Russian leader a friend
articles.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky condemned Vladimir Putin as an enemy and a killer during a CNN interview after Donald Trump referred to the Russian leader as a friend following trilateral talks in China. The exchange coincided with massive Russian missile and drone strikes across Ukraine that caused civilian casualties, alongside a reported airspace violation in Poland.
articles.description: Earlier this week, Trump greeted Putin ahead of a meeting in China and said the pair have a "great relationship.

articles.headline: Al Jazeera explains: The US-China AI race is entering a new phase
articles.title: Al Jazeera explains: The US-China AI race is entering a new phase
articles.description: Al Jazeera’s Matthew Torres unpacks the latest from the world of artificial intelligence.

articles.headline: Israeli military launches rare ground operation in central Gaza
articles.title: Israeli military completes ground operation in Gaza beyond Yellow Line
articles.summary: Israeli forces initiated a targeted ground operation in the central Gaza Strip on Wednesday, advancing tanks near the Nuseirat refugee camp and closing a section of the Salah al-Din road. According to the Israeli military, the objective was to dismantle a tunnel. Hamas condemned the incursion as a ceasefire violation, while Gaza's Civil Defence agency reported three deaths from separate drone strikes.
articles.description: Hamas condemned the incursion, which the Israeli military said was to dismantle a "terror tunnel", as a "flagrant" ceasefire violation.

articles.headline: Anthropic begins trading on Nasdaq following massive public offering debut
articles.title: Anthropic starts trading in the US after blockbuster IPO
articles.summary: Artificial intelligence developer Anthropic launched trading on the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT after executing a historic public offering. The company priced ninety eight crore shares at eighty three dollars each, achieving a valuation of two trillion dollars while facing scrutiny over potential technological risks and net losses.
articles.description: Anthropic’s IPO surpasses SpaceX, marking the largest initial public offering in US history at $81bn.

articles.headline: India awaits concrete details following trilateral summit between US, Russia, and China
articles.title: India ‘takes note’ of Trump-Xi-Putin summit, awaits more details
articles.summary: Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal stated on November 20, 2026, that India has taken note of the recent trilateral summit held in Shenzhen between American, Russian, and Chinese leaders. While awaiting further details of the meeting outcomes, officials emphasized India's separate engagements through the Quad framework following criticism from domestic opposition politicians.
articles.description: Opposition questions why India not present at 'G-3' global power summit in Shenzhen; Ministry cites ‘concrete outcomes’ of Quad Summit held earlier in the week

articles.headline: Anthropic goes public on Nasdaq with ticker ANT
articles.title: Anthropic starts trading on Wall Street
articles.summary: Artificial intelligence firm Anthropic began trading on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol ANT at $111.50 per share, following its initial $83 per share price. CEO Dario Amodei stated that the company will pace its AI training to ensure safety and maintain human control. The firm previously reported a net loss of $80.7 billion in the first half of the year alongside $16.3 billion in revenue.
articles.description: Anthropic has officially gone public. It began trading on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol "ANT" at $111.50 per share, up from its initial $83 per share price that put company's value at around $1.5 trillion. The listing comes nearly a month after Anthropic revealed its plans to go public. In its lengthy S-1 filing, […]

articles.headline: Los Angeles jury convicts man of starting deadly wildfire
articles.title: Man convicted of starting Palisades fire in Los Angeles
articles.summary: Jonathan Rinderknecht was found guilty of two federal charges for starting the January wildfire in Pacific Palisades and Malibu that killed twelve people and destroyed thousands of structures. The conviction follows a previous mistrial. Prosecutors presented geolocation and camera evidence showing he targeted the area out of anger. Sentencing is scheduled for March seventeen.
articles.description: The 30-year-old LA resident was convicted of arson leading to wildfires that killed 12 people and destroyed more than 6,800 buildings.

articles.headline: Saudi-led coalition intercepts three Houthi missiles targeting Riyadh
articles.title: Saudi-led coalition intercepts three Houthi missiles headed for Riyadh
articles.summary: The Saudi-led coalition intercepted three ballistic missiles fired by Houthi rebels toward Riyadh following multiple emergency alerts in the capital. The attack follows previous strikes on infrastructure. Coalition spokesperson Turki al-Malki stated that retaliatory special operations targeted smuggling capabilities at the Red Sea port of Hodeidah, prompting concern from the United Nations regarding humanitarian supply routes.
articles.description: Saudi Arabia issues emergency alerts in Riyadh for third night in row, as the Houthis threaten ports and power station.

articles.headline: Anthropic researcher claims solution to Riemann hypothesis using artificial intelligence
articles.title: AI cracks math’s most famous problem. Have mathematicians lost a guiding light?
articles.summary: Levent Alpöge of artificial intelligence firm Anthropic announced on November 20, 2026, that he generated a proof for the Riemann hypothesis using the Claude model. The researcher published 1.7 crore lines of code without a traditional paper. Independent mathematicians and proof systems verified the code passes checks, though the Clay Mathematics Institute bounty remains pending for the unsolved mathematical problem.
articles.description: Levent Alpöge of Anthropic has announced that he and the company’s AI model Claude have found a proof of the Riemann hypothesis, which concerns the distribution of prime numbers. Mathematicians have spent more than 160 years trying to prove it

articles.headline: World Court finds Myanmar forces killed thousands of Rohingya
articles.title: Myanmar guilty of genocide against Rohingya, says top UN court
articles.summary: Judges at the International Court of Justice ruled on Thursday, November 19, 2026, that Myanmar security forces killed thousands of Rohingya civilians and committed widespread sexual violence. According to court president Yuji Iwasawa, evidence supports the estimate of 10,000 violent deaths during 2017 clearance operations, as well as attacks on people fleeing toward Bangladesh. The UN tribunal has not yet ruled on whether genocide occurred.
articles.description: The ruling by the top UN court was the first time in its 80-year history that ICJ judges have determined that a state committed genocide, and is likely to be seen as justice for Rohingya victims of Myanmar’s brutal 2017 crackdown

articles.headline: FBI investigates suspected breach of criminal information database
articles.title: FBI's criminal information database hacked, reports say
articles.summary: The Federal Bureau of Investigation is probing an apparent compromise of the National Crime Information Center database used by law enforcement agencies, according to reports on Friday, November 20, 2026. This potential incident follows a recent string of high-profile cyber disruptions, including a September breach affecting an FBI jobs website by the extortion group ShinyHunters.
articles.description: The apparent compromise of the National ‌Crime Information Center database would ‌mark ⁠the second intrusion involving ⁠an FBI system in recent months

articles.headline: Saudi-led coalition intercepts three ballistic missiles targeted at Riyadh
articles.title: Saudi-led coalition says downed 3 Houthi missiles headed for Riyadh
articles.summary: Air defences intercepted three ballistic missiles launched toward Riyadh on November 21, 2026, according to the Saudi-led coalition. Authorities briefly issued an alert for a hostile aerial threat before civil defence declared the danger had passed. Yemen's Houthis claimed responsibility for the strikes, which followed coalition attacks on the Red Sea port city of Hodeida on November 20, 2026.
articles.description: Yemen's Houthis said on X that they were striking targets across Saudi Arabia, including in Riyadh

articles.headline: Gen Z protests sweep Europe over wars, rising costs and climate
articles.title: Gen Z protests sweep Europe over wars, rising costs and climate
articles.description: Thousands of Gen Z protesters rallied across 25 European countries over living costs, military spending and climate.

articles.headline: Anthropic faces governance scrutiny following record public offering
articles.title: With the biggest IPO of all time, Anthropic’s ‘good guy’ reputation is on the line
articles.summary: Artificial intelligence lab Anthropic completed a record initial public offering raising $81.3 billion, though legal experts and industry watchdogs questioned the oversight power of its Long-Term Benefit Trust. Critics noted that the structure, designed to protect safety missions, grants founders and trustees complex voting controls while leaving actual artificial intelligence expertise among trustees open to debate.
articles.description: Today is a new beginning for Anthropic: a years-in-the-making IPO that beat out SpaceX for most valuable of all time, having raised $81.3 billion and set an important precedent for the other public AI lab debuts to come. But it's not simply a financial milestone. Anthropic was founded on the idea that it prioritized safety […]

articles.headline: Trump highlights trade deals and low interest rates during Washington briefing
articles.title: ‘Look at India, they have low interest rates’: Trump says U.S. could achieve 14–15% economic growth
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump announced new trade agreements with Thailand and the Philippines while speaking at the White House on November 20, 2026. He noted that lower interest rates could help the United States achieve significantly higher economic growth. Additionally, he discussed cooperation measures agreed upon during a recent meeting with leaders of the Quad alliance.
articles.description: “In four days, I met more than 20 world leaders, secured two new trade deals, and about 10 others coming very soon,” Donald Trump told a press conference at the White House in Washington

articles.headline: Donald Trump calls for Nvidia to reinstate Jensen Huang
articles.title: Trump calls for Nvidia to reinstate ‘brilliant’ Jensen Huang
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump stated he would support Jensen Huang returning as chief executive officer of Nvidia following his resignation on November 12 over a scandal involving affairs and a suspected Chinese spy. Despite Trump backing Huang and commerce secretary Howard Lutnick, Nvidia board chairperson Harvey Jones confirmed the directors unanimously rejected a reinstatement.
articles.description: US president calls tech giant to give former CEO 'a second chance' and urges him to 'make a big apology'.

articles.headline: COP31 deal stalls as nations struggle to agree on climate plan
articles.title: COP31 deal stalls as nations struggle to agree on climate plan
articles.description: COP31 deal stalls as nations struggle to agree on climate plan

articles.headline: India maintains consistent position on Indus Waters Treaty amid Delhi forum visit
articles.title: India says no change in its position on Indus Water Treaty as Pakistan minister attends SCO forum in Delhi
articles.summary: India stated that its stance on the Indus Waters Treaty remains unchanged during a media briefing by Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal on November 20, 2026. This development coincided with Pakistan Minister Musadik Malik visiting New Delhi to attend the SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi at Purana Quila.
articles.description: India suspended the treaty in 2025 as one of the punitive measures against Pakistan after the April 22 Pahalgam terror attack last year that claimed 26 lives

articles.headline: Denmark expels Russian defence attaché following alleged assassination plot in Copenhagen
articles.title: Denmark expels Russian diplomat over alleged plot to kill Ukrainian rapper
articles.summary: Danish Foreign Minister Lars Lokke Rasmussen announced the expulsion of Russia's defence attaché after intelligence officials uncovered a suspected plot to kill a Ukrainian rapper at a concert near Copenhagen. Danish police arrested two suspects linked to the conspiracy, while European leaders condemned the operation as aggressive Russian hybrid warfare.
articles.description: Copenhagen accuses Moscow of planning assassination with banned local gang; Russia says no evidence for allegation.

articles.headline: Leaders of US, China and Russia issue peace declaration in Shenzhen
articles.title: ‘Groundbreaking’ Trump-Xi-Putin summit: Five key takeaways
articles.summary: Presidents Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin held an unprecedented trilateral summit in Shenzhen, China, releasing a joint declaration focused on stabilizing energy flows and preventing nuclear proliferation. The leaders also criticized the International Criminal Court, while European officials met in Berlin to coordinate ongoing support for Ukraine amid global conflicts.
articles.description: Leaders hailed the unprecedented meeting as historic, with discussions spanning nuclear risks to energy flows.

articles.headline: Congress proposes four-point formula for delimitation with INDIA bloc support
articles.title: Congress proposes four-point formula for delimitation, says INDIA bloc on board
articles.summary: The Congress party proposed a four-point formula for upcoming parliamentary delimitation, suggesting the retention of 543 Lok Sabha seats, the preservation of current state-wise distribution, the reservation of one-third of seats for women, and a twenty-five-year freeze on these arrangements. Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh stated that all parties in the Indian National Developmental Inclusive Alliance (INDIA) supported the approach, accusing the government of failing to consult the opposition.
articles.description: Party proposes retaining 543 Lok Sabha seats, existing State-wise distribution and a 25-year freeze, with one-third reservation for women

articles.headline: Prime Minister Narendra Modi calls cultural connect global peace guarantee
articles.title: PM Modi says cultural connect can guarantee global peace
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi stated that cultural connections are the biggest guarantee of global peace while speaking at the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation civilisational dialogue forum in New Delhi on Friday. The event features Pakistan's participation for the first time since a May 2025 conflict, with Pakistan represented by Federal Minister Musadik Masood Malik. Modi proposed that Shanghai Cooperation Organisation member countries collaborate on digitising and translating ancient texts.
articles.description: Cultural and civilisational cooperation will strengthen relations among various countries, says Modi at SCO forum; Pakistan Minister to address meet on November 21

articles.headline: ICJ rules Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya
articles.title: ICJ rules Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya
articles.description: The ICJ has ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya in northern Rakhine State.

articles.headline: Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah begins bilateral visit to India
articles.title: A new Nepal, an old neighbour - Balendra Shah's India test on first visit
articles.summary: Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah arrived in Delhi for a two-day visit to meet Indian counterpart Narendra Modi, marking the first engagement between the new political generation and India. Discussions cover economic cooperation, energy, air corridors, and reconstruction aid following devastating flash floods in August that killed over 1,450 people. The visit aims to reset bilateral ties and address long-standing strategic, border, and trade differences.
articles.description: Trade, connectivity and regional cooperation will be on top of the agenda when Nepal's PM meets his India counterpart.

articles.headline: Anthropic employee claims chatbot used to prove Riemann hypothesis
articles.title: In a year of AI solving maths problems, Anthropic may have just solved the biggest
articles.summary: An Anthropic employee and mathematician stated that he used the non-public version of the company's Claude chatbot to create a detailed proof of the 170-year-old Riemann hypothesis over six weeks. Released in the Lean computer language, the proof spans more than 250,000 lines. Prominent mathematician Terence Tao noted that formal verification will take time, while other scholars have raised concerns regarding AI-driven mathematical claims.
articles.description: A mathematician at Anthropic says he used an AI to prove the famed Riemann hypothesis, though verification will take some time.

articles.headline: COP31 climate summit enters overtime amid fossil fuel deadlock
articles.title: Fossil fuel talks deadlock pushes COP31 climate summit into overtime
articles.summary: The COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkiye, extended into overtime after nearly two million delegates remained deadlocked over a draft text that omitted fossil fuel phase-outs. The initial draft called for a faster transition away from fossil fuels, but references were removed following objections from Saudi Arabia and other major oil producers, drawing strong criticism from the European Union, Panama, and environmental groups.
articles.description: EU warns COP31 risks turning into a 'fossil summit' as critical climate commitments are omitted from the draft deal.

articles.headline: UN court convicts Myanmar of genocidal intent against Rohingya
articles.title: UN’s top court finds Myanmar guilty of genocide against Rohingya
articles.summary: The International Court of Justice found Myanmar guilty of genocidal intent regarding military operations in 2017 that caused 10,000 Rohingya deaths and forced more than 730,000 people to flee into Bangladesh. Delivering the verdict on Thursday, November 19, 2026, court president Yuji Iwasawa stated that security forces attacked civilians and violated prevention obligations. The case was initially brought by The Gambia in 2019.
articles.description: The ruling marks the first time a state has been found responsible for genocide by the International Court of Justice.

articles.headline: US lawmakers push for tougher AI chip rules amid China concerns
articles.title: US lawmakers push for tougher AI chip rules amid China export crackdown
articles.summary: United States lawmakers are calling for stricter regulations to prevent advanced artificial intelligence chips from reaching China through third countries. The Department of Commerce introduced a rule requiring special licences for data centres in specific nations. Meanwhile, a congressional probe is investigating whether Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick blocked previous export curbs as officials debate broader national security measures.
articles.description: Washington has new rules restricting remote access to advanced US AI chips, but lawmakers want more.

articles.headline: Houthi rebel forces tighten siege on Yemeni city of Taiz
articles.title: 'I tell my son it's just fireworks': Life inside Yemeni city besieged by Houthis
articles.summary: Houthi rebel fighters have fully encircled the government-controlled city of Taiz, cutting off supplies and leaving residents facing severe shortages of food, medicine, and water. According to local officials and emergency room staff, civilians continue to suffer heavy casualties from ongoing shelling and sniper fire, while Houthi leadership has denied that the strategic Yemeni city is facing a blockade.
articles.description: Orla Guerin speaks to seven people trapped in the key city of Taiz, cut off from the outside world for weeks.

articles.headline: Denmark accuses Russia of plotting to assassinate Ukrainian-American rapper
articles.title: Denmark accuses Russia of plotting to assassinate US-Ukrainian rapper
articles.summary: Denmark has accused Russian intelligence services of planning to kill Ukrainian-American rapper Albert Vasiliev, also known as Kyivstoner, at a Copenhagen concert. Security forces stopped three suspects on 25 September, leading to two attempted murder charges. Foreign Minister Lars Lokke Rasmussen announced the expulsion of Russia's defence attache following the incident, while the Russian embassy rejected the allegations.
articles.description: The Russian embassy in Denmark has denied the allegation, which has led to Russia's defence attaché being expelled.

articles.headline: UK and EU reach post-Brexit agreement following Brussels summit
articles.title: What the new UK-EU deal could mean for future post-Brexit relations
articles.summary: The United Kingdom and the European Union reached an agreement strengthening post-Brexit relations during a Brussels summit on Friday. The pact addresses British food exports, emissions trading, and a youth experience scheme. While Prime Minister Andy Burnham and European Council President Antonio Costa welcomed the accord, opposition figures Kemi Badenoch and Nigel Farage sharply criticised the terms.
articles.description: The BBC's political and Europe editors analyse the new agreements between the UK and EU.

articles.headline: Trump threatens tax on US tech firms building AI data centres abroad
articles.title: Trump threatens tax on US tech firms building AI data centres abroad
articles.description: US President Donald Trump warned US tech companies will face “a tremendous tax” if they build AI data centres abroad.

articles.headline: Trump defends Russia relationship and warns tech companies against overseas data centres.
articles.title: Trump defends Putin relationship, warns AI data centres must stay in US
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump defended his ties with Russian leader Vladimir Putin during a White House briefing on Friday. Trump warned domestic technology companies against building artificial intelligence data centres overseas, threatening them with severe penalties. He also discussed international diplomatic efforts involving China and Iran alongside several cabinet officials.
articles.description: The US president also spoke about the war in Iran and praised trip to China during a wide-ranging news conference.

articles.headline: Donald Trump threatens tax and ban on US companies building overseas data centres
articles.title: Trump threatens ban on US firms building AI data centres overseas
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump announced plans to ban American tech companies from constructing artificial intelligence data centres overseas, warning of a heavy tax for non-compliance. The policy targets foreign investments by firms like Meta and Google, such as a recently halted project in Finland, as Washington seeks to prevent China from gaining dominance in the artificial intelligence sector.
articles.description: The US president provided little detail on the potential policy, saying others in his team were hearing about it for the first time.

articles.headline: United States, Russia and China leaders hold trilateral talks in Shenzhen
articles.title: Trump meets Putin and Xi for trilateral US, Russia, China talks at APEC
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump met with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin on Thursday at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, China. The historic gathering featured discussions on nuclear weapons and the war in Ukraine. Analysts noted that major agreements were unlikely due to deep disagreements among the three superpowers.
articles.description: US president calls both Putin and Xi a 'friend' in separate meetings ahead of rare three-way talks in China.

articles.headline: Trump greets 'my friend' Putin as pair shake hands
articles.title: Trump greets 'my friend' Putin as pair shake hands
articles.description: The pair met ahead of a trilateral meeting later with Chinese leader Xi Jinping.

articles.headline: Israeli drone strikes kill seven Palestinians in central Gaza amid ceasefire violations
articles.title: Israeli drone attacks kill seven Palestinians in central Gaza
articles.summary: Israeli drone attacks across the central Gaza Strip killed at least seven Palestinians and wounded others, striking areas including the Bureij and Nuseirat refugee camps and Deir el-Balah. Medical facilities operated at reduced capacity due to shortages, while military demolition operations continued near the Yellow Line, bringing total Palestinian casualties from ongoing military actions past 74,000 since October 2023.
articles.description: Drones cause 'fear and panic' among Palestinians as Israel continues attacks on the Strip despite 'ceasefire'.

articles.headline: Palestinian anti-Hamas armed groups accused of coordinating with Israeli military in Gaza
articles.title: Palestinian anti-Hamas groups accused of role in Israel Gaza operation
articles.summary: Palestinian security sources and political analysts accused Israeli-backed local armed groups of participating in a recent Israeli military operation in central Gaza by terrorising civilians and forcing evacuations. Operating under Israeli fire cover, these factions expanded their activities from the south to central Gaza, raising concerns that Israel aims to establish permanent local security influence.
articles.description: Israeli-backed Palestinian militias accused of expanding operations, raising concerns over their role in Gaza’s security

articles.headline: Core sector growth hits record 10.9% in October 2026
articles.title: Infra push and low base effect pushes core sector growth to series-high of 10.9% in October 2026
articles.summary: India experienced a significant economic surge as output in key industries reached a series-high of 10.9% in October 2026, according to data from the Ministry of Commerce and Industry. Driven primarily by electricity generation and coal production, experts noted the performance also benefited from a low base effect following weak growth in the previous year.
articles.description: While the coal and electricity sectors saw growth shoot up, a large part of this was due to a statistical effect rather than growth in actual output. On the other hand, fuel-related sectors contracted again

articles.headline: Indian national sentenced to 19 years in US assassination plot
articles.title: Indian man sentenced to 19 years in US Sikh separatist assassination plot
articles.summary: Nikhil Gupta received a prison sentence of over nineteen years in Manhattan federal court after pleading guilty to conspiring to assassinate a Sikh separatist leader in New York City. US District Judge Victor Marrero handed down the penalty on Friday following a murder-for-hire plot involving an undercover officer posing as a hitman.
articles.description: Nikhil Gupta jailed for conspiring to hire a hitman to kill New York-based Sikh leader, Gurpatwant Singh Pannun.

articles.headline: Anthropic raises 81.3 billion dollars in record initial public offering
articles.title: Charting the world’s biggest IPOs as Anthropic overtakes SpaceX
articles.summary: Artificial intelligence firm Anthropic raised 81.3 billion dollars in the largest initial public offering in history on Wednesday, pricing shares at 83 dollars each on the Nasdaq in New York. Founded in 2021 by seven former OpenAI employees including Dario and Daniela Amodei, the company reached a valuation of roughly 1.5 trillion dollars, overtaking SpaceX to become the world's twelfth-biggest company according to the report.
articles.description: The AI company behind Claude raised $81.3bn in the largest initial public offering ever, at a $1.5 trillion valuation.

articles.headline: Indian man sentenced to over nineteen years for assassination plot
articles.title: Indian man sentenced to 19-plus years in plot to assassinate US-based Sikh separatist leader
articles.summary: A federal judge sentenced Indian national Nikhil Gupta to 235 months in prison on Friday following his guilty plea to murder-for-hire charges and conspiracy involving a plan to kill American citizen and Sikh separatist Gurpatwant Singh Pannun. US prosecutors alleged that Gupta was directed by Indian intelligence officer Vikash Yadav to target Pannun in New York. The case involved an undercover Drug Enforcement Agency officer and followed Gupta's June 2023 arrest in Prague and subsequent extradition.
articles.description: Nikhil Gupta pleaded guilty to murder-for-hire, conspiracy to commit murder-for-hire, and conspiracy to commit money laundering in February.

articles.headline: Podcast discusses implications of ICJ Rohingya genocide ruling
articles.title: What are the implications of the ICJ Rohingya genocide ruling?
articles.summary: This news audio segment explores the consequences of the International Court of Justice ruling that Myanmar committed genocide against its Muslim Rohingya minority. Presenter James Bays and guests examine the potential legal and geopolitical impact of the decision, including possible implications for Israel and the ongoing situation in Gaza.
articles.description: Verdict against Myanmar may have implications for Israel's genocide in Gaza.

articles.headline: Trump threatens heavy tax on artificial intelligence data centers built abroad
articles.title: Trump threatens ‘tremendous tax’ for moving AI data centers outside the US
articles.summary: President Donald Trump announced a potential heavy tax on companies constructing artificial intelligence data centers outside the United States during a press conference in Washington. Flanked by Vice President JD Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Trump warned that failing to keep infrastructure domestic would allow China to dominate the sector. The proposal follows growing local restrictions on data centers nationwide and faces a potential challenge from a newly sworn-in Congress.
articles.description: President Donald Trump promised to put a "tremendous tax" on companies that build data centers outside of the US, even as states and cities around the country are placing restrictions on new applications to build them. "We're not going to allow our companies to build data centers outside of our country," Trump said at a […]

articles.headline: ‘It’s my friend’: Moment Trump greets Putin at China summit
articles.title: ‘It’s my friend’: Moment Trump greets Putin at China summit
articles.description: ‘It’s my friend’: Moment Trump greets Putin at China summit

articles.headline: Anthropic mathematician claims Claude chatbot solved Riemann Hypothesis
articles.title: Anthropic researcher says Claude solved maths’ greatest riddle
articles.summary: Anthropic researcher Levent Alpoge announced that he used the firm artificial intelligence chatbot Claude to prove the Riemann Hypothesis, a prominent mathematical problem regarding prime numbers first proposed in 1859. The unverified claim was released in a four-page note on Friday. The hypothesis is one of seven Millennium Prize Problems carrying a one million dollar reward from the Clay Mathematics Institute, which requires peer-reviewed publication and two years of scrutiny.
articles.description: First proposed by German mathematician Bernhard Riemann in 1859, the hypothesis concerns the distribution of prime numbers and is widely regarded as the most important open question in pure mathematics

articles.headline: Cyclone Akvan makes landfall along north Andhra Pradesh and south Odisha coasts
articles.title: Cyclone ‘Akvan’ crosses Odisha coast, no damage reported
articles.summary: According to the India Meteorological Department, the severe cyclonic storm Akvan entered the north Andhra Pradesh and south Odisha coasts on November 20, 2026. Moving from the westcentral Bay of Bengal at twenty-one kilometres per hour, the system weakened into a cyclonic storm and is expected to cross near Gopalpur with winds reaching up to ninety kilometres per hour, bringing heavy rain to coastal districts.
articles.description: Ganjam district and its adjoining areas receive heavy rainfall, with Patrapur (209 mm) recording the highest; several districts of West Bengal are battered by rain and flight and train services affected

articles.headline: New METR evaluation shows artificial intelligence models lag in judgment tasks
articles.title: The most misunderstood graph in AI just got a major update
articles.summary: A report from the artificial intelligence evaluation nonprofit METR indicates that while model capabilities continue an exponential trajectory on verifiable tasks like coding, they still fall short on open-ended tasks requiring human judgment. Researchers tested models on designing evaluations and scoring philosophical arguments, finding that frontier systems struggle with tasks essential for automating research. Experts note that while progress on verifiable tasks remains rapid, predicting future advancements in judgment-heavy domains is difficult.
articles.description: A new report from the AI evaluation nonprofit METR finds that some AI capabilities are continuing to improve along an exponential trajectory—but it also indicates that models aren’t quite as good at tasks that require judgment as they are at coding. The report is an update to the organization’s time horizon plot, which was widely…

articles.headline: UK prime minister explores closer European Union ties after agreement
articles.title: UK to explore even closer ties with EU after agreeing deal, says Burnham
articles.summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham stated the United Kingdom will discuss options for closer ties with the European Union after agreeing to a deal covering food exports, emissions trading, and a youth experience scheme. European Council President Antonio Costa noted the European Union remains open to close relations, while critics such as Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch condemned the agreement. Legislation to implement the deal is expected to be introduced in the United Kingdom Parliament next week.
articles.description: The UK-EU deal agreed on Friday covers British food exports, emissions trading and a youth experience scheme.

articles.headline: Anthropic shares drop after historic Wall Street market debut
articles.title: US tech sell-off continues as Anthropic tumbles after mega IPO
articles.summary: Anthropic experienced a stock price decline on Friday in New York, trading 9.5 percent down at $87.95 by 11:30 am. The drop followed a record public offering that had briefly surpassed $2 trillion in value. Major technology stocks and chip makers also fell during the broader sell-off, with Nvidia down nearly 7 percent and AMD sliding 11.2 percent, driven by investor concerns regarding high market values and heavy artificial intelligence spending.
articles.description: Anthropic's listing had been viewed as a potential boost for an industry struggling to regain its footing.

articles.headline: Estonia closes road border crossings with Russia for six months
articles.title: Estonia to close border with Russia, Moscow decries 'new Iron Curtain'
articles.summary: Estonia will shut its road border crossings with Russia on December 1 for at least six months on security grounds, according to the government. Interior Minister Igor Taro stated the measure limits Russia's ability to organise further attacks after an alleged arson attempt on a defence company. Moscow condemned the decision as an attempt to erect a new Iron Curtain, threatening political and diplomatic responses.
articles.description: NATO and EU member ‌Estonia on November 15 accused Russian security services of staging an attempted ‌arson ⁠attack on an Estonian defence company, in what it said ⁠was the second such incident this year

articles.headline: Watch: Trump, Xi and Putin to hold historic trilateral talks in China on APEC sidelines
articles.title: Watch: Trump, Xi and Putin to hold historic trilateral talks in China on APEC sidelines
articles.description: U.S. President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping, and Russian President Vladimir Putin are set to hold a landmark trilateral meeting in Shenzhen, China, on Thursday, November 19, on the sidelines of the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting. The gathering is historic because it brings together the heads of the world’s three most influential military powers in a formal three-way setting for the first time amid deep global fractures.

articles.headline: Saudi-led coalition targets Hodeida port in ongoing Yemen attacks
articles.title: Saudi-led coalition says targeted Yemen's Hodeida, other attacks 'ongoing'
articles.summary: The Saudi-led coalition fighting Yemen's Houthis conducted airstrikes targeting Hodeida port and other sites on Friday. Coalition spokesman Turki al-Malki stated via social media that the operations targeted operational capabilities used in smuggling and weapons transport. The military actions are ongoing across Sanaa, Saada, and Taiz governorates following reprisal warnings from the Houthi group.
articles.description: We targeted operational capabilities at Hodeidah port that were used in smuggling operations and the transport of weapons and ballistic missiles, said spokesman

articles.headline: Nepal prime minister to visit India on November 22
articles.title: Nepal PM Balendra Shah to visit India on November 22-23
articles.summary: Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah will undertake a state visit to India from November 22 to November 23 at the invitation of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, as announced by Foreign Secretary Amrit Bahadur Rai. Mr. Modi will hold bilateral talks with Mr. Shah in New Delhi on November 23 to review relations, while the leaders will also inaugurate several energy projects.
articles.description: In his first India visit, Nepal Prime Minister is expected to sign several MoUs and inaugurate projects

articles.headline: UK and EU plan youth mobility scheme during Brussels summit
articles.title: U.K., EU move closer together with deals on food, carbon permits and youth mobility
articles.summary: United Kingdom Prime Minister Andy Burnham met with European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen in Brussels to discuss closer ties. The leaders are expected to announce a mobility scheme allowing young adults to live and work across borders. Discussions also cover food prices, carbon trading, and migration, though the Labour government maintains strict red lines regarding the single market and free movement.
articles.description: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham, who travelled to Brussels for the Summit, said this was the “limit” of what the two sides would converge during this Parliament (U.K.), i.e., until 2029

articles.headline: Trump wants to talk nuclear with Putin and Xi
articles.title: Trump wants to talk nuclear with Putin and Xi
articles.description: US President Donald Trump says he plans to raise nuclear non-proliferation with China’s Xi and Russia’s Putin.

articles.headline: Xi Jinping secures historic meeting with Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump in Shenzhen
articles.title: This is a remarkable diplomatic moment for China's Xi - but it comes with pitfalls
articles.summary: Chinese leader Xi Jinping has hosted a trilateral summit in Shenzhen with United States President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin, aiming to project global influence ahead of next year's Communist Party Congress. The meeting addressed nuclear arms control and geopolitical tensions, while presenting significant domestic and international challenges for Beijing amid ongoing economic pressures and global diplomatic balancing acts.
articles.description: The meeting comes with challenges as there are things Xi does not appear keen to discuss with Putin and Trump.

articles.headline: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham announces new deals with European Union
articles.title: 10 years after divisive Brexit referendum, UK weighs a ‘Breturn’ to the EU
articles.summary: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced a series of agreements with the European Union on Friday following a summit in Brussels with European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen. The deals aim to ease trade restrictions, expand youth opportunities, and address carbon levies to rebuild relations a decade after the Brexit referendum. Polling expert Sir John Curtice noted that surveys show average support of 62 percent for rejoining the bloc among decided respondents.
articles.description: Prime Minister Andy Burnham returns from the UK-EU summit with a potential new deal and a new start.

articles.headline: Anthropic mathematician claims to have solved the Riemann hypothesis using AI
articles.title: Anthropic mathematician claims to have solved prestigious Millennium Prize problem with Claude
articles.summary: Mathematician Levent Alpöge of the AI company Anthropic claims he has proved the Riemann hypothesis, a major Millennium Prize problem, with assistance from the AI model Claude. The proof remains unverified by the global mathematics community. Alpöge stated he formalized the arguments without assumptions, though independent experts have not yet confirmed the validity of his findings.
articles.description: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge claims he has proved the Riemann hypothesis, one of mathematics's most notoriously difficult problems, with the help of Claude, cracking a puzzle that has eluded some of the world's best mathematicians for decades. If verified, it would mark yet another seismic achievement for AI in mathematics and add to the upheaval […]

articles.headline: South African police report nearly 600 women killed between July and September
articles.title: Nearly 600 women killed in South Africa within three months
articles.summary: Official crime statistics revealed that 581 women were killed in South Africa between July and September, including 131 in Gauteng province. The figures encompass 13 victims found partially naked near Johannesburg, sparking national outrage. Acting Police Minister Firoz Cachalia called for enhanced prevention efforts as authorities investigate recent mass shootings and gender-based violence across the country.
articles.description: Police officials called for "greater efforts to prevent... violence" against women and children.

articles.headline: One third of attacks on children worldwide recorded in Palestine
articles.title: One third of attacks on children worldwide recorded in Palestine
articles.description: Almost one in three reported violations against children worldwide occurred in Palestine in 2025.

articles.headline: Jerusalem Daily: Palestinians return home to ruins
articles.title: Jerusalem Daily: Palestinians return home to ruins
articles.description: Palestinians return to find their homes reduced to rubble after Israel’s ground offensive, as attacks on Gaza continue.

articles.headline: Poland reports Russian airspace violations during military exercises
articles.title: Poland condemns Russian ‘provocation’ after airspace violations
articles.summary: Poland reported three Russian airspace incursions involving two missiles and a drone overnight, which Prime Minister Donald Tusk described as a provocation. Defence Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz confirmed investigations are ongoing at three locations. The incident occurred during military exercises involving NATO allies, prompting calls for increased security support along the alliance's eastern flank from Warsaw.
articles.description: The incidents came as European troops were taking part in a Ukraine post-war military exercise.

articles.headline: Russia targets Kyiv and railway stations in massive missile assault
articles.title: What we know about the latest Russian missile strikes on Ukraine
articles.summary: Russian forces launched a nationwide missile assault targeting bridges in Kyiv and railway stations overnight. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky described the operation as one of the heaviest strikes of the war, resulting in at least nine deaths. According to the BBC, the attack followed a recent explosion on the Crimean Bridge and coincided with diplomatic talks regarding security guarantees.
articles.description: Russia struck bridges and railway stations in the capital Kyiv in a major attack.

articles.headline: China’s Xi greets Putin and Trump at APEC before historic summit
articles.title: China’s Xi greets Putin and Trump at APEC before historic summit
articles.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping greeted Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin at APEC summit.

articles.headline: Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping hold trilateral meeting in Shenzhen
articles.title: What do Trump, Putin and Xi want from their Shenzhen meeting?
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin have convened for a rare three-way meeting on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen. Analysts note that the leaders arrived with competing objectives, ranging from trade and technology controls to ongoing conflicts in Ukraine and the Middle East, with expectations remaining low for major diplomatic breakthroughs.
articles.description: The US, Chinese and Russian leaders are to hold their first three-way talks on the sidelines of the APEC summit.

articles.headline: Saudi-led coalition and Houthi rebels exchange threats to bomb ports
articles.title: Saudi coalition and Houthis exchange threats to bomb key ports
articles.summary: Yemen's Houthi rebels and the Saudi Arabia-led coalition have exchanged threats to strike key ports, escalating their ongoing conflict. The Houthis threatened to target Saudi Red Sea ports following coalition strikes on the Houthi-held port of Hodeidah. Both sides have intensified aerial operations, with the coalition targeting Houthi ballistic missile and drone capabilities across several governorates.
articles.description: Yemen's Houthis have warned airlines of military activity in Saudi airspace in the coming hours.

articles.headline: Supreme Court dismisses Tamil Nadu plea for additional Cauvery water
articles.title: Cauvery verdict is a reflection of the dire ground reality in Karnataka: Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar
articles.summary: The Supreme Court on November 20 rejected Tamil Nadu's request for more Cauvery water, citing Karnataka's own severe drinking water shortages. Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar stated the verdict reflects ground reality, noting the state lacks sufficient reserves. Karnataka officials emphasized the need for a scientific distress-sharing formula to balance the needs of both states.
articles.description: The Supreme Court on Friday dismissed a plea by Tamil Nadu claiming that Karnataka has to make good a shortfall of 16.01 tmcft (later modified to 11.719 tmcft) of Cauvery water on a pro rata basis during the current irrigation year of 2026-27.

articles.headline: Chinese Communist Party publishes revised regulations for local committees
articles.title: Xi’s new rulebook for local Party leaders
articles.summary: The Chinese Communist Party published revised regulations on Monday detailing governance rules for local committees across provincial, city, and county levels. The updated text removes references to Marxism-Leninism and Mao Zedong Thought, replacing them with Xi Jinping Thought as the primary guide. It also expands the political remits and oversight powers held by higher-level committees over local staff.
articles.description: The Communist Party has published rules that centralise control over every provincial, city and county committee with four shifts from the 2015 version: a sharper focus on Xi Jinping Thought, a wider remit for local committees, tighter control over personnel and a new emphasis on discipline

articles.headline: U.S., China and Russia pledge to increase global petrol supplies
articles.title: Trump, Putin, Xi pledge to increase global petrol supplies – but how?
articles.summary: Leaders from the United States, China, and Russia pledged to boost refined petroleum production following a trilateral summit in Shenzhen on Thursday. Analysts expressed skepticism regarding the feasibility of this commitment, citing limited U.S. refining capacity, Russian infrastructure damage from Ukrainian drone strikes, and disruptions to Chinese crude imports caused by the ongoing conflict in Iran.
articles.description: Analysts are sceptical about how this will be achieved amid the ongoing wars in Ukraine and Iran.

articles.headline: Myanmar and China reject ICJ ruling on Rohingya genocide
articles.title: Myanmar, China object to landmark ICJ ruling on Rohingya genocide
articles.summary: Myanmar’s government has dismissed an International Court of Justice ruling that its military committed genocide against the Rohingya minority, labeling the verdict unfair. China also criticized the decision, arguing it hinders dispute resolution. The court found that Myanmar’s security forces carried out mass killings and sexual violence during a 2017 crackdown that displaced 700,000 people.
articles.description: A Myanmar government spokesperson said the ruling was unjust and noted that the court's decision was not unanimous.

articles.headline: Brexit debate returns as UK PM seeks closer EU ties
articles.title: Brexit debate returns as UK PM seeks closer EU ties
articles.description: Brexit debate returns as UK PM seeks closer EU ties

articles.headline: ICJ rules Myanmar committed genocide against Rohingya population
articles.title: What does the ICJ’s Rohingya genocide ruling mean for Gaza?
articles.summary: The International Court of Justice in The Hague has delivered a historic verdict ruling that Myanmar committed genocide against its minority Rohingya population. United Nations judges found that security forces carried out widespread atrocities, including killings and sexual violence. Legal experts note the landmark ruling could potentially influence South Africa's ongoing genocide case against Israel at the court regarding the conflict in Gaza.
articles.description: The case sets a precedent for establishing a state's intent to commit genocide beyond explicitly written orders.

articles.headline: Anthropic raises 81.3 billion dollars in record initial public offering
articles.title: Anthropic raises $81.3bn in biggest IPO of all time
articles.summary: Artificial intelligence giant Anthropic has raised 81.3 billion dollars in the largest initial public offering in history by selling 980 million shares at 83 dollars each on Wednesday. The New York Nasdaq stock exchange debut surpassed SpaceX's previous 75 billion dollar record, giving the artificial intelligence company a market valuation of approximately 1.5 trillion dollars ahead of its trading launch.
articles.description: AI giant prices shares at $83 in blockbuster market debut.

articles.headline: US military tightens naval blockade on Iranian cargo transfers
articles.title: US targets Iran’s ship-to-ship transfers: Can Tehran break the blockade?
articles.summary: The United States military announced that vessels receiving Iranian cargo through ship-to-ship transfers will face potential military action and enforcement measures. United States Central Command stated the advisory aims to close loopholes allowing petroleum exports to bypass existing blockades. Analysts warn the escalation could provoke Iranian retaliation against regional energy infrastructure and increase wider geopolitical tensions in the Middle East.
articles.description: CENTCOM declares vessels bypassing the Iran blockade could be stopped, boarded or even seized by US forces.

articles.headline: Supreme Court dismisses Tamil Nadu plea over Cauvery water release
articles.title: Cauvery dispute: SC dismisses Tamil Nadu plea on Karnataka not making good shortfall in water share
articles.summary: The Supreme Court on November 20, 2026, dismissed an application from Tamil Nadu claiming a shortfall of 11.719 thousand million cubic feet in Cauvery water flows from Billigundulu. A Bench led by Justice Vikram Nath delivered the judgment after Karnataka opposed the request, arguing that the Cauvery Water Management Authority had not ordered the release.
articles.description: The judgment is based on applications filed by T.N., alleging that Karnataka had failed to implement the binding judgment of the SC to ensure water to to TN at Billigundulu on a pro-rata basis during distress years like the current one

articles.headline: ‘We didn’t come here to beg’: Africa’s message at COP31
articles.title: ‘We didn’t come here to beg’: Africa’s message at COP31
articles.description: Ghana has demanded climate justice and funding for African nations, warning COP31 leaders against empty promises.

articles.headline: European Union and United Kingdom reach post-Brexit policy agreements
articles.title: ‘The deal is done’: EU, UK agree to reset relations 10 years after Brexit
articles.summary: The European Union and the United Kingdom sealed agreements covering youth mobility, sanitary regulations, and emissions trading systems following a Brussels summit. British Prime Minister Andy Burnham stated the deals will benefit both economies, though domestic critics condemned the arrangements. Implementation will require legal processes in each country as both sides pursue a broader reset in relations.
articles.description: Deals on food and animal goods, mobility and student fees have been agreed, but months of negotiations lay ahead.

articles.headline: Indonesian wildfires cause economic losses exceeding thirty billion dollars
articles.title: Economic losses from Indonesia fires could reach $30 billion, research shows
articles.summary: Severe wildfires across Indonesia have destroyed 2.88 million hectares of land this year, generating economic losses and health costs estimated at over thirty billion dollars. According to research from the Center of Economic and Law Studies published on November 20, 2026, asset damages and respiratory illness treatment expenses accounted for the total. Researchers attribute the intensified fire season to climate change, deforestation, and El Nino weather patterns.
articles.description: Wildfires have burned through 7.1 million acres so far in 2026, according to the Nusantara Atlas deforestation monitor, an area 18 times the size of London

articles.headline: International Court of Justice considers historic genocide case against Myanmar over Rohingya
articles.title: Myanmar faces historic genocide verdict at UN court over Rohingya massacres
articles.summary: Judges at the International Court of Justice in The Hague are preparing to deliver a landmark verdict in a genocide case filed by The Gambia against Myanmar. The legal action centers on the military operations in Rakhine State that drove hundreds of thousands of Rohingya into Bangladesh in 2017. Myanmar authorities have rejected the accusations, arguing military actions targeted militants.
articles.description: No state has ever been found guilty by an international court of committing genocide.

articles.headline: US envoy Jared Kushner says Russia is comfortable with NATO-like security pact for Ukraine
articles.title: Kushner says Russia OK with ‘NATO-like’ security pact for Ukraine: Is it?
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump's envoy Jared Kushner stated that Russia is comfortable with post-war security guarantees for Ukraine modeled on NATO Article 5. Speaking in Berlin alongside European leaders, Kushner indicated Trump is open to the package. Meanwhile, Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Sergei Ryabkov rejected any form of quasi-membership for Kyiv, highlighting ongoing tensions over Ukraine's 2022 NATO application.
articles.description: NATO Article 5 says attack on one member is an attack on all. Analysts say inclusion of Ukraine 'stretches credulity'.

articles.headline: Malaysia plans to resettle 10000 Rohingya refugees in Turkiye
articles.title: Malaysia plans to resettle 10,000 Rohingya in Turkiye
articles.summary: Malaysia plans to resettle 10000 Rohingya refugees in Turkiye through a structured skills training programme. Deputy Prime Minister Ahmad Zahid Hamidi announced the Cabinet decision following the International Court of Justice ruling that Myanmar committed genocide against the ethnic minority. The initiative aims to provide vocational training and employment opportunities for refugees, who make up two-thirds of Myanmar asylum seekers in Malaysia.
articles.description: The announcement by Deputy PM Ahmad Zahid Hamidi comes a day after the UN's top court, in a landmark ruling, said that Myanmar committed genocide against the ethnic minority

articles.headline: Prime Minister Modi criticizes corporate India over domestic manufacturing progress
articles.title: Why is PM Modi upset with corporate India? | Explained
articles.summary: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi addressed Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry leaders, criticizing the domestic industry for failing to enhance manufacturing since the 1930s. Speaking on November 19, 2026, the leader highlighted economic concerns that have frequently been raised by the political opposition, lending additional institutional weight to these longstanding structural issues.
articles.description: The Prime Minister pulled up industry leaders on four different issues. Government data and anecdotal evidence shows why he is angry

articles.headline: Rohingya refugees welcome United Nations court ruling on Myanmar genocide
articles.title: Rohingya in Bangladesh welcome UN court’s genocide verdict but say they want to go home to Myanmar
articles.summary: Rohingya refugees in Cox's Bazar camp welcomed the International Court of Justice ruling that Myanmar committed genocide during military operations. The legally binding judgment ordered reparations and safe returns for refugees, though implementation challenges remain. Approximately one million two hundred thousand displaced individuals currently reside in crowded Bangladeshi camps.
articles.description: “The Rohingya have their own distinct culture, their own language, their own land and everything else that defines an ethnic group,” said a Rohingya community leader

articles.headline: Myanmar calls UN court genocide ruling unfair and unjust
articles.title: Myanmar calls ICJ ruling on genocide 'unfair'
articles.summary: Government spokesperson Khaing Khaing Soe stated that the United Nations International Court of Justice ruling was unfair and that Myanmar was unjustly accused. The court found Myanmar responsible for state-sponsored genocide against the Rohingya Muslim minority. Judges highlighted mass executions and sexual violence during clearance operations. The case was initially filed by Gambia seven years prior.
articles.description: The ruling by the ⁠International Court of Justice was the first time the court has held a ​State responsible for ‌genocide

articles.headline: Pakistan climate change minister visits India for SCO forum
articles.title: Pakistan minister visits India for first time since 2025 war
articles.summary: Musadik Malik arrived in New Delhi to attend the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Civilisational Dialogue Forum, marking the first visit by a Pakistani federal minister since a brief war in May 2025. Prime Minister Narendra Modi is set to inaugurate the gathering. Both governments framed the visit as routine multilateral business, with no bilateral meetings currently scheduled between the two nuclear-armed neighbours.
articles.description: Islamabad and New Delhi insist the visit is strictly multilateral, despite hopes it could open a channel for contact.

articles.headline: El Salvador president launches controversial third term re-election campaign
articles.title: El Salvador’s Bukele seeks third term after constitution change
articles.summary: El Salvador President Nayib Bukele officially registered his candidacy for the February elections following constitutional changes by his party Nuevas Ideas that removed term limits. While popular due to a gang crackdown, critics and human rights organizations accused the forty-five-year-old populist of consolidating power, packing courts, and creating a de facto one-party state.
articles.description: Critics accuse populist president of engineering a de facto one-party state in El Salvador.

articles.headline: US President Trump and Russian President Putin to meet in China
articles.title: Trump and Putin to meet one-on-one in China Thursday
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump will hold a one-on-one meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin on Thursday in China, according to a US official. The leaders will also join Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping for a trilateral summit during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum. Meanwhile, American envoys are scheduled to meet Ukrainian officials and European partners in Berlin to discuss security guarantees.
articles.description: US and Russia leaders meet in China amid efforts to resolve Ukraine crisis and enhance post-war security guarantees.

articles.headline: White House fires cyber chief Sean Cairncross amid outages
articles.title: White House fires cybersecurity chief after widespread outages
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump administration dismissed cyber security chief Sean Cairncross following widespread communication and travel outages, a source told Agence France-Presse on November 19, 2026. Defense Department Chief Information Officer Kirsten Davies will fill the role in an acting capacity. State Secretary Marco Rubio congratulated Davies on X, as concerns persist over artificial intelligence threats and credential requirements.
articles.description: Sean Cairncross’ role will be filled in an acting capacity by current Defense Department Chief Information Officer Kirsten Davies

articles.headline: Prime Minister Modi calls for government action against the narcotics trade
articles.title: PM Modi calls for sustained government drive against drug trade, stresses financial prudence
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi urged a sustained government campaign to eliminate the narcotics trade during a review meeting with his Council of Ministers. Following the ASEAN summit, the Prime Minister also emphasized financial prudence among citizens and cited World Bank findings showing five hundred million people lifted out of poverty.
articles.description: At a review meeting with his Council of Ministers, the Prime Minister also assessed progress in poverty reduction and the elimination of left-wing extremism

articles.headline: UK and EU expected to agree on youth mobility scheme
articles.title: UK and EU to agree youth mobility scheme, BBC understands
articles.summary: Up to one hundred thousand young people from the European Union and the United Kingdom could gain the ability to travel, work, and study in each other's territories annually under an upcoming agreement negotiated ahead of a Brussels summit. According to the BBC, discussions are continuing regarding caps and fees while officials aim to finalize broader packages covering food trade rules and immigration enforcement.
articles.description: The scheme is expected to be approved at Friday's UK-EU summit, with new deals on food trade and carbon emissions also on the table.

articles.headline: British and European Union leaders to meet for summit
articles.title: EU and Britain to agree steps towards relations reset
articles.summary: British and European Union leaders are scheduled to meet in Brussels to discuss steps toward resetting relations a decade after the Brexit vote. UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham will meet European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen and European Council head Antonio Costa to seal potential deals on food exchange, emissions trading, and youth mobility.
articles.description: A decade after Brexit, London is signalling a willingness to align more closely with the EU on various policies.

articles.headline: Russian missile and drone strikes damage two bridges in Kyiv
articles.title: Russian strikes damage two bridges in Kyiv: Mayor
articles.summary: Russian attacks damaged the Podilsko-Voskresensky and Darnytsky bridges in Kyiv on November 20, 2026, according to Mayor Vitali Klitschko, as Moscow launched a fresh wave of missiles and drones. The strikes also set buildings ablaze in the Obolon and Podil districts, while a separate drone attack in Kharkiv damaged a hospital and injured four people, municipal officials reported.
articles.description: Russian president Vladimir Putin vowed "much more painful" retaliatory attacks after Ukraine this week damaged the Crimea bridge, a symbol of Putin's rule over the annexed region

articles.headline: Supreme Court declines separate hearing for split verdict recall plea
