articles.title: Supreme Court declines plea for separate hearing on recall of split verdict in ECs’ appointment case
articles.summary: The Supreme Court on November 20, 2026, declined to separately list a recall application regarding a split verdict on whether challenges to the 2023 Chief Election Commissioner appointment law should go to a larger bench. Chief Justice of India Surya Kant stated the five-hearing Constitution Bench can evaluate the recall plea, despite the impending retirement of Justice Satish Chandra Sharma.
articles.description: The CJI also said the five-judge Bench could consider the recall application even after the retirement of one of the judges who delivered the split verdict

articles.headline: Trump bows to pressure, replaces US cyber security director
articles.title: Trump bows to pressure, replaces US cyber security director
articles.description: President Trump has removed National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross and named a Defense Department official as interim.

articles.headline: Rohingya refugees react with relief to ICJ genocide ruling
articles.title: Tears of joy, prayers for return home: Rohingya react to genocide ruling
articles.summary: Rohingya refugees in Cox's Bazar expressed relief and hope on November 20, 2026, after the International Court of Justice found Myanmar responsible for genocide during 2017 military operations. Brought by The Gambia, the landmark ruling acknowledged the killing of more than 10,000 people, prompting renewed aspirations among displaced communities for safe repatriation and global justice.
articles.description: For refugees, the ICJ ruling that Myanmar committed genocide is a vindication. But will they be able to return home?

articles.headline: India and the Netherlands upgrade bilateral ties to strategic partnership
articles.title: India, Netherlands upgrade ties; sign 17 MoUs on water, renewable energy, and semiconductors
articles.summary: During Prime Minister Narendra Modi's visit on May 16 and 17, 2026, India and the Netherlands elevated their relations to a Strategic Partnership. Both nations signed 17 agreements covering water, agriculture, health, renewable energy, and critical minerals. According to Dutch media, Prime Minister Rob Jetten also raised sensitive topics including press freedoms, which the Ministry of External Affairs rejected.
articles.description: MEA pushes back on Dutch concerns over press freedom and minority rights in India. PM Jetten raises child abduction case with PM Modi. Agreements signed include a semiconductor fabrication project between TATA Electronics and Dutch company ASML

articles.headline: Gaza Civil Defence struggles with broken vehicles and severe shortages
articles.title: Gaza Civil Defence struggles to rescue lives as vehicles break down
articles.summary: Emergency rescue operations in Gaza City are severely hampered as over 85 percent of Civil Defence vehicles are out of operation due to damage and restrictions on spare parts. Field officer Abdullah al-Majdalawi stated that crews must carry equipment on foot. The United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs warned that prolonged shortages severely impact humanitarian work across the territory.
articles.description: More than 85 percent of Gaza Civil Defence vehicles are out of service as crews struggle to reach trapped people.

articles.headline: U.S. Commerce Department issues interim rule restricting advanced AI chip exports
articles.title: How U.S. controls flow of advanced tech, chip, and compute to China | Explained
articles.summary: The U.S. Commerce Department issued an interim final rule on November 16, 2026, barring foreign data centers with American AI chips from providing cloud services to businesses in twenty-four countries, including China, Iran, and Russia. China criticized the move as an overreach of national security, while the policy builds on export controls established in 2018.
articles.description: The U.S. Commerce Department, on November 16, 2026, issued an interim final rule barring data centre operators outside of the U.S., equipped with advanced American AI chips, from providing cloud service to businesses in two dozen countries, including China, Iran and Russia

articles.headline: Iran launches new attacks on Gulf neighbours following US strike
articles.title: Kuwait, Bahrain face new Iran attacks after US strike on Qeshm Island
articles.summary: Iran launched new attacks targeting a United States military airbase in Kuwait and carrying out several strikes in Bahrain. The actions followed a US bombing on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, which occurred after an Iranian assault on a US radar installation. Regional officials and the Gulf Cooperation Council condemned the escalation, warning it threatens security and complicates diplomatic efforts.
articles.description: Iranian attacks on the Gulf countries draw condemnation from across the region.

articles.headline: Kushner: Trump open to NATO-like security guarantees for Ukraine
articles.title: Kushner: Trump open to NATO-like security guarantees for Ukraine
articles.description: US President Donald Trump is open to offering NATO-like security guarantees to Ukraine, envoy Jared Kushner has said.

articles.headline: Crowds gather as Trump arrives in China ahead of talks with Xi and Putin
articles.title: Crowds gather as Trump arrives in China ahead of talks with Xi and Putin
articles.description: Crowds gathered in Shenzhen, China, to welcome US President Donald Trump as he arrived for the APEC summit

articles.headline: India and Japan agree to allow live-fire military training
articles.title: In a first, Japanese forces will use Indian facilities for live-fire training
articles.summary: During a two-plus-two dialogue held in Tokyo on November 19, 2026, Indian and Japanese defense and foreign ministers signed an agreement allowing Japan's Self-Defence Forces to utilize Indian test ranges for surface-to-ship missile live-fire training. The ministers, including External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar, also advanced discussions concerning naval radar systems, joint shipbuilding, and broader regional security cooperation in the Indo-Pacific.
articles.description: Foreign and Defence Ministers of the two countries hold talks in Tokyo; both sides announce deepening security and defence cooperation in joint statement, indicate forward movement in India receiving the UNICORN naval radar system from Japan

articles.headline: Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin meet in China ahead of summit
articles.title: Trump shakes hands with Putin and Xi ahead of historic talks in China
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump met Russian President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen on Wednesday before a historic Asia-Pacific summit in China. The leaders are expected to hold talks on Thursday regarding global conflicts including Ukraine and Iran, alongside Chinese President Xi Jinping. The meeting marks the first in-person encounter between Trump and Putin since August 2025.
articles.description: The three leaders will meet together for the first time on Thursday during a closely-watched summit.

articles.headline: Interfaith marriage priest murdered across border in Kolhapur
articles.title: Shadows over Shahu’s Land: The cost of loving and living across caste
articles.summary: Mandar Ajit Ranade, a thirty-five-year-old priest and astrologer, was killed on October 31 in Mankapur near the Maharashtra-Karnataka border after being lured to a secluded spot. Karnataka police arrested thirty-five-year-old Babaso alias Deepak Magadum, who allegedly plotted the murder to avenge his daughter marrying a man from a nomadic tribe earlier in January 2026 across caste and religious lines.
articles.description: More than a century after Chhatrapati Shahu Maharaj, the ruler of Kolhapur, legalized inter-caste unions, the murder of a priest, symbolic funerals, and forced disinheritance reveal how caste prejudice is tightening its grip on western Maharashtra, even as safe houses and reformists keep hope alive, writes Radheshyam Jadhav

articles.headline: Climate summit enters final day as nations seek fossil fuel cuts
articles.title: COP 31: Nations still seeking deeper fossil fuel cuts as climate summit enters final day
articles.summary: Delegates attending United Nations climate talks in Turkiye on November 20, 2026, sought meaningful commitments to curb fossil fuel emissions before the annual summit concluded. According to a Climate Action Tracker report, global warming progress has stalled, meaning the 2015 Paris Agreement goal of limiting temperature rises to 1.5 degrees Celsius will likely be surpassed by the end of the century.
articles.description: The two-week annual summit, which has so far largely failed to advance any big ideas to move away from fossil fuels — mainly coal, oil and gas — which are contributing to more intense and deadly heat waves, droughts, floods and other disasters, ends on Nov. 20

articles.headline: Asian stock markets drop amid ongoing fears of an AI bubble
articles.title: Asia’s stock markets dive as Anthropic debut fails to allay AI bubble fears
articles.summary: Asian stock markets opened with steep losses on Friday despite Anthropic completing a historic public offering on the Nasdaq stock exchange in New York. Benchmarks in Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, and Hong Kong tumbled as investors remained concerned about the sustainability of multi-trillion-dollar investments in the artificial intelligence sector, following similar sell-offs on Wall Street.
articles.description: Indexes in Japan, South Korea, Taiwan and Hong Kong fall amid tech sell-off.

articles.headline: Kimi Antonelli becomes the youngest Formula One champion in history
articles.title: Kimi Antonelli - A new face for a new era
articles.summary: Italian driver Kimi Antonelli secured the Formula One world championship after finishing third at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez in Mexico City. At twenty years and sixty-eight days old, he surpassed Sebastian Vettel's previous age record. This victory made him the first Italian to claim the title since Alberto Ascari in 1953, watched live across Italy.
articles.description: Mercedes team boss punted on the Italian and backed him through a bruising rookie year, a barrage of doubts and a few departing sponsors. But he never once wavered in his belief. The youngest champion in F1 history has repaid that faith, and silenced the critics along the way

articles.headline: Trump nominee refuses to call Jan 6 an ‘attack’ at Senate hearing
articles.title: Trump nominee refuses to call Jan 6 an ‘attack’ at Senate hearing
articles.description: Trump’s nominee to lead the US agency responsible for election security, refused to call the insurrection an attack.

articles.headline: California Attorney General subpoenas Nvidia over former CEO affair
articles.title: California Attorney General subpoenas Nvidia over chips, former CEO’s affair
articles.summary: California Attorney General Rob Bonta issued an investigative subpoena to Nvidia on November 19, 2026, regarding former chief executive officer Jensen Huang's affair with a suspected Chinese spy. State authorities are investigating whether advanced chips reached China or if investors were misled. Huang and general counsel Tim Teter agreed to congressional interviews scheduled for December 1 and December 2.
articles.description: The California Department of Justice said it is asking Nvidia whether its advanced chips or confidential information may have gone to China and whether Nvidia misled investors and the public

articles.headline: Iran army targets United States base in Kuwait with drones
articles.title: Iran strikes U.S. air base in Kuwait, targets Bahrain amid wider Gulf attacks
articles.summary: The Iranian military stated on November 18, 2026, that it launched drone strikes against the United States Ali Al Salem air base in Kuwait, activating regional air defences. Kuwaiti authorities confirmed their military intercepted incoming aerial threats and the foreign ministry strongly condemned the assault. This development follows previous strikes and ongoing Middle East tensions.
articles.description: Iran said its recent attacks — including those on other U.S. facilities in Bahrain on November 15 and November 13 — were in response to U.S. drone surveillance operations and an attack on Iranian communications towers

articles.headline: Meta reconsiders 2030 climate goals due to artificial intelligence
articles.title: Meta rethinks 2030 climate goals as AI data centres drive emissions up
articles.summary: Meta executives Rachel Peterson and Blair Swedeen stated in a November report that the company is re-evaluating its 2030 net-zero emissions deadline because artificial intelligence data centres are driving energy consumption up. Meta reported a 45 percent increase in net carbon-equivalent emissions to 11.8 million tonnes in 2025. This shift follows broader corporate environmental retreats under United States President Donald Trump.
articles.description: Rising data centre energy needs force Meta to review sustainability targets amid growing corporate climate retreat.

articles.headline: Union Home Minister Amit Shah outlines security updates in New Delhi
articles.title: Emerging radicalisation hotspots now under purview of Multi-Agency Centre: Amit Shah
articles.summary: Union Home Minister Amit Shah announced that the Multi-Agency Centre now tracks cybersecurity, narcotics, organised crime, and radicalisation hotspots. Speaking in New Delhi at a counter-terrorism conference organised by the National Investigation Agency, he highlighted regional security grids and counter-terrorism measures. Senior officials including Intelligence Bureau Director Mahesh Dixit attended the inaugural session.
articles.description: Union Home Minister calls on anti-terrorism squads of every State to strengthen their cyber-expert units

articles.headline: Kuwait and Bahrain repel overnight Iranian drone attacks amid rising regional hostilities
articles.title: Kuwait says it repelled first Iranian attack in two months after US strikes island
articles.summary: Kuwait and Bahrain reported intercepting Iranian air attacks overnight, marking a new escalation in ongoing regional hostilities. The drone strike in Kuwait targeted an airbase hosting American forces without causing damage, following United States strikes on an Iranian missile site. Meanwhile, an oil tanker was attacked in the Strait of Oman, leaving one crew member missing and raising widespread fears of a broader conflict.
articles.description: Bahrain says it was also attacked by Iran following a US air strike on the Iranian island of Qeshm in the Gulf on Tuesday.

articles.headline: Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele registers candidacy for third consecutive term
articles.title: El Salvador’s Bukele expected to formalise bid for third presidential term
articles.summary: Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele registered his candidacy for the upcoming presidential election scheduled for February 28, 2027, following a constitutional amendment that allows him to seek a third consecutive term. The founder of the Nuevas Ideas party faces challengers including Maytee Iraheta and Rafael Aguirre, while human rights groups have raised concerns regarding his administration's ongoing state of emergency.
articles.description: The Salvadoran president has won popularity through a crime crackdown that has granted the state enormous power.

articles.headline: Daily pill daraxonrasib shrinks and eliminates tumours in cancer trials
articles.title: Massive hope for pancreatic cancer pill after trial saw tumours vanish
articles.summary: Medical experts report that a daily medication called daraxonrasib combined with chemotherapy successfully halted tumour growth in nearly ninety percent of advanced pancreatic cancer patients during early trials. According to Cancer Research UK, tumours became completely undetectable in one in twelve participants. Researchers emphasize that longer studies are required to determine whether the treatment can achieve lasting remission and extend overall survival.
articles.description: Daily pill daraxonrasib appears to shrink and possibly even eliminate tumours in some patients with one of the deadliest cancers.

articles.headline: How did Anthropic's stock market debut unfold?
articles.title: How did Anthropic's stock market debut unfold?
articles.description: The BBC's Samira Hussain breaks down the AI company's first day as a publicly traded company, as shares closed up 17%.

articles.headline: Trump arrives in China ahead of trilateral summit with Xi, Putin
articles.title: Trump arrives in China ahead of trilateral summit with Xi, Putin
articles.description: US President Donald Trump was greeted by Chinese President Xi Jinping as he arrived in China.

articles.headline: California attorney general investigates Nvidia over potential China chip transfers
articles.title: California targets Nvidia in China AI chip probe
articles.summary: California Attorney General Rob Bonta has served an investigative subpoena on artificial intelligence chip designer Nvidia to probe whether the company or former Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang misled investors regarding advanced chips or confidential information reaching China. The inquiry follows Huang's recent departure after disclosures of an extramarital relationship with an executive at Megaspeed, a major customer based in Singapore.
articles.description: The probe by California, where the AI chipmaker has its global headquarters, follows former CEO Jensen Huang's departure.

articles.headline: Mosque torched in Israel sparks political backlash against Netanyahu
articles.title: Mosque torched in Israel sparks political backlash against Netanyahu
articles.description: A mosque in al-Dahi, a Palestinian Arab village in northern Israel, was set on fire in a suspected arson attack.

articles.headline: United States approved exports of nearly 900,000 artificial intelligence chips to China
articles.title: US signed off on sales of nearly 900,000 AI chips to China in six months
articles.summary: The United States Department of Commerce approved export licenses for nearly 900,000 advanced artificial intelligence chips to Chinese companies between December 2025 and May 2026, according to the House Foreign Affairs Committee. The approvals included products from Nvidia and Advanced Micro Devices destined for firms such as Alibaba and Tencent, drawing renewed scrutiny from lawmakers.
articles.description: US House committee releases chip export data amid scrutiny of former Nvidia CEO's alleged links to a Chinese spy.

articles.headline: Wall Street closes sharply lower as Anthropic initial public offering fails to lift sentiment
articles.title: Wall Street ends sharply lower as Anthropic’s debut fails to revive AI fervour
articles.summary: United States stock indexes declined significantly on Thursday as Anthropic's high-profile market debut failed to revive enthusiasm for artificial intelligence. The benchmark S&P 500 fell 2.03 percent to 7,175.24 points, logging its fifth consecutive session of losses. Meanwhile, investors adjusted expectations for upcoming monetary policy decisions following the release of Federal Reserve meeting minutes.
articles.description: All three major U.S. stock indexes ended the session ⁠sharply lower, with the benchmark S&P 500 logging its fifth straight session of losses

articles.headline: Appeals court permits United States administration to end deportation protections for Venezuelans
articles.title: US appeals court lets Trump end TPS deportation protections for Venezuelans
articles.summary: A United States appeals court issued a ruling on Wednesday allowing the administration of President Donald Trump to proceed with removing deportation protections for approximately 600,000 Venezuelans. The decision overrides a previous order from a lower-court judge that had blocked the expiration of Temporary Protected Status. Legal challenges against the policy remain ongoing in the court system.
articles.description: The appeals court's ruling prevents a lower-court decision from taking effect, which would block Trump from lifting TPS.

articles.headline: Leaders of China, Russia and United States sign joint peace declaration in Shenzhen
articles.title: Will the Shenzhen summit safeguard world peace?
articles.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping hosted Russian leader Vladimir Putin and United States President Donald Trump for a summit in Shenzhen on Thursday. The three heads of state signed a joint Peace Declaration committing to international security, increased petroleum product output, and the prevention of nuclear conflict. The leaders also agreed to maintain communication channels regarding ongoing global conflicts.
articles.description: Xi, Putin and Trump issue 'Peace Declaration' after historic summit.

articles.headline: Gulf nations repel aerial attacks following United States strikes
articles.title: Bahrain, Kuwait attacked after U.S. strikes Iranian island
articles.summary: Bahrain and Kuwait announced on November 18, 2026, the successful interception of air attacks launched in the wake of United States strikes on Iranian territory. The widening conflict involves retaliatory drone and missile operations targeting facilities used by Washington across the region, while diplomats also address separate security allegations and upcoming trilateral summits.

articles.headline: US Senate rejects measure to limit Trump war powers in Iran
articles.title: Senate Republicans in US reject measure to limit Trump’s war powers in Iran
articles.summary: United States lawmakers defeated a resolution demanding an end to military action against Iran or congressional authorization. The measure failed in a 51 to 48 vote on Thursday, mostly along party lines. Democratic Senator Tim Kaine argued the vote reflects public dissatisfaction with the conflict. Three Republicans joined Democrats, while one Democrat opposed the resolution.
articles.description: The resolution was defeated 51-48. Three Republicans broke rank, voting for the measure.

articles.headline: What does the Myanmar genocide ruling mean for the Rohingya?
articles.title: What does the Myanmar genocide ruling mean for the Rohingya?
articles.description: Rohingya refugees in Bangladesh cheered an International Court of Justice finding that Myanmar committed genocide.

articles.headline: COP31 climate negotiators publish revised draft omitting fossil fuels reference
articles.title: Draft of COP31 cover text drops references to fossil fuel phase-out, net zero dates
articles.summary: Climate negotiators at the COP31 summit in Antalya removed references to ending fossil fuel use from a revised draft deal published on Thursday. The updated document also dropped a specific adaptation finance target for developing nations while retaining acknowledgment of global warming thresholds and greenhouse gas emission cuts ahead of the Friday deadline.
articles.description: A major concern raised by developing countries, of phasing out unilateral trade measures such as the CBAM (Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism) by 2027, that was present in the earlier draft has also been eliminated

articles.headline: Save the Children reports record dangers facing children in Gaza
articles.title: Save the Children: Gaza’s children face ‘unmatched dangers’
articles.summary: Save the Children released a report stating that Gaza children face unmatched dangers with at least 20,000 killed over three years of war. The findings coincided with the conclusion of an Israeli military ground operation in central Gaza. Gaza Health Ministry data indicated hundreds of children died waiting for medical permits, while displaced residents highlighted severe shortages of basic necessities during the ongoing conflict.
articles.description: Aid group says one third of violations against children worldwide were in occupied Palestinian territory.

articles.headline: Rohingya survivors react to landmark genocide ruling against Myanmar
articles.title: Rohingya survivors react to landmark genocide ruling against Myanmar
articles.description: Rohingya refugees in Bangladesh and an activist in New York react as the UN's top court rules Myanmar committed genocide

articles.headline: Families flee Gaza’s Bureij camp as Israel launches new offensive
articles.title: Families flee Gaza’s Bureij camp as Israel launches new offensive
articles.description: Families flee Gaza’s Bureij camp as Israel launches new offensive

articles.headline: India administers over one crore HPV vaccine doses to girls
articles.title: Over 1 crore HPV vaccines given to 14-year-old girls in nine months: Health Ministry
articles.summary: India distributed over one million human papillomavirus vaccine doses to 14-year-old girls in under nine months under a campaign launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in February. According to the Health Ministry, six states achieved full coverage, utilising the U-WIN platform for monitoring as part of efforts to prevent cervical cancer.
articles.description: Six States — Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh, Mizoram, Madhya Pradesh, and Bihar — have achieved 100% coverage of their identified target populations, the Ministry said

articles.headline: Scientists predict La Niña conditions could strengthen India's 2027 monsoon season
articles.title: After strong El Niño, La Niña may boost India’s 2027 monsoon, says INCOIS forecast
articles.summary: Researchers at the Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services in Hyderabad reported that the current El Niño weather pattern will likely persist until March. Climate models suggest a subsequent shift toward neutral conditions and a growing probability of La Niña emerging to potentially enhance rainfall during the Southwest Monsoon in 2027.
articles.description: Scientists indicate that the ongoing strong El Niño could persist until March 2027, followed by neutral conditions and a possible transition to La Niña during the Southwest Monsoon. They are also monitoring widespread marine heatwaves across the Indian Ocean

articles.headline: Palestinians in Gaza face new displacement after Israeli military operation
articles.title: Palestinians in Gaza face new displacement after Israeli army operation
articles.summary: Thousands of Palestinian civilians fled makeshift shelters in central Gaza after the Israeli military launched a ground operation targeting a suspected tunnel. The offensive, which ended a period of relative stability following an October 2025 ceasefire, forced families out without humanitarian assistance. According to Gaza authorities, thousands escaped as gunfire and shelling affected camps.
articles.description: Families in Nuseirat spend the night without shelter, while many fear returning despite Israel ending offensive.

articles.headline: Congress criticizes government over delimitation bill and parliamentary majority
articles.title: PM, HM still searching for ‘supertainted’ two-thirds majority for delimitation bill, says Congress
articles.summary: The Congress party stated that Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah remain focused on securing a two-thirds majority in the Lok Sabha for a delimitation bill. Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh argued that current parliamentary configurations and reservations for women should remain frozen until achieving the Viksit Bharat objective.
articles.description: Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh said it is in the nation's interest to let the current Lok Sabha strength and state-wise configuration continue with one-third reservation for women implemented till the Viksit Bharat objective is achieved

articles.headline: K.L. Rahul and Devdutt Padikkal lead India to 239/1 at lunch
articles.title: IND vs NZ, 1st Test: India end Day 3 on 486/4, lead by 118
articles.summary: K.L. Rahul and Devdutt Padikkal advanced India's first-innings score to 239 for one at lunch on the third day of the first Test against New Zealand at Basin Reserve, trailing by 129 runs. Rahul reached 93 not out while Padikkal contributed an unbeaten 53, adding 80 runs during the morning session under clear skies and a breeze, leaving Rahul seven runs shy of his 13th Test hundred.
articles.description: India amassed 327 runs in 86 overs to finish the third day at 486/4. That gave it a lead of 118 runs, with two days remaining

articles.headline: Severe cyclonic storm Akvan triggers red alerts in Andhra Pradesh
articles.title: Akvan may spare most of Andhra Pradesh; red alert issued for Srikakulam, Vizianagaram
articles.summary: The India Meteorological Department issued red alerts for the Srikakulam and Vizianagaram districts in Andhra Pradesh as severe cyclonic storm Akvan approaches. While sparing most of the state, the system is expected to bring heavy rainfall and gales reaching up to 100 kmph before making landfall near Gopalpur in Odisha by Friday noon.
articles.description: Parvathipuram-Manyam, Visakhapatnam, Alluri Sitharama Raju and Anakapalli districts may record isolated very heavy rainfall till Friday evening, says IMD

articles.headline: Pune startup QuPrayog develops laboratory-scale atomic clock prototype
articles.title: Pune startup develops atomic clock prototype amid growing export curbs on critical technologies
articles.summary: Pune-based startup QuPrayog Private Limited built a Rubidium-87 atomic clock prototype using Coherent Population Trapping technology within seven months. Chief executive officer Jay Mangaonkar stated the project aims to reduce reliance on imported timing systems amid export controls, supporting India's National Quantum Mission and indigenous capabilities.
articles.description: Atomic clocks are critical to satellite navigation, telecommunications, space missions and strategic systems, where highly precise and stable timekeeping is essential.

articles.headline: Montek Singh Ahluwalia says States must drive next economic reforms phase
articles.title: States must drive next phase of reforms, says Montek Singh Ahluwalia
articles.summary: Former Planning Commission deputy chairman Montek Singh Ahluwalia stated on Friday at a conference in Hyderabad that India's next economic reforms must rely on State-level policies. Speaking at the Public Policy 2026 event, he emphasized that advanced States like Gujarat and Maharashtra must grow faster to help achieve Viksit Bharat by 2047, while addressing land acquisition and urban infrastructure.

articles.headline: Google updates Gemini on macOS with new computer use features
articles.title: Gemini on Mac can now use your computer
articles.summary: Google introduced a new computer use feature for its Gemini app on macOS, allowing the artificial intelligence tool to assist users with multi-step workflows across local files, desktop applications, and the web. The English-language feature is currently rolling out in the United States ahead of upcoming Apple security restrictions regarding full disk access.
articles.description: Google's Gemini app for macOS now has computer use, meaning it can help you "get multi-step tasks done across your local files, desktop apps, and the web," the company says. Google suggests the feature might be useful for things like speeding up workflows, filling in forms, making presentations, and listing items for sale. Users will […]

articles.headline: Kiren Rijiju questions Congress over past governance following Rahul Gandhi jibe
articles.title: Kiren Rijiju hits back at Rahul Gandhi’s 'compromised PM' jibe, questions Congress on 1962 war, poverty
articles.summary: Union Minister Kiren Rijiju criticized Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Saturday regarding his compromised prime minister remark directed at Narendra Modi. Rijiju challenged the opposition party on social media to apologize for the 1962 Chinese war humiliation and explain India's historical poverty. This exchange followed Gandhi's comments on a trilateral meeting at the APEC summit in China.
articles.description: The Congress leader's remarks triggered a war of words between the BJP and the opposition party, with several BJP leaders accusing Rahul Gandhi of being "clueless" about global geopolitics

articles.headline: UK-EU deal proceeds independently of tuition fees agreement, Ed Miliband says
articles.title: Deal with EU not dependent on tuition fees agreement, Miliband says
articles.summary: British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband confirmed to the BBC on Sunday that the recently agreed cooperation pact with the European Union will take effect in 2028 regardless of a separate tuition fees agreement. The Brussels deal includes reduced checks on British food exports and a youth mobility scheme, though opposition leaders criticized the terms and economic projections.
articles.description: Brussels sources had previously suggested the bloc might not apply the wider deal until fees were lowered for EU students in Britain.

articles.headline: Justice B.V. Nagarathna delivers inaugural Cornelia Sorabji Memorial Lecture at Oxford
articles.title: Full text of the inaugural Cornelia Sorabji Memorial Lecture delivered by Supreme Court Justice B.V. Nagarathna
articles.summary: Supreme Court Justice B.V. Nagarathna stated on Wednesday that women occupying high public offices does not prove societal equality has been achieved. Delivering the inaugural Cornelia Sorabji Memorial Lecture at Somerville College, she traced the historical evolution of women's legal status in India from feudal protection to constitutional rights and professional inclusion.
articles.description: Only the practice of substantive equality could take care of these differences among women hailing from and living through diverse life experiences, the Judge said.

articles.headline: Teenager develops severe kidney ailment after using online fairness cream
articles.title: Keralam girl develops kidney ailment after ‘using’ fairness cream promoted on social media
articles.summary: A 17-year-old girl in Keralam developed membranous nephropathy after using a fairness cream ordered online through Instagram promotion, doctors at Aster MIMS Mother Hospital stated on November 21, 2026. Nephrologist Gowri S reported dangerously high mercury levels in the patient's blood and the product. The family plans to initiate legal proceedings against the company in the consumer court.
articles.description: Nephrologist, who is treating the girl, said medical examinations detected dangerously high mercury levels in the 17-year-old’s body. Tests on the cream allegedly found mercury levels of 12,500 parts per million, far exceeding permissible limit of less than 1 ppm, the doctor said

articles.headline: Israeli opposition alliance faces internal strain amid caretaker Prime Minister Netanyahu moves
articles.title: Can Israel’s opposition bloc stay united against Netanyahu?
articles.summary: Israel's opposition change bloc faces internal divisions as caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu attempts to fracture the alliance ahead of the December 6 government formation deadline. Former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett held a security meeting with Netanyahu, sparking criticism within the 48-seat opposition coalition led by Gadi Eisenkot, which struggles with deep ideological differences.
articles.description: Eisenkot's fragile alliance must overcome deep ideological divisions to turn its opposition into a government.

articles.headline: Israel military completes central Gaza ground operation following ceasefire
articles.title: Israel army says it completed ground operation in central Gaza
articles.summary: The Israeli military concluded a tank-supported ground operation in central Gaza that targeted a tunnel west of the Yellow Line. The Coordinator of Government Activities in the Territories announced the reopening of Salah al-Din Street. While the military stated the action responded to ceasefire violations, Hamas condemned the incursion as a blatant violation.
articles.description: Hamas denounced a "blatant ceasefire violation," while the military said the rare ground incursion was a response to Hamas ceasefire violations in the area

articles.headline: Mirra Andreeva wins WTA Finals to cap breakthrough tennis season
articles.title: Perfect week caps Mirra Andreeva’s star-making year
articles.summary: Nineteen-year-old tennis player Mirra Andreeva won the season-ending Women's Tennis Association Finals in Indian Wells, California, without dropping a single set. She became the youngest champion at the tournament since Maria Sharapova in 2004. Andreeva achieved the victory following a successful year that included a Roland-Garros triumph and a milestone fifty match wins, motivated by a desire to defeat top-ten opponents.
articles.description: The 19-year-old demolished the field at the WTA Finals in Indian Wells. The dominant performance against the world’s best, ending a season in which she won her first Major title, suggests she is growing into a player who can ⁠shape the future of women’s tennis

articles.headline: Cricket Australia backs Pat Cummins to remain Test captain amid scandal fallout
articles.title: Pat Cummins wins Cricket Australia's ‘unanimous support’ to remain Test captain
articles.summary: Cricket Australia endorsed Pat Cummins as Test captain on November 21, 2026, dismissing integrity concerns following renewed fallout from the 2018 Sandpapergate scandal. Chairman David Boon stated the board rejects any implication against Cummins. The decision follows claims by Usman Khawaja and Cameron Bancroft that the entire team knew of the ball-tampering plot in South Africa. Pacer Josh Hazlewood threatened to quit if Cummins was removed.
articles.description: Cummins has been under huge pressure since Usman Khawaja claimed the whole team knew about the plot to alter the ball in a Test at Cape Town in 2018

articles.headline: Ukraine aerial attack on Kerch Bridge halts rail traffic
articles.title: Third Ukrainian strike in 4 days halts rail traffic on Russia's Kerch Bridge to Crimea
articles.summary: A third Ukrainian aerial attack in four days on the Kerch Bridge temporarily halted rail traffic on Thursday, November 19, 2026, according to officials, following earlier strikes that damaged the road section. The strike coincided with talks in Berlin involving U.S. and European leaders, while separate Russian drone strikes across Ukraine killed two people and injured twenty-three others.
articles.description: The attack came hours before the start of talks in Berlin between U.S. envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy alongside more than 40 European leaders who are supporting Ukraine's war effort

articles.headline: Funeral held for New York teen shot while walking to school
articles.title: Funeral held for New York teen shot while walking to school
articles.description: Funeral held for New York teen shot while walking to school

articles.headline: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth faces scrutiny after midterm elections
articles.title: ‘Not an acquittal’: After impeachment vote, Hegseth still under microscope
articles.summary: Following Democratic majorities winning the November 3 midterm elections, U.S. Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth faces mounting calls for his removal after a lame-duck House blocked an impeachment push on November 10, 2026. Critics and analysts debate his accountability for controversial military campaigns, including the war on Iran, while he maintains his position.
articles.description: A week after a fizzled impeachment bid, analysts say Hegseth continues to face backlash for his leadership at Pentagon.

articles.headline: Skyscraper in Riyadh damaged amid renewed Houthi missile attacks
articles.title: Riyadh's tallest building damaged as Saudi reports new Houthi attacks
articles.summary: A skyscraper housing the sovereign wealth fund headquarters in Riyadh was damaged on Thursday, November 19, 2026, after the Saudi-led coalition addressed a missile threat from Yemen's Houthis. Witnesses reported shattered facades on several floors of the Public Investment Fund Tower, amid escalating cross-border attacks that have displaced hundreds of thousands.
articles.description: The Iran-backed Houthis have stepped up their attacks against Saudi Arabia in recent weeks, striking targets including airports, energy infrastructure, military sites and Riyadh's financial district

articles.headline: IRDAI imposes two crore penalty on Star Health
articles.title: IRDAI imposes ₹2 cr penalty on Star Health
articles.summary: The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India levied a two crore penalty on Star Health and Allied Insurance Company following an inspection conducted from January 31 to February 11, 2022. The regulator stated the insurer processed claims inconsistently with policy terms and health insurance regulations regarding Covid claim settlements and arbitrary deductions.
articles.description: The insurer is advised to ensure all policies are serviced as per the terms and conditions of the policy documents and no arbitrary deductions/denial are made to the claim without proper justification, IRDAI said.

articles.headline: Prime Minister Modi urges Indian industry to suggest further economic reforms
articles.title: PM Modi pulls up industry leaders over static wages, employment, manufacturing standards
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi asked corporate leaders during the FICCI Annual General Meeting on November 19, 2026, to suggest reforms without hesitation to drive national growth. Addressing the industry in New Delhi, Modi highlighted that 50 crore people have overcome poverty over the past 12 to 13 years while corporate tax rates were reduced from 30 percent in 2014 to 22 percent.
articles.description: Modi slams India Inc for not passing on tax benefits to people; Congress says Modi ‘nervous and rattled’

articles.headline: Trump and Putin ‘hijacked’ China summit
articles.title: Trump and Putin ‘hijacked’ China summit
articles.description: Trump and Putin’s statements during trilateral talks distracted from the planned agenda, Einar Tangen says.

articles.headline: EPFO approves systematic withdrawal plan for periodic retirement payouts
articles.title: What does EPFO’s Systematic Withdrawal Plan entail for retirees | Explained
articles.summary: The Central Board of Trustees of the Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation approved a systematic withdrawal plan on November 19, 2026, in New Delhi. Retiring members can now choose monthly, quarterly, half-yearly, or annual payouts instead of taking a lump sum. The remaining corpus stays invested to earn interest, while members gain flexible options to enhance savings through voluntary contributions.
articles.description: As per the proposed SWP, upon retirement or superannuation, a member will have several options to receive the accumulated PF corpus or a part through periodic withdrawals instead of a lump-sum withdrawal

articles.headline: Supreme Court asks central government for response on consanguineous marriages
articles.title: Supreme Court asks Centre for response on bringing in law on marriages between those closely related by blood
articles.summary: The Supreme Court asked the central government for its response on the desirability of legislation regarding marriages between individuals closely related by blood. A Bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana noted that while the court cannot regulate such unions, it aims to sensitize the administration on the issue.
articles.description: Counsel for the petitioner highlighted the need to create awareness about the inter-generational consequences of such marriage

articles.headline: Supreme Court quashes Odisha mining land acquisition for lacking Gram Sabha consent
articles.title: Supreme Court upholds tribal land rights, quashes mining-linked acquisition in Odisha
articles.summary: The Supreme Court invalidated land acquisition proceedings for limestone mining by Dalmia Cement Bharat Limited in Odisha’s Sundargarh district. A bench consisting of Justices Dipankar Datta and Satish Chandra Sharma ruled that prior consent from the local Gram Sabha is mandatory under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition Act of 2013.
articles.description: Court says prior Gram Sabha consent was mandatory under the 2013 land acquisition law; sets aside acquisition for Dalmia Cement’s mining project in Sundargarh

articles.headline: Odisha evacuates nearly three lakh people ahead of cyclone Akvan
articles.title: Odisha gears up for cyclone Akvan, shifts 3 lakh people to safety
articles.summary: The Odisha administration relocated approximately 2.98 lakh people as severe cyclonic storm Akvan approached the coast near Gopalpur with winds reaching up to 110 kmph. Special Relief Commissioner Rajesh Pravakar Patil reported that rescue teams from various disaster forces were deployed, while the India Meteorological Department issued heavy rainfall warnings for multiple districts across Odisha and West Bengal.
articles.description: The severe cyclonic storm is likely to cross north Andhra Pradesh and south Odisha coasts close to Gopalpur, by noon of November 20 with the maximum sustained wind speed of 90-100 kmph gusting to 110 kmph, says IMD

articles.headline: Data reveals private sector hospital births reach record high via C-section
articles.title: Study shows most births in private sector hospitals taking place via C-section
articles.summary: Corporate employee health insurance claims analyzed by Plum Data Labs show that the average rate of Caesarean section births in private hospitals reached 69 percent. According to Chief Technology Officer Saurabh Arora, clinical factors and hospital choices drive high rates, while 82 percent of insured families still pay out of pocket because median claims exceed standard policy limits.
articles.description: The four cities with the lowest C-section rates at private hospitals are all in Tamil Nadu: Chennai, Coimbatore, Salem and Vellore

articles.headline: Cyclone Akvan brings heavy rain and inundates low-lying Srikakulam areas
articles.title: Cyclone Akvan: Heavy rain inundates low-lying areas of Ichchapuram, Sompeta in Srikakulam district
articles.summary: Srikakulam district recorded heavy rainfall under the impact of Cyclone Akvan before it crossed the coast. Low-lying areas in Ichchapuram, Kaviti, and Sompeta were inundated, with Ichchapuram receiving 184.6 mm of rain. Collector Swapnil Dinakar noted that the situation remains under control through precautionary measures, while officials coordinate with Odisha regarding rising water levels in local rivers.
articles.description: Ichchapuram records 184.6 mm in 24 hours; the Collector says leave for all officials has been cancelled for relief work

articles.headline: Maharashtra FDA commissioner withdraws high court petition against central regulations
articles.title: Why did Tukaram Mundhe withdraw his petition after dragging the Centre to court? | Explained
articles.summary: Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration Commissioner Tukaram Mundhe withdrew a Bombay High Court petition filed on September 3, 2026. The lawsuit had challenged the constitutional validity of central regulations and the creation of specific posts by the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India, arguing that centralisation encroached upon state enforcement powers regarding food safety.
articles.description: How does the jurisdiction issue between FSSAI and FDA affect businesses and consumers? The history behind the tussle and how Maharashtra had raised concerns earlier too

articles.headline: Prime Minister Andy Burnham heads to Brussels for UK-EU summit
articles.title: As Burnham heads to Brussels, are new Brexit wars about to begin?
articles.summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham travels to Brussels for the second UK-EU Summit on Friday to discuss potential agreements on youth mobility, emissions trading, and food trade. Ten years after the Brexit vote, recent polling indicates that a majority of Britons view leaving the European Union as a mistake and support rejoining the bloc.
articles.description: The UK premier is heading to Brussels for the second round of EU talks aimed at deepening post-Brexit cooperation.

articles.headline: India and Japan discuss economic security during Tokyo talks
articles.title: India, Japan discuss economic security, deeper business, people-to-people ties
articles.summary: Indian External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar met Japanese Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi in Tokyo on November 19, 2026, for the nineteenth India-Japan Foreign Ministers' Strategic Dialogue. The ministers reviewed bilateral cooperation, focusing on economic security and government, business, and people linkages. Mr. Jaishankar also participated in a two-plus-two meeting with Japanese Defence Minister Rajnath Singh and met Liberal Democratic Party Vice-President Taro Aso.
articles.description: Jaishankar flagged the growing “weaponisation” of connectivity, resources, services, supply chains and market shares, saying many of these developments had direct implications for national security

articles.headline: Bihar secures ₹1.72 lakh crore in energy project investments
articles.title: MoUs signed of ₹1.72 lakh crore for six energy projects in Bihar
articles.summary: State officials in Patna signed Memoranda of Understanding for six nuclear and pumped storage energy projects totalling ₹1,72,885 crore on November 20, 2026. Attended by Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary during Bihar Business Connect, the agreements aim to enhance power generation, strengthen energy security, and accelerate industrial growth across Banka, Siwan, Nawada, Jamui, and Aurangabad districts.
articles.description: Nuclear power plants to be established in Banka and Siwan; Four pumped storage projects to be developed in Nawada, Jamui and Aurangabad

articles.headline: French court sentences three police officers for racist assault
articles.title: Three French police officers sentenced over racist assault on Black man
articles.summary: A Paris criminal court sentenced three police officers on November 21, 2020, for assaulting Black music producer Michel Zecler, citing racism as an aggravating factor. Aurelien Lapersonne received five years with three suspended, Philippe Tondeux received five years with three and a half suspended, and Pierre Plantier received five years with four suspended.
articles.description: Paris criminal court finds racism was an aggravating factor in the 2020 assault of Black music producer Michel Zecler.

articles.headline: Somalia expels UAE ambassador and accuses Abu Dhabi of violating sovereignty
articles.title: Somalia expels UAE ambassador, accuses Abu Dhabi of violating sovereignty
articles.summary: Somalia ordered the United Arab Emirates ambassador to depart within seventy-two hours and recalled its own envoy from Abu Dhabi. Information Minister Abdifatah Kasim Mohamud condemned regional port agreements and military base support as an open invasion, following earlier presidential accusations regarding unauthorized political and economic interference in domestic federal affairs.
articles.description: Somalia says the UAE is interfering in its internal affairs with actions that amount to an 'open invasion'.

articles.headline: International Court of Justice rules Myanmar committed Rohingya genocide
articles.title: What the ICJ genocide ruling means for the Rohingya people
articles.summary: The International Court of Justice ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya Muslim minority, marking the first time the court held a state responsible for genocide. Delivered in The Hague by President Yuji Iwasawa, the landmark verdict ordered Myanmar to cease violence, punish perpetrators, and implement reparations within two years.
articles.description: This is the first time the court has ruled that a state committed genocide.

articles.headline: Magnitude 6.9 earthquake strikes central Peru without causing immediate damage
articles.title: Magnitude 6.9 earthquake shakes Peru’s Andes, with no damage or casualties immediately reported
articles.summary: A magnitude 6.9 earthquake struck the Andes in central Peru at 7:09 pm local time on Friday, according to the U.S. Geological Survey. The epicentre was located 34 kilometres north of Junin at a depth of 108 kilometres. Peru's Geophysical Institute reported no immediate damage or casualties, though the tremor was felt in the capital.
articles.description: Peru's Geophysical Institute said no damage or casualties had been reported. The earthquake was felt in the Peruvian capital, prompting residents to rush into the streets

articles.headline: African Union launches new credit rating agency to challenge international assessments
articles.title: Can Africa’s new credit rating agency change how the continent is assessed?
articles.summary: The African Union officially launched the Africa Credit Rating Agency in Port Louis, Mauritius, on October 7. Led by interim chief executive Sifiso Falala, the institution aims to provide independent assessments for African governments and corporate borrowers using local data. The initiative responds to concerns that international rating methodologies inadequately account for the continent's economic structures.
articles.description: The new African agency aims to bring greater transparency to credit ratings.

articles.headline: US and Venezuela re-establish military ties after leadership transition
articles.title: Venezuela signs military deal with US less than a year after Maduro's removal
articles.summary: The United States and Venezuela signed a military cooperation agreement in Caracas less than a year after American forces seized former leader Nicolás Maduro in a raid. Interim President Delcy Rodríguez and US Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth finalized the deal at the presidential palace, marking a strategic shift toward regional security partnership.
articles.description: The US Secretary of Defence says Venezuela has "gone from our most aggressive regional threat to a compliant security partner".

articles.headline: Police investigate mosque arson in northern Israel village
articles.title: Mosque set on fire in Israel, politicians blame Netanyahu’s ‘incitement’
articles.summary: Police are investigating an arson attack on a mosque in al-Dahi after masked individuals reportedly threw an incendiary bottle and scrawled racist graffiti on Thursday. Politicians and community leaders condemned the incident, linking it to political incitement. This attack follows a separate vehicle-ramming incident in Kaf Qasim on Wednesday that left eight people injured.
articles.description: Knesset MPs call the incident 'a hate crime' while Hamas blames Israeli 'settler gangs'.

articles.headline: Crimean Bridge faces repeated attacks by Ukrainian forces
articles.title: Putin vows 'far more painful' response to Ukraine's strikes on Crimean Bridge
articles.summary: The strategically vital Crimean Bridge suffered a third strike in a single week, according to Moscow-installed regional head Sergei Aksyonov, causing temporary traffic suspensions as damage assessments began. The recurring attacks coincide with a landmark summit in China involving Russian President Vladimir Putin, U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping amidst ongoing regional hostilities.
articles.description: The bridge - a symbol of Russia's occupation of the Crimean Peninsula - suffered major damaged following a combined attack by Ukraine earlier this week.

articles.headline: Immigration bail scams continue despite multi-million dollar fines against operators
articles.title: They were fined $811m for conning detained migrants, but the scams didn't stop
articles.summary: Interconnected operations linked to past fraudsters have continued charging detained migrants fees for bond services without securing their release, according to public records and BBC interviews. Former clients described severe detention conditions and prolonged waits after paying companies recommended by lawyers. Federal regulators previously penalised related firms for deceptive practices involving private GPS monitoring requirements.
articles.description: How convicted fraudsters made millions from detained immigrants, evaded efforts to shut down their bail business and left migrants behind bars.

articles.headline: International Court of Justice to deliver verdict in Myanmar Rohingya genocide case
articles.title: Top UN court finds that Myanmar committed genocide against Rohingya: Refugee crisis, timeline of the case, and more
articles.summary: The United Nations court in The Hague will issue a final ruling on November 19, 2026, regarding allegations that Myanmar committed genocide against the stateless Rohingya minority. Gambia initiated the lawsuit in November 2019 under the 1948 Genocide Convention. The landmark case follows decades of sectarian violence, military crackdowns, and mass refugee exoduses into neighboring Bangladesh.
articles.description: The ICJ had for seven years weighed the accusations made by Gambia against Myanmar’s treatment of its minority Rohingya community.

articles.headline: Geneva hosts world chess championship match starting on November 24
articles.title: Countdown: From Steinitz to Gukesh: an elite club of kings
articles.summary: The world chess championship match is set to begin in Geneva on November 24, featuring challenger Javokhir Sindarov and reigning champion D. Gukesh. As the elite club of undisputed world champions marks its 140th anniversary since Wilhelm Steinitz won the inaugural title in 1886, players must score 7.5 points across a 14-game format to claim victory in the prestigious mind sport competition.

articles.headline: Infant deaths rise in Attappadi as medical authorities examine ten cases
articles.title: In Keralam, the children beyond healthcare
articles.summary: Ten infant deaths have been reported this year in the tribal settlement of Attappadi, located in the Palakkad district of Keralam. Six of the cases involved congenital anomalies, including heart defects. An expert committee of researchers and doctors is currently examining the fatalities. Among the victims was five-month-old Dakshina, whose parents alleged that a cooperative hospital in Perinthalmanna withheld her body over unpaid medical bills.
articles.description: Attappady’s recurring infant deaths this year point to a crisis that goes beyond malnutrition and access to timely healthcare. Poverty, land alienation, and the erosion of traditional food systems, are taking a toll on maternal and child health in this predominantly tribal region of Keralam

articles.headline: African National Congress struggles to secure local government coalitions
articles.title: ANC fights to keep control of South Africa's key cities after election setback
articles.summary: The African National Congress is racing to form power-sharing agreements in South African cities following a historic drop in support during local elections. Winning a majority in only Limpopo province and securing the most votes in two cities, the party faces a November 27 deadline to negotiate local governments while appearing reluctant to replicate its national coalition with the Democratic Alliance.
articles.description: The ANC appears reluctant to replicate its national power-sharing deal with the pro-business DA at the local level.

articles.headline: Ancestral home of former Bangladesh leader Yunus set on fire
articles.title: Home of Bangladesh’s former leader Muhammad Yunus set on fire
articles.summary: The ancestral home of former interim Bangladesh leader Muhammad Yunus was set on fire in Chittagong before midnight on Wednesday, according to police. The arson occurred amid nationwide protests called by the Awami League party to mark the anniversary of the sentencing of ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina. Authorities reported no casualties and stated that an investigation is currently underway.
articles.description: The blaze broke out during heightened violence before ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina's planned return.

articles.headline: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani plans to close Rikers Island by 2032
articles.title: Mamdani announces plan to close New York's Rikers Island jail by 2032
articles.summary: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani has unveiled an official plan to shutter the notorious Rikers Island jail complex by 2032. The proposal aims to reduce the detainee population from over 6,500 to 4,100 while constructing four smaller new facilities across the city boroughs. The initiative includes significant investments in mental health and substance use treatment, although the correction officers union has strongly criticized the population cap.
articles.description: Plans to shutter the troubled facility date back to 2019, when the city council first voted to close it but delays arose over where to place inmates.

articles.headline: Trump accuses Iran of exploring chemical and biological weapons
articles.title: Trump claims Iran is developing bioweapons: Is there any evidence?
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump claimed on Thursday that Iran is exploring chemical and biological weapons, though he provided no evidence to support the allegation. The comments follow a recent United States intelligence report regarding potential threats to administration officials. While Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated there is no imminent threat, analysts note that Iran has a history of research into unconventional capabilities.
articles.description: Trump threatens to 'wipe out' Iran in case of attack as Tehran's capabilities remain unclear.

articles.headline: Overturned boat in southern Nigeria kills at least four mourners
articles.title: Overturned boat carrying mourners to funeral kills at least four in Nigeria
articles.summary: An overcrowded boat carrying passengers to a funeral capsized in southern Nigeria after suffering a mechanical failure. Police spokesperson Musa Mohammed stated that two adults and two children died in the accident in Bayelsa State. Twenty-four individuals were rescued by local divers and emergency responders, while the boat driver fled and the vessel manager was taken into custody following the incident.
articles.description: Police say two children among dead as search continues for more victims.

articles.headline: United States opposes globalist regulation of artificial intelligence
articles.title: Trump says U.S. opposes 'globalist regulation' of AI
articles.summary: President Donald Trump stated on November 19, 2026, that the United States opposes any form of globalist regulation of artificial intelligence, warning it could hinder national competitiveness. Speaking at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation meeting in Shenzhen ahead of talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping, Mr. Trump emphasized managing risks while rejecting international governance frameworks. Meanwhile, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney argued that the lack of global oversight poses significant risks.
articles.description: Despite the countries' fierce tech rivalry, AI safety risks of shared concern range from infrastructure hacking to people using the technology to help build bioweapons.

articles.headline: Rahul Gandhi backs strong India-Israel ties despite Gaza war
articles.title: Rahul Gandhi backs strong India-Israel ties despite Gaza war
articles.description: India’s opposition leader Rahul Gandhi, says New Delhi should continue to maintain strong ties with Israel.

articles.headline: Danish parliament ratifies security pact with United States and Greenland
articles.title: Denmark parliament approves security deal with Greenland and US
articles.summary: The Danish parliament unanimously ratified a security agreement with the United States covering Greenland to bolster Arctic security and ease tensions following threats by US President Donald Trump. Adopted by 109 votes on Thursday in Copenhagen, the pact allows the US to build two military bases and restricts non-EU and non-NATO nations from strategic sectors to limit Chinese and Russian influence.
articles.description: All 109 Danish lawmakers present approved the deal, easing tensions over Trump's desire to annex the Arctic island.

articles.headline: Anthropic prepares for public stock market debut with expected valuation over one trillion dollars
articles.title: Anthropic raises $81bn in record-breaking stock market debut
articles.summary: Artificial intelligence company Anthropic is set to price its shares at $83 each on the Nasdaq stock exchange in New York. The maker of the chatbot Claude expects to raise $94bn through its initial public offering and private placements, becoming the first US firm focused exclusively on AI to go public amid investor questions about profitability.
articles.description: The company behind the Claude chatbot will become one of the most valuable firms in the world.

articles.headline: Violence erupts in Bangladesh as Muhammad Yunus home is torched
articles.title: Yunus's ancestral home set ablaze as violence grips Bangladesh
articles.summary: Unidentified arsonists set fire to Muhammad Yunus ancestral home in Chattogram following a lockdown call issued by the banned Awami League. Police reported at least four injuries and numerous improvised explosive device detonations in Dhaka. The unrest coincided with the anniversary of a special tribunal sentencing former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina to death in absentia for crimes against humanity.
articles.description: Newspaper reports said rival activists, presumably belonging to Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP), overnight attacked or set ablaze the residences of two Awami League leaders in Dhaka.

articles.headline: Anthropic shares decline toward initial price amid broader technology sell-off
articles.title: Tech stock sell-off drags markets down as Anthropic shares slide
articles.summary: Anthropic shares fell more than twelve percent to approximately eighty-five dollars by Friday lunchtime, retreating toward their eighty-three dollar initial public offering price as a wider technology sector downturn affected global markets. The artificial intelligence firm, maker of the Claude chatbot, experienced the decline alongside drops in major United States indexes and global markets as investors shifted focus from growth toward profitability and cash flow.
articles.description: Pressures weighed on US markets, with the S&P 500 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average pushed into correction territory.

articles.headline: French police officers sentenced for racially motivated beating of music producer
articles.title: French police officers sentenced for beating of music producer Michel Zecler
articles.summary: Three French police officers were convicted of beating black music producer Michel Zecler in Paris and falsifying a police report. Aurelien Lapersonne, Philippe Tondeux, and Pierre Plantier received five-year sentences with varying suspended terms and lifetime police bans. The court upheld an aggravated circumstance of racism after CCTV footage exposed the 2020 assault during coronavirus lockdown restrictions.
articles.description: The court has upheld the 2020 beating of the black music producer as an aggravated circumstance of racism.

articles.headline: Supreme Court rules failed relationships cannot turn sex into rape
articles.title: Failed relationships cannot turn consensual sex into rape: Supreme Court
articles.summary: The Supreme Court stated on Friday, October 30, 2026, that women cannot retroactively classify consensual sexual acts as rape simply because a relationship has ended. Justice B.V. Nagarathna delivered the ruling in a Kerala case, cautioning that using the justice system for vengeance after a breakup dilutes the gravity of genuine offenses like sexual assault and subjects the accused to severe stigma and harassment.
articles.description: Court distinguishes between consent allegedly obtained through deception and regret over consensual intimacy after a relationship ends

articles.headline: Supreme Court lists marital rape petitions for final hearing in December
articles.title: Supreme Court to commence final hearing of pleas on marital rape in December
articles.summary: The Supreme Court of India announced on November 19, 2026, that a batch of petitions concerning marital rape exemptions will receive a final hearing in December, potentially before the winter break starts on December twenty-first. A Bench led by Chief Justice Surya Kant is set to examine whether the exception under criminal law violates constitutional rights.
articles.description: Under the exception clause of Section 375 of the Indian Penal Code, now repealed and replaced by the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, sexual intercourse or sexual acts by a man with his wife, the wife not being minor, is not rape

articles.headline: Supreme Court awaits central government stance on marital rape pleas
articles.title: Supreme Court to fix marital rape hearing date after Centre’s response
articles.summary: The Supreme Court announced on Monday, September 7, 2026, that it will wait for the central government to submit a substantive reply on petitions challenging the criminalisation of marital rape before scheduling a hearing date. Senior advocate Indira Jaising mentioned the matter before a bench led by Chief Justice Surya Kant, noting that formal pleadings and replies regarding the legal exceptions under criminal law remain incomplete.
articles.description: Senior advocate Indira Jaising urged a three-judge bench headed by CJI Surya Kant to list the marital rape petitions for hearing in November

articles.headline: Jammu and Kashmir deputy chief minister defends dialogue with Pakistan
articles.title: BJP’s invitation to Pakistan’s Minister vindicates Abdullah’s stance: J&K Deputy Chief Minister
articles.summary: Jammu and Kashmir Deputy Chief Minister Surinder Choudhary stated that the federal government's invitation to Pakistan's Minister Musadik Masood Malik for an event validated the National Conference stance on bilateral talks. Speaking on 20 November 2026, Choudhary emphasised the need for neighbourly relations while urging Pakistan to end terrorism. People's Democratic Party legislator Muntazir Mehdi also welcomed the ministerial visit.
articles.description: People’s Democratic Party legislator Muntazir Mehdi termed the Pakistani Minister’s visit to India “a welcome development” and urged the resumption of dialogue between India and Pakistan

articles.headline: Nvidia chief Jensen Huang resigns amid dual relationship scandals
articles.title: Jensen Huang | AI rainmaker meets his Waterloo
articles.summary: Jensen Huang stepped down as chief executive officer of Nvidia following reports of relationships with Alice Huang and Kimberly Powell. The controversy emerged alongside allegations involving a Chinese businesswoman at the center of a spy scandal, prompting intense scrutiny for the co-founder who built the technology company from its inception.
articles.description: The Nvidia chief’s abrupt exit marks a stunning fall from grace for the man who built the hardware foundation of the AI revolution, forged deep ties with Silicon Valley’s tech leaders and expanded the company’s reach across every layer of the AI stack

articles.headline: Aid groups condemn Gaza peace plan as humanitarian crisis deepens
articles.title: ‘Displacement by design’: Trump’s Gaza peace plan a failure, aid groups say
articles.summary: A coalition of five international aid organisations released a scorecard grading the United Nations Security Council-endorsed Gaza peace plan at four out of twenty-six points. The assessment follows a new Israeli ground offensive in central Gaza that expanded territorial control and displaced roughly two point one million Palestinians into a heavily congested area, leading to acute shortages and mounting winter casualties.
articles.description: With two million Palestinians confined to an area of less than 130sq km, UN-backed Gaza peace plan has collapsed.

articles.headline: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi calls for dialogue with China
articles.title: Japanese PM Takaichi calls for continued dialogue with China to ease bilateral tensions
articles.summary: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi urged continued communication with Beijing during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen to ease bilateral tensions stemming from her previous remarks on Taiwan. Speaking on November 19, 2026, she emphasized that China remains an important neighbor, while also discussing the detention of Japanese nationals and company treatment during a meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin.
articles.description: Earlier in the day, Ms. Takaichi shook hands with Chinese President Xi Jinping and later held a meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin

articles.headline: Trump calls for nuclear arms reduction at APEC summit
articles.title: Trump calls for nuclear arms reduction at APEC summit
articles.description: Trump calls for nuclear arms reduction at APEC summit

articles.headline: Odisha evacuates over one lakh people as cyclone Akvan approaches
articles.title: Cyclone ‘Akvan’ heads for Odisha; over one lakh people evacuated
articles.summary: Odisha evacuated more than one lakh people, including about 10,000 pregnant women, and positioned disaster response forces ahead of Severe Cyclonic Storm Akvan. The India Meteorological Department stated the storm is expected to cross the coast near Gopalpur by November 20 with maximum sustained wind speeds up to 100 kilometers per hour, prompting heavy rainfall warnings and closure of tourist sites and schools.
articles.description: Odisha Government closes coastal tourist sites including Chilika Lake, Puri beaches, Bhitarakanika and Nandankanan Zoological Park

articles.headline: Trinamool supporters allegedly attacked outside Kolkata police station during leader questioning
articles.title: Trinamool supporters attacked outside the police station as police questioned Abhishek
articles.summary: Clashes erupted on November 20, 2026, outside the Girish Park police station in Kolkata where All India Trinamool Congress leader Abhishek Banerjee was being questioned. Rival factions blamed each other for the violence, while the Trinamool party later filed a counter complaint against opposition leaders for past threats made against law enforcement officers.
articles.description: The supporters of Trinamool had gathered outside the police station in support of Abhishek Banerjee

articles.headline: Iraq PM targets militia stronghold in bid to assert state control
articles.title: Iraq PM targets militia stronghold in bid to assert state control
articles.description: Iraqi PM Ali al-Zaidi said an operation in Jurf al-Sakhar marks the start of a nationwide push to assert state control.

articles.headline: North Korea expands uranium enrichment facility at Yongbyon nuclear centre
articles.title: North Korea expanding uranium enrichment facility, UN nuclear watchdog says
articles.summary: North Korea has expanded its uranium enrichment facility at the Yongbyon nuclear centre between mid-September and late October 2026, according to International Atomic Energy Agency Director General Rafael Grossi. The ongoing development at the secretive site persists as United States President Donald Trump visits Asia and expresses readiness for renewed diplomatic dialogue with Pyongyang.
articles.description: North Korea can produce both highly enriched uranium and weapons-grade plutonium at its facilities, according to IAEA.

articles.headline: Sajjan Singh Yadav takes charge as new Chief Secretary of Jammu and Kashmir
articles.title: IAS officer Sajjan Singh Yadav assumes charge as Chief Secretary of J&K
articles.summary: Senior Indian Administrative Service officer Sajjan Singh Yadav formally assumed office as the Chief Secretary of Jammu and Kashmir. Officials welcomed the 1995-batch officer at the Civil Secretariat in Jammu. Yadav joins the Union Territory administration with extensive multi-sectoral experience, facing critical pending administrative files including daily wager regularisation and reservation rationalisation.
articles.description: He joins at a time when the Chief Secretary post acts as the main interface between the Lok Bhavan and the Chief Minister’s office in the Union Territory (UT)

articles.headline: US court orders delivery of summonses to Indian officials through Delhi courts
articles.title: U.S. court orders delivery of summonses to Doval, Goel through Delhi courts
articles.summary: A United States federal court ordered its clerk on November 13, 2026, to deliver summonses to National Security Advisor Ajit Doval and former Research and Analysis Wing chief Samant Goel through Delhi district courts. Judge Katherine Polk Failla authorized the alternative mode of service under the Hague Convention after standard procedures were rejected regarding a civil lawsuit filed by Khalistani separatist Gurpatwant Singh Pannun.
articles.description: Citing the Hague Conventions and relevant provisions of the Indian Code of Civil Procedure (CPC), a U.S. federal court Judge Katherine Polk Failla said foreign courts can serve summonses to Mr. Doval and Mr. Goel through Indian courts

articles.headline: Two Salvadoran soldiers killed in Haiti while handling explosive material.
articles.title: Three Salvadoran soldiers killed in Haiti while handling explosives
articles.summary: Two soldiers from El Salvador were killed and two others injured in an explosion at a military camp in Haiti, according to the Salvadoran army. The fatalities mark the first military deaths among approximately 2,500 troops deployed by President Nayib Bukele. The troops arrived following an initial rescue mission for missing aviation technicians before expanding into a broader gang-suppression operation.
articles.description: One other was injured in the explosion, marking the first deaths among troops deployed to Haiti since late October.

articles.headline: Can the UK and EU turn the page on Brexit?
articles.title: Can the UK and EU turn the page on Brexit?
articles.description: A decade after the Brexit vote, the UK and EU have struck deals. But divisions persist.

articles.headline: Chandel district administration issues advisory after spurious liquor kills 11 people.
articles.title: Chandel district official issues advisory after spurious liquor kills 11 in Manipur
articles.summary: Manipur authorities issued a public advisory on Friday following the deaths of 11 individuals from adulterated alcohol consumption in the Chakpikarong Sub-Division. Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh visited 180 affected patients receiving treatment at two private hospitals in Imphal. The local administration urged residents to report illicit alcohol activities and immediately seek medical evaluation for related symptoms.
articles.description: The Chandel district authorities have urged the people to report suspected manufacturing, storage, sale or distribution of adulterated liquor

articles.headline: Sudan conflict leaves disabled children without education and specialised support services.
articles.title: Sudan’s war leaves disabled children missing out on education
articles.summary: The ongoing war in Sudan has severely disrupted education and rehabilitation services for children with disabilities, leaving thousands without necessary institutional support.
