Organisations like the Usratuna Sudanese Association for Children with Disabilities are currently unable to operate due to facility damage, funding shortages, and safety concerns. Officials report that numerous schools remain non-operational or converted into shelters.
articles.description: War forces schools, rehabilitation centres to close, forcing children with disabilities to lose access to education.

articles.headline: Prime Minister Modi visits Bihar to inaugurate six-lane bridge named after Nitish Kumar.
articles.title: PM to visit Bihar to inaugurate a six-lane bridge named after ex-CM Nitish
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will visit the Vaishali district in Bihar on Friday to inaugurate a 9.76-kilometre six-lane bridge spanning the River Ganga. The infrastructure project, connecting Patna and Vaishali districts, has been officially named Nitish Setu after former Chief Minister Nitish Kumar. The naming decision has drawn opposition from the Rashtriya Janata Dal party amid ongoing political developments in the state.
articles.description: JD(U) working chief Sanjay Kumar Jha said that “the decision of CM Choudhary to name the bridge as Nitish Setu symbolises the immense affection, respect, and gratitude that Bihar people have for our leader Nitish Kumar”

articles.headline: Russia condemns Estonia over planned road border closure
articles.title: Russia complains of ‘new Iron Curtain’ as Estonia shuts its borders
articles.summary: Moscow criticized Tallinn after the Baltic state approved a preliminary six-month shutdown of road border crossings starting December 1. Russian officials warned of diplomatic retaliation, alleging the restrictions aim to construct a modern barrier. Estonian authorities stated the measure intends to prevent security threats and sanctions evasion following an alleged arson incident, though the Kremlin denied involvement.
articles.description: Tallinn's decision to shut road border crossings comes after an attack on a drone manufacturer.

articles.headline: Is Trump helping rehabilitate Putin on the world stage?
articles.title: Is Trump helping rehabilitate Putin on the world stage?
articles.description: Is Trump helping rehabilitate Putin on the world stage?

articles.headline: Islam projected to surpass Christianity as world religion by 2035
articles.title: Muslims to outnumber Christians by 2035 worldwide: Pew research
articles.summary: Islam is expected to become the largest global religion by 2035 and continue growing through 2070, driven primarily by higher fertility rates rather than conversions, according to a Pew Research Centre study released on November 18, 2026. The research indicates that while global populations will increase, India will see its Hindu majority shift slightly alongside rising numbers of religiously unaffiliated individuals worldwide.
articles.description: The absolute number of Hindus in India and worldwide will rise from 1.2 billion in 2020 to 1.4 billion by 2070

articles.headline: Saudi-led coalition intercepts Houthi missiles targeting Riyadh and south
articles.title: Saudi-led coalition intercepts Houthi missiles targeting Riyadh and south
articles.summary: The Saudi-led coalition announced it intercepted ballistic missiles launched toward Riyadh and Saudi Arabia's southern region by the Houthi armed group on Thursday. The attacks prompted retaliatory air raids on Sanaa, while the United Nations children's agency reported over 330,000 displacements due to renewed fighting, and the World Health Organization stated the death toll from the August escalation reached 2,260.
articles.description: Material damage was reported after ​debris fell following the latest Houthi strikes launched towards Saudi Arabia.

articles.headline: Xi, Trump and Putin exchange greetings ahead of Shenzhen summit
articles.title: Xi, Trump, Putin exchange greetings before historic China summit
articles.summary: Presidents Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin exchanged initial greetings in Shenzhen on November 18, 2026, ahead of their scheduled trilateral meeting during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit. Russian leader Vladimir Putin defended his military campaign in Ukraine by declaring that Western sanctions had failed, while international counterparts discussed nuclear disarmament and regional security issues.
articles.description: The agenda for the November 19 meeting between Presidents Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin -- which has raised fears of a carve-up into new "spheres of influence" -- was unclear

articles.headline: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announces new military deal with Venezuela
articles.title: Why is Pete Hegseth strengthening US military ties with Venezuela?
articles.summary: United States Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced a cooperation agreement with Venezuela's interim government in Caracas on Wednesday to combat drug trafficking and enhance border security. Interim President Delcy Rodriguez welcomed the pact, which follows the January ousting of former President Nicolas Maduro and the ongoing US control over revenue generated from Venezuelan oil sales administered through accounts supervised by Washington.
articles.description: Hegseth's new military deal with Venezuela raises questions about US influence, regional security and Maduro's removal.

articles.headline: Israeli soldiers face psychological trauma and denial over Gaza conflict
articles.title: Gaza Syndrome: Why Israeli soldiers’ trauma erases Palestinian victims
articles.summary: Thousands of Israeli soldiers and security personnel have entered the Defence Ministry rehabilitation system since October 7, with about 63 percent suffering from psychological injuries like post-traumatic stress disorder. The Israeli army reported 22 soldier suicides in 2025. Experts and trauma therapists warn that untreated combat trauma, combined with a lack of remorse and widespread impunity, poses severe societal risks within Israel.
articles.description: Israeli soldiers describe the psychological toll of the genocide in Gaza, yet many express no remorse.

articles.headline: Monsoon rain to resume across Tamil Nadu after cyclone
articles.title: Following Cyclone Akvan, monsoon rain to resume over T.N. from tomorrow
articles.summary: Tamil Nadu experienced a brief pause in monsoon activity following the passage of Cyclone Akvan on Friday, leading to a temporary rise in daytime temperatures and ground frost in isolated regions. The Regional Meteorological Centre reported that wet weather is set to return on Sunday and intensify across several districts through November 26.
articles.description: The RMC has forecast moderate rainfall in coastal districts, including Chennai and Cuddalore, and mild rainfall over adjoining areas; wet weather likely to last till the first week of December

articles.headline: French authorities investigate Gérard Depardieu and Michel Houellebecq over allegations
articles.title: Gérard Depardieu and French author investigated over sexual allegations
articles.summary: French judicial authorities launched an investigation into actor Gérard Depardieu and author Michel Houellebecq following a complaint filed in May 2025 regarding alleged sexual misconduct during a 2018 film set. An unnamed actress accused the men of assault, while the film director faces allegations of complicity after reportedly filming the incident.
articles.description: A judicial investigation was launched after a complaint was filed last year over "allegations of a sexual nature".

articles.headline: Madras High Court orders CB-CID probe into disputed will
articles.title: Lawyer seeks to probate will left behind by former DGP’s wife: Madras High Court orders CB-CID probe after suspecting its genuineness
articles.summary: The Madras High Court directed the Crime Branch-Criminal Investigation Department to register a First Information Report and investigate a lawyer's claim regarding a will left by Rani Ravindran, wife of a former Director General of Police. The court suspected land grabbing and ordered the Administrator General and Official Trustee to take possession of properties in Chennai and New Delhi.
articles.description: Justices N. Sathish Kumar and G.K. Muthukumaar direct incumbent DGP Mahesh Kumar Aggarwal to ensure that an investigation gets conducted after registering a FIR

articles.headline: Calcutta High Court rules Abhishek Banerjee's comments not contemptuous
articles.title: Comments by Abhishek Banerjee painful but not contemptuous: Calcutta High Court
articles.summary: The Calcutta High Court stated that remarks made by Trinamool leader Abhishek Banerjee regarding the judiciary were painful but did not amount to wilful contempt while extending his interim protection in a police case. Justice Saugata Bhattacharya questioned the MP's actions during the hearing, following separate criminal contempt proceedings initiated by another judge over social media posts.
articles.description: The development comes days after Justice Krishna Rao of the Calcutta High Court on November 17 issued criminal contempt proceedings against Abhishek Banerjee for remarks made on November 7

articles.headline: Bengaluru court rejects anticipatory bail pleas in Siddaramaiah sting case
articles.title: Court rejects anticipatory bail pleas of six in Siddaramaiah ‘sting’ case
articles.summary: A Bengaluru court denied anticipatory bail applications for six individuals, including expelled Congress leader Kripa Alva, linked to an alleged sting operation targeting former Chief Minister Siddaramaiah. The city police registered the case under the Information Technology Act based on a complaint regarding a circulating defamation video, which investigation traces back to a Union Minister's residence.

articles.headline: Karnataka Chief Minister meets examination reform task force
articles.title: State candidates should get better opportunities in medical colleges, Chief Minister tells high-powered task force
articles.summary: Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar met with a high-powered task force on examination reforms chaired by Nandan Nilekani to discuss incorporating board exam marks into National Eligibility cum Entrance Test results. State representatives supported board exam weightage, while officials also addressed infrastructure requirements for implementing computer-based testing to prevent paper leaks across government examinations.
articles.description: ‘Given that it is difficult for rural students to compete with their urban counterparts in national-level examinations like NEET, grace marks should be provided to students from rural areas’

articles.headline: Anbumani Ramadoss questions dismissal of Guidance TN employees
articles.title: State govt. should clarify on dismissal of Guidance employees: Anbumani
articles.summary: Pattali Makkal Katchi president Anbumani Ramadoss expressed concern over the reported dismissal of fifteen Guidance TN employees and urged the Tamil Nadu government to clarify the situation. Citing investments from South Korean companies shifting to Andhra Pradesh, he highlighted conflicting accounts regarding whether employees were dismissed or resigned due to an unfavourable working environment.
articles.description: People have a right to know the truth behind these reports after investments worth ₹1,614 crore from three South Korean companies that were expected to come to Tamil Nadu moved to Andhra Pradesh: PMK leader

articles.headline: Former election commissioner Quraishi warns institutional credibility is at risk
articles.title: Safeguards against abuse of power essential to preserve critical institutions like ECI: S.Y. Quraishi
articles.summary: Former Chief Election Commissioner S.Y. Quraishi warned on November 20, 2026, that constitutional bodies like the Election Commission of India require stronger safeguards against power abuse. Delivering a lecture in Delhi, he criticized political appointments and procedural flaws, citing the West Bengal SIR voter deletions and urging independent oversight to prevent permanent damage to democratic institutions.
articles.description: He said the ECI’s credibility had come under strain since 2019; the controversy over the 2024 Lok Sabha election turnout figure also did not help

articles.headline: Experts say impact of United States blockade on Iran remains unclear
articles.title: ‘Too early’ to determine impact of US blockade on Iran, with Tehran defiant
articles.summary: The United States economic embargo and naval blockade on Iran are expected to contract the Iranian economy further, though experts state it remains too early to determine if Washington will achieve its goals. Iran Central Bank Governor Abdolnaser Hemmati noted the country has secured 30 billion dollars in foreign currencies, while annual inflation reached 76.8 percent in the twelve-month period ending October 22.
articles.description: The US blockade of Iranian ports has a crippling effect on the economy, but Tehran insists its economy can survive.

articles.headline: White House replaces national cyber director Sean Cairncross following tech failures
articles.title: White House removes cyber-security chief after series of tech outages
articles.summary: National cyber director Sean Cairncross is leaving his position following a series of technological outages that impacted the National Security Agency, air traffic control, and banks. Secretary of State Marco Rubio announced that Department of Defense chief information officer Kirsten Davies will replace him. Media reports indicated Cairncross was dismissed after losing the confidence of White House chief of staff Stephen Miller.
articles.description: He has been fired after losing the confidence of new White House chief of staff Stephen Miller, according to reports.

articles.headline: India and Canada plan to announce defence pact in December
articles.title: India, Canada eye defence pact during Modi visit in December
articles.summary: India and Canada are expected to sign a defence agreement during Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s visit on December 11 and 12, 2026. High Commissioner Dinesh K. Patnaik stated that both nations have restored trust following diplomatic tensions over the 2023 murder of Hardeep Singh Nijjar. Negotiations for a comprehensive economic partnership are also nearing completion.
articles.description: India’s High Commissioner to Ottawa says both countries cannot afford to let fringe issues derail their extensive mutual interests

articles.headline: Prime Minister Modi meets Prince and Princess of Wales in New Delhi
articles.title: PM Modi meets Prince and Princess of Wales, discusses boosting U.K.-India ties
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi met Prince William and Princess Catherine in New Delhi on November 18, 2026, to discuss strengthening the India-U.K. Comprehensive Strategic Partnership. According to a Prime Minister's Office statement, the talks covered defense, health, and education, while Modi praised the Earthshot Prize for recognizing innovative environmental solutions during the royal couple's three-day visit.
articles.description: PM commends the work of the 'Earthshot Prize' in encouraging innovative solutions to pressing environmental challenges

articles.headline: Trump, Xi and Putin meet in Shenzhen for trilateral summit
articles.title: Xi-Putin-Trump trilateral: Why is it being compared to 1945 Yalta Conference?
articles.summary: Leaders from the United States, China and Russia gathered in Shenzhen on November 19, 2026, for a high-level meeting on the sidelines of the APEC Summit. While commentators drew parallels to the 1945 Yalta Conference, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky expressed concern over potential geopolitical restructuring, though Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov dismissed comparisons as political science games.
articles.description: The Xi-Putin-Jinping meet is being compared with the Yalta Conference of 1945, which led to the establishment of four quarters of post-Nazi Germany and laid the foundations of the United Nations.

articles.headline: Officials urge complete coverage for population phase of Census 2027
articles.title: Ensure no household is left out in Census enumeration, officials told
articles.summary: District Revenue Officer S.D. Anita instructed officials to accurately complete the population enumeration phase of Census 2027 within the stipulated timeframe. Speaking in Visakhapatnam, she emphasized that all households and homeless individuals must be counted. GVMC Additional Commissioner K. Ramesh suggested a forty percent self-enumeration target, which will be available from January 10 to 24, 2027, under the Census Act, 1948.

articles.headline: IEA warns West Asia crisis poses unprecedented threat to global energy security
articles.title: West Asia crisis 'largest threat' to energy security ever: IEA
articles.summary: The International Energy Agency warned on November 19, 2026, that the West Asia crisis sparked by United States and Israeli bombing of Iran in February has created the largest threat to energy security in history. Executive Director Fatih Birol noted that consumers face higher prices and supply shortfalls as Gulf nations struggle to export oil due to blockades in the Strait of Hormuz.
articles.description: The report said elsewhere that "increasingly it is falling to consumers — and high prices — to absorb the impact as other buffers are run down"

articles.headline: Swimming lessons offer Gaza’s children a moment of relief
articles.title: Swimming lessons offer Gaza’s children a moment of relief
articles.description: Palestinian children gathered along Gaza’s coast for swimming lessons, finding relief from the psychological toll of war

articles.headline: Chief Minister promises action over attacks against Youth Congress workers
articles.title: CM promises action over alleged attacks, police atrocities against YC workers
articles.summary: Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan promised strict accountability for alleged attacks and police atrocities against Youth Congress workers during the previous administration. Speaking in Kannur, he assured party members that investigation teams would pursue all cases without compromise. Additionally, he announced plans to expand nursing education seats in Keralam from ten thousand to thirty thousand within three years to retain young talent.
articles.description: The Chief Minister says that everyone found responsible will face action regardless of their position and that the government will pursue the cases to the end.

articles.headline: Kerala appoints expert committee to investigate air quality data discrepancies
articles.title: Keralam’s air quality under scrutiny amid discrepancies in air quality data
articles.summary: The Kerala government has formed an expert committee to address conflicting Air Quality Index readings in Kochi and Thiruvananthapuram. The panel, including members from The Energy and Resources Institute and NIT Calicut, will identify reasons for data mismatches and recommend mitigation measures. The committee must submit a detailed report to the state government within two weeks.
articles.description: The committee has been constituted against the backdrop of discrepancies in recent Air Quality Index readings for Kochi and Thiruvananthapuram, which have heightened public concern

articles.headline: Nvidia must hire outside chief executive after Huang departure, Bessent says
articles.title: U.S. Treasury chief Scott Bessent wants answers soon from Nvidia
articles.summary: United States Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent stated that Nvidia must hire an outside chief executive following the resignation of Jensen Huang. Huang stepped down on November 12, 2026, amid revelations of extramarital affairs, including one involving a suspected Chinese spy. Bessent added that the board and outside counsel must answer questions regarding export compliance within 10 days.
articles.description: U.S. Treasury ‌Secretary Bessent said he wants to know if Nvidia used shell companies to dodge U.S. restrictions and sell its most powerful chips to China

articles.headline: Supreme Court permits one-time lamp lighting at Thirupparankundram Hill
articles.title: Supreme Court allows lighting of lamp on deepathoon at Thirupparankundram as limited one-time arrangement
articles.summary: The Supreme Court of India has granted permission for a lamp to be lit on the Thirupparankundram Hill for the Karthigai Deepam festival on November 24, 2026. Justice Aravind Kumar described the ruling as a limited, one-time arrangement. The court imposed strict security protocols, including barring public gatherings and requiring a status report from the District Collector.
articles.description: A Bench headed by Justice Aravind Kumar, however, stayed the conclusive findings of the Madras High Court in a January 6 judgment that upheld the right to light the lamp on the deepathoon as an essential practice

articles.headline: Keralam government sanctions investigation into former Sports Minister V. Abdurahiman
articles.title: Messi visit row: Keralam govt. grants sanction to investigate former Sports Minister V. Abdurahiman
articles.summary: The State government sanctioned an investigation under the Prevention of Corruption Act against former Sports Minister V. Abdurahiman and two former officials regarding financial irregularities tied to an aborted visit by the Argentina national football team. The Special Investigation Team, led by Additional Director General of Police P. Vijayan, alleges that officials bypassed standard procedures to benefit event sponsor Reporter Broadcasting Company.
articles.description: According to an order issued by the Home department, the Special Investigation Team (SIT) probing the case has been cleared to incorporate relevant sections of the Prevention of Corruption Act into its ongoing investigation

articles.headline: Akhilesh Yadav meets opposition leaders to discuss alliance in Uttar Pradesh
articles.title: Akhilesh Yadav meets CPI(ML), AAP leaders fuelling talk of wider Opposition alliance in Uttar Pradesh
articles.summary: Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav met with Communist Party of India (Marxist-Leninist) general secretary Dipankar Bhattacharya and Aam Aadmi Party leader Sanjay Singh in Lucknow to discuss strengthening the India bloc and upcoming assembly elections. The discussions on November 19 and 20, 2026, come as opposition parties explore coalition possibilities while seat-sharing negotiations between the Samajwadi Party and Congress remain ongoing ahead of next year's state polls.
articles.description: SP and Congress yet to finalise seat-sharing pact; discussions scheduled on November 23; sources say CPI(ML) has been asked by the SP to submit a list of seats it wishes to contest

articles.headline: Bengaluru police restructuring faces criticism over uneven division distribution
articles.title: Bengaluru Police Commissionerate restructuring leaves some divisions overburdened and others underutilised
articles.summary: The recent reorganization of the Bengaluru City Police Commissionerate into five parts has drawn criticism for creating an unbalanced distribution of police stations. Officials report that the process lacked data-backed planning and sufficient consultation. Several rapidly urbanizing areas remain under rural police jurisdiction, while new divisions like Peenya are left with disproportionately few stations.
articles.description: The newly created Peenya division has been the biggest casualty. Under the supervision of a single DCP, the division, which falls under the West Commissionerate, has only four police stations

articles.headline: Indian seafarer remains missing following second attack on tanker
articles.title: One Indian seafarer of LPG ship still missing
articles.summary: One Indian crew member, identified as third officer K. Subramanian from Aruppukottai, is unaccounted for after the Panama-flagged LPG tanker Tara Gas suffered a second attack in the Strait of Hormuz near Oman. The Very Large Gas Carrier, carrying twenty-five crew members, was initially struck by a missile on November 16, resulting in hull damage and a fire before subsequent assaults forced the crew to abandon ship.
articles.description: The missing seafarer is from Aruppukottai in Tamil Nadu, who was serving as third officer on board the vessel, which was attacked a second time in the Strait of Hormuz

articles.headline: Ukraine targets Kerch bridge with successive drone and missile strikes
articles.title: Why Ukraine keeps targeting the Kerch Bridge
articles.summary: Ukrainian forces launched back-to-back attacks using drones and missiles against the Kerch bridge, damaging both the road and rail infrastructure linking mainland Russia to Crimea. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy described the assault as an unprecedented operation involving a seven-stage plan. Russian authorities acknowledged the damage and restricted transport, though the impact is mitigated by existing land corridors and ferry services.
articles.description: Ukraine has targeted the structure several times, latest on November 17, 2026

articles.headline: Protesters rally across twenty-five European countries over living costs and wages
articles.title: Protests held across Europe over wages, services, high living costs
articles.summary: Demonstrators took to the streets across twenty-five European countries on Friday, organizing rallies in nations including the United Kingdom, Austria, Germany, Spain, Italy, Sweden, and Croatia to protest high living costs, low wages, and increased military spending. Inspired by recent unrest in France, thousands of workers and students participated in strikes and demonstrations, with trade unions and youth groups criticizing government budget policies and demanding greater public service investments.
articles.description: Workers and students take to the streets as protests inspired by demonstrations in France show no sign of abating.

articles.headline: Pakistan army chief Munir vows to eliminate terrorism from country
articles.title: Pakistan Army chief Munir vows to eliminate terrorism from country
articles.summary: Pakistan Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir expressed security forces resolve to eradicate terrorism during a November 2026 visit to Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. According to the Inter-Services Public Relations, Munir reviewed intelligence-based operations and praised troop readiness. The Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies reported a national decline in violence for October.
articles.description: Pakistan overall witnessed a significant decline in terrorism-related violence during October, with attacks falling by 37%, deaths resulting from these attacks declining by 57%, and injuries decreasing by 71% compared to September, said Dawn newspaper report

articles.headline: NIA anti-terror conference discusses cross-border terrorism and drone threats
articles.title: NIA’s anti-terror conference discusses cross-border terrorism, threat from drones
articles.summary: The National Investigation Agency concluded its sixth Anti-Terror Conference in New Delhi on November 19, 2026, focusing on cross-border threats and drone smuggling. According to Director General Rakesh Aggarwal, officials addressed international cooperation and prosecution strategies. Union Home Minister Amit Shah reiterated a zero-tolerance policy, while Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan urged states to strengthen anti-terror units.
articles.description: NIA D-G Rakesh Aggarwal says drone smuggling of arms, narcotics, cash and explosives was a key concern, while adding that cheap and easily available drones are increasingly being used in cross-border operations

articles.headline: Qatar’s emir calls for diplomacy to end regional conflicts
articles.title: Qatar’s emir calls for diplomacy to end regional conflicts
articles.description: Qatar’s Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani called for diplomatic efforts to de-escalate conflicts.

articles.headline: US sanctions Myanmar armed group leader over cyberscam links
articles.title: U.S. sanctions Myanmar armed group leader over scam links
articles.summary: The United States Treasury Department froze assets on November 19, 2026, for General Saw Shwe Wah, commander-in-chief of the Democratic Karen Benevolent Army, and Colonel Saw A One over allegations of facilitating cyberscam compounds and human trafficking. Washington also sanctioned Zhao Hui and two companies for operating scams in Cambodia, following regional crackdowns against illicit financial networks.
articles.description: The U.S. Treasury Department said on November 19 it had imposed an asset freeze on General Saw Shwe Wah, commander-in-chief of the Democratic Karen Benevolent Army (DKBA), and one of his top officers, and had banned Americans from dealing with them

articles.headline: UN top court to deliver verdict in Rohingya genocide case against Myanmar
articles.title: ICJ to rule on Rohingya genocide case against Myanmar: What’s at stake?
articles.summary: The International Court of Justice in The Hague is scheduled to rule on whether Myanmar committed genocide against its Rohingya Muslim minority during a 2017 military crackdown. Brought by The Gambia under the 1948 Genocide Convention, the case centers on allegations that military operations forced hundreds of thousands to flee to Bangladesh, where approximately 1.2 million refugees now live in camps.
articles.description: World court to issue key verdict in its first genocide ruling in more than a decade.

articles.headline: Bangladesh hit by fresh arson attacks amid political unrest
articles.title: Bangladesh hit by fresh arson attacks in political unrest
articles.summary: Fresh arson attacks occurred across Bangladesh on November 20, 2026, amid unrest over the planned December return of former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, who was sentenced to death in absentia. Attackers targeted properties including a junior minister residence and Grameen Bank branches. Police reported 124 arrests in Dhaka as paramilitary troops deployed to contain violence.
articles.description: Police said 124 people linked to the Awami League had been arrested in the capital Dhaka over the past 24 hours, without providing further details

articles.headline: US Democrat Jamie Raskin warns Trump administration against destroying official records
articles.title: Top US Democrat warns Trump admin against destroying records
articles.summary: Congressman Jamie Raskin warned the United States Department of Justice and Department of Homeland Security on November 20, 2026, to preserve records, citing evidence that Trump administration officials used encrypted messaging apps like Signal to delete communications. Raskin instructed officials to recover the data by December 3. The White House defended its compliance with federal recordkeeping laws.
articles.description: In a new letter, Congressman Jamie Raskin says officials in the US government are ignoring federal recordkeeping laws.

articles.headline: European leaders gather in Berlin to discuss Ukraine defence funding and peace talks
articles.title: Far from Trump-Putin meeting, Europe to count cost of Ukraine’s defence
articles.summary: European leaders are gathering in Berlin on Thursday for a summit hosted by German Chancellor Friedrich Merz to agree on funding for Ukraine and secure a role in upcoming peace talks. The meeting follows a European Commission proposal for an additional 45 billion euro loan for 2027, amid ongoing transatlantic disagreements over military strategy and long-range strikes against Russian infrastructure.
articles.description: European leaders set to meet in Berlin as Kyiv faces a 25 billion-euro ($27.4bn) financing gap next year.

articles.headline: Italian workers and students strike nationwide over wages and public services
articles.title: Italian workers, students protest over wages and public services
articles.summary: Tens of thousands of workers and students participated in a general strike across Italy on November 20, 2026, called by the CGIL trade union to demand higher wages and increased public spending. CGIL leader Maurizio Landini reported over one million demonstrators in more than 100 cities. The protests targeted Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni's government and its 2027 budget.
articles.description: Parliament is examining Meloni's €26 billion ($30 billion) budget for 2027, which CGIL says does not go far enough to support incomes and public services

articles.headline: Lodge owner and employee arrested following Adivasi youth's death
articles.title: Lodge owner, employee arrested in Bhadrachalam over assault and death of Adivasi youth
articles.summary: Bhadrachalam police arrested a lodge owner and an employee on November 20 following the death of 23-year-old Tellam Sharath. The victim, an Adivasi youth, allegedly died after being assaulted by the suspects during a dispute over room allotment on November 16. The accused have been remanded in judicial custody as investigations into the incident continue.

articles.headline: Karnataka government to establish India's first sports technology center
articles.title: Karnataka to open India’s first government Sports Technology CoE
articles.summary: The Karnataka government signed a letter of intent with Bengaluru-based Amagi Media Labs to launch a Centre of Excellence for Sports Technologies. The facility will focus on sports analytics, athlete development, and research. Funded by the state, the center aims to integrate industry expertise to strengthen India’s growing sports ecosystem, currently valued at 1.99 lakh crore.
articles.description: To this end, the government has on Thursday signed a Letter of Intent with Amagi Media Labs, a cloud-based software-as-a-service firm based in Bengaluru

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh approves exploration of small modular reactor nuclear power
articles.title: Andhra Pradesh clears APGenco plan to explore SMR-based nuclear power
articles.summary: The Andhra Pradesh government has authorized APGenco to explore establishing nuclear power plants using Small Modular Reactor technology. The initiative targets sites where thermal power units are retiring. The project will proceed in phases, pending technology stabilization and regulatory reviews. Officials previously discussed potential collaborations with Russian nuclear firm Rosatom for next-generation power generation.
articles.description: Government permits APGenco to examine SMR plants at retiring thermal-power sites or other suitable locations; private-sector participation envisaged after the technology stabilises

articles.headline: Britain's Prince William launches accident insurance for temporary Indian forest personnel
articles.title: Britain’s Prince William announces insurance scheme for 10,000 temporary forest personnel
articles.summary: Beginning in December 2026, a five-year accident insurance programme will protect 10,000 temporary forest personnel across seven Indian states. Announced by Britain's Prince William in November 2026, the initiative covers daily-wage watchers facing severe occupational hazards like animal attacks. The partnership involves United for Wildlife, K.M. Dastur and Company, and local conservation groups to assist vulnerable workers lacking government benefits.
articles.description: The programme, which will begin in December 2026, will cover personnel in Madhya Pradesh, Karnataka, Assam, Uttarakhand, Maharashtra, Kerala and Rajasthan

articles.headline: John Brittas warns Parliament Winter Session uncertainty threatens accountability tool
articles.title: Parliament Winter Session uncertainty puts Question Hour at risk: John Brittas
articles.summary: Communist Party of India Marxist Rajya Sabha leader John Brittas warned that ongoing uncertainty regarding the Parliament Winter Session threatens Question Hour. Pointing out that the Monsoon Session adjourned in August 2026 without prorogation, Brittas criticized the government for maintaining total secrecy. He emphasized that a 15-day notice period is essential for members to file questions and hold the administration accountable.
articles.description: CPI(M) Rajya Sabha leader says that MPs need to send questions in advance, with at least 15 days of notice; with no clarity on the session, this exercise cannot begin, he says

articles.headline: Commercial coal mine auctions attract 85 bids and twenty first-time bidders
articles.title: Coal auction rounds attract 85 bids; 20 first-time players enter sector
articles.summary: The sixteenth round of commercial coal mine auctions in India attracted 83 bids for 17 blocks, alongside two bids for a block from the previous round, according to an announcement by the Union Coal Ministry on November 20, 2026. Twenty first-time bidders entered the sector, marking a quadrupling in bids compared with the preceding round of auctions.
articles.description: The 16th round of commercial mine auctions put forth 25 blocks, comprising 21 fully explored and four partially explored mines.

articles.headline: Enforcement Directorate searches former MLA Rekha Naik's residence and rice mill
articles.title: Paddy diversion case: ED searches former MLA Rekha Naik’s residence, rice mill linked to her in Khanapur mandal of Nirmal district
articles.summary: Enforcement Directorate officials conducted simultaneous searches at former MLA A. Rekha Naik's residence and a linked rice mill in Khanapur mandal of Nirmal district. The Friday raids examined financial transactions regarding the alleged diversion of paddy worth 40.96 crore rupees allocated under the Custom Milled Rice process across three rabi seasons. A local police case was registered against the mill management in August 2026.

articles.headline: Telangana merchandise exports surge significantly under Revanth Reddy's Congress administration
articles.title: Telangana’s merchandise exports surge in 3-years of Congress regime
articles.summary: Merchandise exports in Telangana increased significantly during the first three years of the Revanth Reddy-led Congress government, rising 68 percent higher compared to the previous Bharat Rashtra Samithi regime. Driven by manufacturing sector support, annual exports reached 1,33,000 crore rupees, led by strong growth in engineering goods, pharmaceuticals, and aerospace components from districts like Medchal-Malkajgiri and Hyderabad.
articles.description: Average annual merchandise export rose 68% from ₹79,000 crore during 2020-2023 period under BRS to ₹1,33,000 crore in 2023-2026 on the back of the Congress government’s support to the manufacturing sector

articles.headline: Cost of living protests sweep across Europe
articles.title: Cost of living protests sweep across Europe
articles.description: Thousands marched across European cities on Friday to protest against the cost of living and other issues.

articles.headline: Trump administration asks Supreme Court to end Venezuelan migrant protections
articles.title: Trump makes third Supreme Court bid to end Venezuelan migrant protections
articles.summary: The United States Department of Justice filed an emergency application asking the Supreme Court to suspend a federal judge's ruling that blocked officials from ending Temporary Protected Status for hundreds of thousands of Venezuelan migrants. Government attorneys argued that reinstating the protections would prevent up to 332 removal orders and cause severe harm, marking the third appeal to the nation's top court on this issue.
articles.description: Emergency appeal follows a California judge's ruling that ending their temporary protected status was unlawful.

articles.headline: NIA requests UAE assistance to investigate flydubai co-pilot attack on captain
articles.title: NIA sends request to UAE to probe any Indian footprints of copilot of flydubai flight who attacked Smit Machchhar
articles.summary: The National Investigation Agency sent a mutual legal assistance request to the United Arab Emirates on November 20, 2026, to investigate the Indian footprints of an Omani co-pilot who attacked Indian Captain Smit Machchhar on a flydubai flight on September 30, 2026. NIA Director-General Rakesh Aggarwal stated the request seeks document copies and permission to examine witnesses.
articles.description: “Who did the co-pilot come in contact with? Are there any Indian footprints of his friends circle who could be lurking. We will go ahead as soon as we get documents and permission from UAE to join the investigation,” says NIA chief

articles.headline: Chief Economic Adviser urges alignment of capital markets with development priorities
articles.title: CEA flags need to align capital markets with India’s development priorities
articles.summary: Chief Economic Adviser V. Anantha Nageswaran spoke at the Confederation of Indian Industry Financial Summit in Mumbai on November 20, 2026, calling for capital markets to channel household savings into productive investments. Nageswaran noted that equity market capitalisation reached approximately 130 percent of gross domestic product, while the corporate bond market remained at roughly 16 percent.
articles.description: Equity market capitalisation stood at around 130% of GDP, while the corporate bond market accounted for only about 16%.

articles.headline: Qatar and Germany expand cooperation on defence and investment
articles.title: Qatar and Germany deepen strategic ties during emir’s Berlin visit
articles.summary: Qatar’s Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani met with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz and President Frank-Walter Steinmeier in Berlin on November 20, 2026, to broaden diplomatic, security, and economic ties. Chancellor Merz announced that Qatar pledged 15 billion euros in investments for artificial intelligence and aviation, while leaders discussed diplomatic solutions to end the war on Iran.
articles.description: German chancellor says Qatar pledged $16.5bn in new investments as the two countries deepen defence and technology ties.

articles.headline: US Senate passes bipartisan bill to accelerate energy project approvals
articles.title: US Senate passes bill to speed up energy project approvals
articles.summary: The United States Senate voted 62 to 33 on November 20, 2026, to pass a bipartisan bill designed to shorten federal review timelines for power plants and transmission lines. Supported by President Donald Trump, the legislation aims to lower electricity bills and meet artificial intelligence demands, though environmental groups criticized it for weakening protections and boosting fossil fuels.
articles.description: The legislation aims to lower energy bills by making energy project approvals faster and limiting court challenges.

articles.headline: Santiago Abascal and Vox party emerge as potential kingmakers in snap election
articles.title: ‘Expel invaders’: The dangerous promises of Spain’s far-right Vox party
articles.summary: As Spain approaches a November 29 snap election, the far-right Vox party led by Santiago Abascal could emerge as a kingmaker in a coalition with the conservative Popular Party. Campaigning on anti-immigration policies, remigration, and nationalist priorities, Vox has grown in popularity. The party focuses its exclusionary rhetoric on Muslim migrants while welcoming Latin American newcomers through shared cultural and linguistic ties.
articles.description: As Spain prepares to vote, Vox is campaigning on mass deportations and 'national priority'.

articles.headline: Anthropic shares rise following Nasdaq debut as broader technology stocks decline
articles.title: Anthropic’s 17% IPO gain fails to lift AI stocks as Nasdaq slides 2.25%
articles.summary: Artificial intelligence firm Anthropic closed 17.1 percent higher on its Nasdaq debut under the ticker ANT on November 20, 2026, after trading at 97.17 dollars. Despite the strong listing, the debut failed to lift the wider sector as the Nasdaq Composite dropped 2.25 percent amid mounting investor concerns regarding stretched valuations across technology stocks.
articles.description: The stock opened 34% above its IPO price and closed 17% higher, but a technology sell-off and contrasting views among investors left questions about the wider AI rally.

articles.headline: Miami federal court convicts Florida pastor over the assassination of Haitian President Jovenel Moise
articles.title: Miami court convicts US-Haitian pastor over 2021 assassination of president
articles.summary: Christian Emmanuel Sanon, a Florida pastor holding dual American and Haitian citizenship, has been found guilty in a Miami federal court on eight charges related to the 2021 assassination of Haitian President Jovenel Moise. Prosecutors stated that the conspiracy involved foreign mercenaries funded through United States pandemic relief programmes, leaving Sanon facing up to life in prison with sentencing scheduled for February 10.
articles.description: Prosecutors accused Christian Emmanuel Sanon of seeking to replace then-Haitian President Moise.

articles.headline: SEBI proposes review of additional disclosure framework for foreign portfolio investors
articles.title: SEBI mulls review of additional disclosure norms for FPIs; floats consultation paper
articles.summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India released a consultation paper on November 20, 2026, proposing the removal of additional disclosure norms for Foreign Portfolio Investors to align with global standards and improve ease of doing business. Public comments are open until December 11 as foreign investors have withdrawn more than 5.61 lakh crore rupees since late 2024.
articles.description: The proposal aims to improve ease of doing business for foreign investors and make Indian capital markets a more attractive investment destination; SEBI has sought public comments on the proposal till December 11

articles.headline: Russia warns EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas would collapse Ukraine talks
articles.title: Russia says role for EU's Kallas in Ukraine talks with Moscow would lead to their collapse
articles.summary: Russian Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova stated on November 20, 2026, that involving European Union foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas in Ukraine peace negotiations with Moscow would derail the talks. Ms. Kallas previously argued that Russia cannot choose the bloc's representatives and must agree to a ceasefire first. Meanwhile, Deputy Foreign Minister Sergei Ryabkov noted that a potential Moscow visit by European envoys is being discussed.
articles.description: Zakharova told a press briefing in Moscow that Kallas was totally unsuitable to take part in such talks and listed ‌a series of statements from Kallas which she ​said showed the EU official was anti-Russian

articles.headline: Infra push and low base effect pushes core sector growth to series-high of 10.9% in October 2026
articles.title: Infra push and low base effect pushes core sector growth to series-high of 10.9% in October 2026
articles.description: While the coal and electricity sectors saw growth shoot up, a large part of this was due to a statistical effect rather than growth in actual output. On the other hand, fuel-related sectors contracted again

articles.headline: Munduruku communities face mercury poisoning from illegal gold mining in the Brazilian Amazon
articles.title: Blood Gold: The Munduruku’s fight for survival in the Brazilian Amazon
articles.summary: Indigenous Munduruku families living in the Brazilian Amazon are facing severe health consequences as illegal gold mining operations poison local rivers with mercury. Driven by soaring gold prices, miners have pushed deeper into the rainforest, contaminating the food chain and endangering the fish populations upon which residents rely for their survival according to recent investigative reporting.
articles.description: Fault Lines investigates how illegal gold mining poisons and threatens Indigenous communities in the Brazilian Amazon.

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh seeks central aid for cyclone-damaged horticulture crops
articles.title: Arnab, Murasu cyclones caused ₹1,092 crore loss to horticulture crops in A.P., says Naidu
articles.summary: Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu requested ₹96.33 crore in additional central assistance following cyclones Arnab and Murasu. The storms damaged 29,960 hectares of horticulture crops across 18 districts, impacting over 71,000 farmers. With total losses estimated at ₹1,092 crore, the state seeks support for restoring banana plantations and vegetable crops under various national agricultural schemes.
articles.description: Detailing the crop damaged suffered by over 70,000 farmers in 18 districts of the State, in a letter to Union Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan, Chief Miinister N. Chandrababu Naidu seeks early release of Central aid besides ₹96.33 crore additional assistance for restoration of damaged plantations

articles.headline: Child death in Perumbavoor highlights lack of migrant childcare
articles.title: Death of child in Perumbavoor plywood factory puts spotlight back on lack of childcare for migrant workers in Keralam
articles.summary: A four-year-old migrant boy died after getting caught in a dryer at a Perumbavoor plywood factory on Thursday. The tragedy highlighted severe gaps in childcare facilities for inter-State workers, prompting officials to demand stricter enforcement of mandatory crèche rules by the Factories and Boilers Department. Previous initiatives, including a district-run crèche, have failed due to a lack of sustained support.

articles.headline: Police increase security in Tadipatri following attack on former MLA's home
articles.title: Tension grips Tadipatri as unruly mob attacks former MLA Kethireddy’s house, sets fire to vehicles
articles.summary: Tension escalated in Tadipatri on November 20 after a mob attacked the residence of former YSRCP MLA Kethireddy Peddareddy with petrol bombs and stones. Several vehicles were damaged in the arson incident. Superintendent of Police P. Jagadeesh has deployed additional forces to the town, confirming the situation is now under control and currently peaceful.
articles.description: Unidentified men resort to stone pelting, use petrol bombs; YSRCP points finger of blame at TDP leader J.C. Prabhakar Reddy; police rush to the spot and bring situation under control

articles.headline: Onion prices rise to 70 rupees per kilogram due to drought
articles.title: Drought hits onion production; prices rise to ₹70 per kg
articles.summary: Retail onion prices in Karnataka have climbed to ₹70 per kilogram as drought conditions significantly impact production. The Karnataka State Department of Horticulture reported that over 128,000 hectares of onion crops were lost during the 2026-27 Kharif season. Traders noted that supplies from Vijayapura are currently helping to stabilize prices, which otherwise could have surged higher.

articles.headline: Japan considers lifting United States potato import ban amid trade pressure
articles.title: Hot potato: Can Japan resist Trump pressure to import food staple?
articles.summary: Japanese authorities are evaluating a potential end to a decades-long ban on agricultural imports from the United States under intense pressure from President Donald Trump. While the Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries investigates possible pest and disease risks, local farmers and regional officials have strongly opposed the proposal over fears of crop damage and sales impacts.
articles.description: Japan imports 60 percent of its food, but it fiercely draws the line at potatoes.

articles.headline: United States experiences widespread technology outages affecting banks and government services
articles.title: Outages in US cause worry, despite official attempts to downplay concerns
articles.summary: Recent technology outages across the United States have disrupted operations for major companies and government agencies, including a national aviation ground stop and banking services. While officials attribute the disruptions to individual events and artificial intelligence maintenance updates, experts and former emergency officials warn of potential vulnerabilities and growing cybersecurity threats facing critical national infrastructure.
articles.description: Experts say Trump administration is not taking the threat of AI attacks seriously, as consumers stock up on supplies.

articles.headline: International Court of Justice prepares to rule on Rohingya genocide case
articles.title: ICJ to rule on Rohingya genocide case against Myanmar
articles.summary: The International Court of Justice is scheduled to deliver a final judgment on Thursday at the Peace Palace in The Hague regarding allegations that Myanmar committed genocide against its Rohingya minority. Brought by The Gambia in November 2019, the landmark case stems from a 2017 military offensive that forced hundreds of thousands to flee into Bangladesh.
articles.description: The Gambia accuses Myanmar of genocide following a 2017 military crackdown that displaced at least 730,000 Rohingya.

articles.headline: United Kingdom and European Union strike post-Brexit deal to ease trade restrictions
articles.title: UK says new deal will ‘rebuild bridges’ with EU: What’s in it?
articles.summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham and European Union leaders announced a new agreement aimed at repairing economic ties and easing trade restrictions a decade after Brexit. The package includes measures to reduce paperwork on agricultural products, link emissions-trading systems, and establish a youth mobility programme, though significant disagreements regarding university tuition fees remain unresolved.
articles.description: Agreements aim to simplify trade checks, link emissions systems and launch a youth mobility programme.

articles.headline: Hegseth unveils new US-Venezuela military deal
articles.title: Hegseth unveils new US-Venezuela military deal
articles.description: Pete Hegseth has unveiled a new military deal with Venezuela in his first visit since the US capture of Nicolas Maduro.

articles.headline: Iraqi security forces deploy to Jurf al-Sakhar following Kataib Hezbollah withdrawal deal
articles.title: Iraqi forces deploy to Jurf al-Sakhar after deal with Iran-backed group
articles.summary: Iraqi security forces entered the town of Jurf al-Sakhar in Babil province following a compromise agreement that will see the Iran-aligned Kataib Hezbollah group relocate. The deployment comes after an investigation raised allegations of oil smuggling, prompting a government deadline and subsequent negotiations supported by regional diplomatic efforts to secure oil pipelines and state control.
articles.description: Iraq's Federal Police are due to assume control of town's newly established control headquarters.

articles.headline: Settler rams into Palestinians at multiple locations in central Israel
articles.title: Settler rams into Palestinians at multiple locations in central Israel
articles.description: At least eight Palestinians were injured after a settler driver was caught on camera running them over.

articles.headline: India and Japan sign letter of intent for military firing ranges
articles.title: Why India is opening its military firing ranges to Japan | Explained
articles.summary: India and Japan signed a letter of intent to allow the Japan Self-Defense Forces to use designated firing ranges in India for training exercises. Announced during a bilateral meeting in Tokyo between Defence Minister Rajnath Singh and his Japanese counterpart Shinjiro Koizumi, the framework aims to enhance operational coordination and defense cooperation in the Indo-Pacific region without establishing a permanent military presence.
articles.description: The arrangement does not imply unrestricted access for Japanese forces to Indian military facilities or the establishment of a permanent Japanese military presence in India

articles.headline: Spain face France and England play Norway in Nations League quarterfinals
articles.title: Nations League quarterfinal draw: Spain face France, England play Norway
articles.summary: Following the draw conducted on Friday, the Union of European Football Associations Nations League has scheduled two-legged quarterfinal matches for late March. World champions Spain will compete against France, while England is set to play Norway with the initial match hosted in Norway. Additional pairings feature Portugal challenging the Netherlands and Belgium meeting Germany, with winners progressing to the final stages in June.
articles.description: World Cup winners and European champions Spain have reached three of the four Nations League finals, winning in 2023.

articles.headline: Texas inmate Reinaldo Dennes screams in pain during prolonged lethal injection execution
articles.title: Texas death-row inmate screams as execution takes more than one hour
articles.summary: Reinaldo Dennes, a seventy-year-old Texas death-row inmate, screamed in pain during an execution lasting over an hour on an unspecified date. Witnesses reported difficulties finding veins for the pentobarbital injection, and Dennes shouted that his leg was killing him and the procedure was not working correctly. Dennes was condemned for the 1996 murder of diamond dealer Janos Szucs, while the drug faces renewed scrutiny following previous botched executions.
articles.description: This prolonged execution comes weeks after Christa Pike survived the lethal injection of the same drug.

articles.headline: Pew Research Center projects religious shifts in India and global populations
articles.title: India's religious make-up - what a new Pew study says about Hindus and Muslims
articles.summary: A comprehensive study by the Pew Research Center indicates that India will maintain a Hindu majority through 2070 while experiencing a growing Muslim demographic due to higher fertility rates and younger ages. Globally, Pakistan is projected to surpass Indonesia as the largest Muslim-majority nation. Meanwhile, Christianity's center of gravity is shifting toward sub-Saharan Africa according to the Washington-based research organization.
articles.description: India will remain predominantly Hindu, though its Muslim population is projected to grow faster, according to a new survey.

articles.headline: Botswana-origin cheetah KOMG 3 gives birth to four cubs at Kuno National Park
articles.title: Cheetah brought from Botswana gives birth to four cubs at Kuno
articles.summary: A two-and-a-half-year-old female cheetah brought from Botswana gave birth to four healthy cubs in the wild at Madhya Pradesh's Kuno National Park. Union Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav announced the milestone, marking the first time a Botswana cheetah has reproduced in India. The birth raises India's total cheetah population to 62 under the ongoing reintroduction project.
articles.description: With these four new arrivals, India’s cheetah population has risen to 62, including 43 Indian-born individuals

articles.headline: Indian rupee settles above 93 against US dollar for first time in seven months
articles.title: Rupee settles above 93 level after seven months on FII flows
articles.summary: The Indian rupee appreciated 65 paise to settle at 92.67 against the United States dollar, closing above the 93 threshold for the first time since April 10. Analysts attributed the five-day winning streak to sustained foreign institutional investor capital inflows and a domestic stock market rally, supported by falling global crude oil prices.
articles.description: Forex analysts attributed the rupee's strength to foreign institutional investors' unabated chase for higher returns amid a weaker American currency and waning AI-related stock rallies in the U.S. and markets like Taiwan and South Korea

articles.headline: NHAI deploys artificial intelligence tool to monitor highway damage and contractors
articles.title: NHAI’s AI tool to monitor road damage, follow-up complaints with contractors
articles.summary: The National Highways Authority of India is implementing dashcam analytics systems mounted on patrol vehicles to automatically detect road damage such as potholes and broken signage. Officials at the Indian Roads Congress in Hyderabad explained that the technology captures geotagged photographs and transmits complaints directly to contractors to ensure timely repairs of infrastructure.

articles.headline: Signal blocks screenshots on mobile devices to prevent AI reading data
articles.title: Signal is blocking Gemini and Siri AI from reading your screen
articles.summary: Signal is restricting screenshot capabilities on Android and iOS devices to prevent artificial intelligence agents from reading user messages and personal data. According to Signal president Meredith Whittaker, the integration of operating system-level artificial intelligence tools threatens application privacy because developers lack robust technical tools to restrict data access. The encrypted messaging service is urging major technology companies to provide accurate documentation and simple controls.
articles.description: Signal is restricting the ability to take screenshots on Android and iOS devices in an effort to prevent AI agents from reading users' messages and other data. The agentic AI capabilities built into operating systems that analyze on-screen information to learn more about the user are "undermining Signal's ability to independently guarantee privacy," Signal president […]

articles.headline: Supreme Court dismisses Karnataka appeal against allowing bike-taxis
articles.title: Supreme Court dismisses Karnataka appeal against bike-taxis
articles.summary: The Supreme Court dismissed an appeal by the Karnataka government challenging a High Court decision that permitted bike-taxis as public transport. A Bench led by Justice Satish Chandra Sharma ruled that regulation is preferable to a ban, noting safety benefits and broad usage across 25 States. The State had argued motorcycles lacked proper passenger safety standards.
articles.description: A Bench headed by Justice Satish Chandra Sharma said regulation was better than a blanket ban

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh chief minister declares Kakinada green hydrogen valley
articles.title: Kakinda will be ‘Green Hydrogen Valley of India’, says Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu
articles.summary: Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu declared Kakinada as the green hydrogen valley of India following a bhumi puja for a production complex. Built by AM Green on a 495-acre campus, the facility targets initial production by mid-2027 and will supply green ammonia primarily to Germany. The project contributes to decarbonization targets and supports the state clean energy policy.
articles.description: Green ammonia produced in Kakinada will be supplied mostly to Europe, and Germany is the major importer, says the Chief Minister after laying stone for AM Green’s ₹15,600-crore Green Hydrogen and Green Ammonia Production Complex; first drone ambulance will be deployed this year, he adds

articles.headline: Central Pollution Control Board data reveals winter air quality trends
articles.title: Beyond Delhi’s smog: What does CPCB AQI data say about rest of India?
articles.summary: Central Pollution Control Board data indicates that Delhi and surrounding Indo-Gangetic regions remain among the most polluted areas in India during winter months. However, data comparing winters from 2022 to 2025 shows median air quality index levels increased in industrial towns like Nandesari while improving significantly across several districts in Bihar, according to state pollution control board records released in 2026.

articles.headline: Pennsylvania resident dies from measles during United States outbreak
articles.title: Unvaccinated Pennsylvania resident dies amid historic US measles resurgence
articles.summary: An unvaccinated resident in Clinton County has died from measles, marking the eighth fatality in Pennsylvania this year amid the worst United States outbreak in three decades. The Department of Health confirmed the fatality on Wednesday as the country faces surging infections and the loss of its measles elimination status following thousands of reported cases nationwide.
articles.description: Pennsylvania records eighth measles death of 2026, a day after the US formally loses its 26-year elimination status.

articles.headline: Karnataka High Court rules in favor of bike taxis
articles.title: Karnataka High Court allows bike taxies; asks State government to register two-wheelers as ‘transport vehicles’
articles.summary: The High Court of Karnataka ruled that the state government ban on using two-wheelers as bike taxis contradicts the Motor Vehicles Act. Transport authorities were directed to register two-wheelers as transport vehicles and issue contract carriage permits to operate them legally. The court emphasized that the governing legislation explicitly contemplates the inclusion of two-wheelers within transport vehicle classifications.

articles.headline: European Union governments approve trade agreement with Indonesia to counter tariffs
articles.title: EU governments approve trade deal with Indonesia to offset Trump tariffs
articles.summary: European Union governments approved a trade agreement with Indonesia on Wednesday to offset United States President Donald Trump's tariffs by eliminating import duties on over ninety percent of products. The deal removes Indonesia's fifty percent car duty within five years, saving businesses an estimated 600 million euros annually while connecting the economic bloc with the populous nation.
articles.description: The deal, initially concluded in 2025, will see both sides remove import duties on more than 90 percent of products.

articles.headline: Madras High Court bars Tamil Nadu government from opening new liquor shops
articles.title: Madurai Bench of Madras High Court directs T.N. government not to open any new Tasmac shops
articles.summary: The Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court ordered the Tamil Nadu government not to open any new Tasmac liquor shops across the state. Justices P. Velmurugan and K.K. Ramakrishnan issued the directive while allowing a public interest litigation petition regarding a proposed outlet in Tiruchi district, citing public interest, student safety, and community concerns over existing alcohol availability.
articles.description: A Division Bench said the State already had a large number of Tasmac shops, and considering the public interest, new Tasmac shops should not be opened

articles.headline: India progresses Project Cheetah following initial translocation from Namibia in September 2022
articles.title: Watch | How has ‘Project Cheetah’ progressed in India?
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi released eight cheetahs flown from Windhoek, Namibia, into Kuno National Park in Madhya Pradesh in September 2022 as part of Project Cheetah. The initiative, originally proposed in 2008 and 2009, involves gradual releases from enclosures, radio-collar tracking, and monitoring by wildlife scientists to help the big cats adapt to Indian conditions and prey.
articles.description: A video explainer on 'Project Cheetah', the first intercontinental transfer of wild cats into the country.

articles.headline: India cheetah population reaches 52 as Project Cheetah marks four years
articles.title: As Project Cheetah completes 4 years, big cat population in India rises to 52
articles.summary: India has reached a cheetah population of 52, including 32 cubs born domestically, as Project Cheetah marked four years on September 17, 2026. Officials highlighted the reintroduction success, cub survival, and expansion from Kuno National Park to Gandhi Sagar Sanctuary in Madhya Pradesh. The programme aims to establish a long-term meta population by expanding suitable habitats across multiple regions.
articles.description: The next phase of the cheetah restoration programme involves expanding suitable habitat for cheetahs and establishing a comprehensive, long term cheetah meta population in India.

articles.headline: Indian equity indices close higher as Sensex gains 898 points
articles.title: Stock markets defy global rout; Sensex jumps 898 points, Nifty climbs to 25,800
articles.summary: Indian benchmark equity indices ended sharply higher on November 20, 2026, defying weak global market trends due to bank stock buying, foreign fund inflows, and lower crude prices. The BSE Sensex rose 897.96 points to settle at 83,919.71, while the NSE Nifty surged to 25,800.60. Meanwhile, major Asian and European markets, alongside US indices, recorded significant declines.
articles.description: Rising for the second day, the 30-share BSE Sensex jumped 897.96 points, or 1.08%, to settle at 83,919.71. During the day, it surged 1,016.21 points, or 1.22%, to 84,037.96

articles.headline: NASA space probe Voyager 1 reaches distance of one light-day from Earth
articles.title: NASA’s Voyager 1 hits record one light-day distance, 50 years after launch
articles.summary: NASA spacecraft Voyager 1 has reached a distance of 26 billion kilometres from Earth, marking the first time a human-made object has achieved a distance of one light-day. Launched in 1977, the probe continues to study interstellar space and magnetic fields while operating alongside its twin Voyager 2, which is expected to reach the same milestone in 2035.
articles.description: Voyager 1 reaches one light-day from Earth, marking a historic milestone nearly 50 years after its 1977 launch.

articles.headline: Emmanuel Bacry warns hospitals lack capacity to assess healthcare AI
articles.title: Healthcare AI: hospitals lack capacity to measure real-world patient outcomes, warns French expert
articles.summary: Emmanuel Bacry, Scientific Director of France's Health Data Hub, stated at the Bengaluru Tech Summit that global hospitals cannot adequately measure real-world patient outcomes from artificial intelligence. Speaking on November 20, 2026, he warned that most training data is Western-centric and highlighted the risks of deploying unadapted tools without proper clinical integration protocols.
articles.description: Emmanuel Bacry warns that laboratory accuracy scores do not establish real-world clinical benefits; says healthcare AI trained largely on Western data may not work elsewhere

articles.headline: US administration appoints Kirsten Davies as new cybersecurity chief after outages
articles.title: US appoints new cybersecurity chief after series of tech failures
articles.summary: The White House appointed Department of Defense chief information officer Kirsten Davies as cybersecurity chief on Thursday, replacing Sean Cairncross following widespread technological failures. Recent disruptions grounded US flights, affected Microsoft servers, and impacted JPMorgan Chase transactions. Officials stated the incidents were not cyberattacks but likely stemmed from organizations using artificial intelligence for maintenance updates.
articles.description: Appointee Kirsten Davies says US has the chance to 'dominate the cyber landscape for generations to come'.

articles.headline: US lawmaker suggests India replace Russian military equipment with American systems
articles.title: Replace Russian junk with American weapons system: U.S. lawmaker to India
articles.summary: United States Representative Michael Baumgartner suggested on November 18, 2026, that India should replace its Russian military equipment with American weapons systems and choose Boeing aircraft over Airbus. Speaking at Capitol Hill during Deepavali celebrations hosted by organizations including the BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha, the Republican lawmaker emphasized strengthening economic and security ties between Washington and New Delhi.
articles.description: Michael Baumgartner made the remarks on Capitol Hill in the presence of Namgya Khampa, the Deputy Chief of Mission at the Indian Embassy in Washington

articles.headline: US school districts consider alternatives after Google links search to AI
articles.title: The nation’s largest school districts consider ditching Google Search
articles.summary: Major American educational authorities in New York, Los Angeles, and Chicago are evaluating alternative platforms after Google announced that disabling artificial intelligence features will also remove access to search functions. Elected officials criticized the policy as coercive, while Google stated it plans to adjust default controls and introduce guided learning tools to address feedback from educators across the country.
articles.description: New York, Los Angeles, and Chicago schools are considering Google alternatives after the company said it will disable Search for schools that opt out of its AI features, according to The New York Times. Starting next year, schools will not have the option to disable Gemini-powered features without also disabling Search. Chris Phillips, Google's vice […]

articles.headline: Kataib Hezbollah faces deadline to leave Iraqi stronghold
articles.title: Kataib Hezbollah faces deadline to leave Iraqi stronghold
articles.description: Kataib Hezbollah faces deadline to leave Iraqi stronghold

articles.headline: United States imposes new sanctions on organizations and individuals linked to Hezbollah
articles.title: US steps up pressure on Iran-backed Hezbollah with new sanctions
articles.summary: The United States Treasury Department announced new sanctions targeting the Wa Ta’awanu Association and three individuals based in Lebanon, accusing the charity of serving as a front for Hezbollah. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent stated that the measures are part of an overarching effort to dismantle financial networks supporting Iran and its regional proxies.
articles.description: The US Treasury has accused Hezbollah of using charitable organisations as 'fronts' for fundraising.

articles.headline: Kadapa MP Avinash Reddy convoy attacked in Pulivendula
articles.title: Kadapa MP Avinash Reddy’s convoy attacked in Pulivendula; TDP leader B.Tech Ravi denies role
articles.summary: A vehicle carrying Kadapa MP Y.S. Avinash Reddy was attacked with stones and petrol bombs at Ankalamma Guduru during a convoy trip for panchayat elections. Mr. Avinash accused Telugu Desam Party leader Mareddy Ravindranath Reddy of leading the mob. Mr. Ravi denied the allegations, stating the MP violated the Model Code of Conduct.
articles.description: The MP is detained for a while at the police station for taking out a convoy in violation of the election code

articles.headline: Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh files reply in Delhi court against appeal
articles.title: Appeal against acquittal: Brij Bhushan files reply in Delhi court
articles.summary: Former Wrestling Federation of India chief Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh filed his court reply in New Delhi to an appeal challenging his acquittal in a sexual harassment case. Special Judge Dig Vinay Singh scheduled further arguments by the women wrestlers for November 27 and 28, with Mr. Singh's arguments set for December. The proceedings are in-camera.
articles.description: Noting that the reply had been filed, the court posted the matter for hearing arguments by the wrestlers on November 27 and 28

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister directs officials to list APMDC by 2027
articles.title: Naidu wants APMDC listed on stock market by December 2027
articles.summary: Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu ordered officials to prepare a roadmap to list the Andhra Pradesh Mineral Development Corporation on the stock market by December 2027. Valued at ₹86,290 crore, the corporation will see a new rare earth development subsidiary established, alongside efforts to secure overseas mining assets and domestic coal blocks.
articles.description: Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu approves a separate Andhra Pradesh Rare Earth Development Corporation for strategic minerals

articles.headline: Anthropic shares surge during record Nasdaq market debut
articles.title: Anthropic’s journey from start-up to stock market giant | Infographics
articles.summary: Shares of the artificial intelligence company Anthropic rose 17% during their Nasdaq debut on November 19, 2026. Closing at approximately $97, the company reached a market valuation of $1.75 trillion. Despite a broader market sell-off, the firm successfully raised $81.3 billion through its initial public offering, defying investor concerns regarding recent industry scandals and tech volatility.
articles.description: From its founding in 2021 to a record-breaking Nasdaq debut, tracing Anthropic’s journey into one of the world’s most valuable AI companies

articles.headline: SEBI plans reforms to accelerate foreign portfolio investor onboarding
articles.title: SEBI eyes faster FPI onboarding, plans fresh reforms to attract foreign capital
articles.summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) aims to reduce foreign portfolio investor onboarding time to five days. Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey announced plans for a consultation paper to simplify investment processes and regulatory compliance. Additionally, the regulator is collaborating with the Reserve Bank of India to develop a market-making framework to improve corporate bond liquidity.
articles.description: “By simplifying procedures and reducing avoidable compliance burdens, we aim to attract a wider pool of international capital and improve financing opportunities for Indian businesses while maintaining investor safeguards,” SEBI Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey said

articles.headline: Pakistan defeats Sri Lanka by eight wickets to secure series win
articles.title: PAK vs SL second Test: Pakistan romps to eight-wicket win; first series win in 2 years
articles.summary: Pakistan achieved a historic victory over Sri Lanka on November 20, 2026, winning the second Test by eight wickets at Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium. This triumph sealed a 1-0 series victory, marking Pakistan's first red-ball series win in two years. Aamer Jamal contributed an unbeaten 34 runs after Sri Lanka set a target of 89 runs following their second-innings total of 316.
articles.description: Pakistan raced to 90-2 in 13 overs within first session on Day 4 to win the series 1-0 after Sri Lanka was bowled out for 316 in the second innings, setting up a slender lead of 89 runs

articles.headline: Asian American women face intensified stereotypes following Nvidia CEO scandal
articles.title: Asian American women feel impact of Nvidia CEO affair scandal, 'spy' accusations
articles.summary: Recent allegations involving former Nvidia Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang and a Chinese businesswoman have triggered a resurgence of harmful tropes targeting Asian American women. Professionals in technology and academia report experiencing increased scrutiny and skepticism in workplaces, compounding long-standing historical prejudices and reinforcing detrimental misconceptions regarding competence, leadership, and trustworthiness across the United States.
articles.description: Asian American women working in tech, civil rights advocacy and academia have felt a sense of dread that this ordeal will diminish how their peers are viewed and treated in their workplaces. It’s a reminder that no accomplishments will completely dispel centuries-old stereotypes

articles.headline: Kenyan marathon champion Peres Jepchirchir receives three-year doping ban
articles.title: Kenya’s growing doping crisis overshadows legacy as athletics powerhouse
