articles.summary: Olympic marathon champion Peres Jepchirchir has been suspended for three years after testing positive for the banned blood booster EPO. The Athletics Integrity Unit confirmed the sample was collected before her victory at the Sydney Marathon in August. This case highlights a growing doping crisis in Kenya, where over 140 athletes have faced sanctions since 2017.
articles.description: More than 140 Kenyan athletes suspended by the Athletics Integrity Unit since 2017, most of them distance runners.

articles.headline: Democrats nominate Hakeem Jeffries for US House Speaker
articles.title: Democrats nominate Hakeem Jeffries to be US Speaker of the House
articles.summary: House Democrats in the United States officially nominated Hakeem Jeffries as Speaker on Wednesday, positioning him to become the first black lawmaker to lead the chamber when the new term begins on January 3. Jeffries secured widespread support following a closed-door vote, with Democrats holding at least 257 seats. Despite internal ideological divisions and potential legislative clashes with President Donald Trump, party leaders aim to address key affordability concerns.
articles.description: The nomination sets him on the path to become the first black lawmaker to lead the chamber when Democrats take control of the House in January.

articles.headline: US Defence Secretary Hegseth announces military partnership with Venezuela
articles.title: US Defence Secretary Hegseth reveals military partnership on Venezuela trip
articles.summary: United States Secretary of Defence Pete Hegseth announced a new agreement for military cooperation with interim President Delcy Rodriguez during an unannounced visit to Caracas. The deal includes intelligence sharing and joint training aimed at stabilising the South American nation. The trip follows the January capture of former leader Nicolas Maduro and discussions on energy development and security partnerships.
articles.description: Pete Hegseth says the agreement will include joint training and intelligence sharing with the Venezuelan military.

articles.headline: Supreme Court dismisses public interest litigation on sexual offense complaints
articles.title: SC rejects PIL seeking database of individuals filing ‘repeated’ complaints of sexual offences
articles.summary: The Supreme Court dismissed a public interest litigation filed by Shonee Kapoor seeking a police headquarters database for individuals filing repeated sexual offense complaints. A Bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana ruled that individuals retain the right to lodge complaints, while warning that such records could endanger victim privacy.
articles.description: The Bench expressed reservations about the database, sought in the plea, saying that maintaining such records could pose a serious risk of disclosure of the identities of victims of sexual offences

articles.headline: Yadadri Thermal Power Station ash pollutes Telangana stream
articles.title: Yadadri Thermal Power Plant: The toxic cost of power
articles.summary: Residents of Veerlapalem village in Telangana's Nalgonda district raised concerns over ash slurry pollution in the Thungapahad stream caused by the Yadadri Thermal Power Station. Farmer V. Nageshwar Rao filed a complaint with the Telangana Pollution Control Board in May 2026, prompting a show-cause notice issued to the Telangana Power Generation Corporation Limited the following month.
articles.description: Fly ash from the 4,000-MW Yadadri thermal plant is polluting a stream that sustains farms and fishing communities, before flowing into the Krishna river. As Telangana powers up, the fallout extends beyond the vicinity of the project, which started operations less than two years ago, with concerns rising over water quality, public health and livelihoods along the river system, reports Swathi Vadlamudi

articles.headline: Israeli forces launch ground operation in central Gaza amid ceasefire
articles.title: What does Israel’s new ground offensive mean for Palestinians in Gaza?
articles.summary: Israeli forces launched a ground operation west of the ceasefire line in central Gaza, advancing near Nuseirat and Bureij refugee camps and forcing Palestinian families to flee. The military stated the precise operation aims to eliminate immediate threats and infrastructure belonging to Hamas. Palestinian groups condemned the offensive as a dangerous escalation and a flagrant violation of the 13-month-old agreement.
articles.description: Israeli tanks advance beyond the 'Yellow Line', forcing Palestinians to flee again in Gaza.

articles.headline: US and Venezuela sign agreement to re-establish military ties
articles.title: U.S., Venezuela sign deal to re-establish military ties: Hegseth
articles.summary: Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth announced that the United States and Venezuela signed an agreement to re-establish military ties, encompassing joint training and intelligence sharing. Speaking in Caracas alongside interim President Delcy Rodriguez, Hegseth praised the close cooperation following the January capture of former leader Nicolas Maduro. The visit underscores ongoing efforts by the administration of President Donald Trump to deepen influence in the region.
articles.description: The U.S. Defence Secretary said that following the January capture of Nicolas Maduro by the U.S. military, the country “has gone from our most aggressive regional threat to a compliant security partner”

articles.headline: Muslims projected to overtake Christians as world’s largest religious group
articles.title: Muslims projected to overtake Christians as world’s largest religious group
articles.description: New Pew Research Center projections point to major changes in the world’s religious landscape by 2070.

articles.headline: Supreme Court stresses protection of Central Secretariat Library books
articles.title: Heritage is not just Lutyens, but also books at the 135-year-old Central Secretariat Library, SC tells government
articles.summary: The Supreme Court told the Union government that cultural heritage extends to protecting centuries-old books at the 135-year-old Central Secretariat Library in Shastri Bhawan. Solicitor General Tushar Mehta assured the Bench led by Justice Sanjay Kumar that the government stands by its November 16 undertaking not to shift the books from their current premises during redevelopment.
articles.description: Centre says it values the books as a treasure; the library has tomes dating back to 1702

articles.headline: US loses measles-free status after 26 years in historic setback
articles.title: US loses measles-free status after 26 years in historic setback
articles.description: The US has lost its measles elimination status after 26 years, as its largest outbreak in over three decades continues.

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh faces severe coastal erosion along thirty-one percent of shorelines
articles.title: How ports and cyclones are eating away the beaches of Visakhapatnam
articles.summary: Satellite mapping by the National Centre for Coastal Research under the Union Ministry of Earth Sciences revealed that nearly thirty-one percent of Andhra Pradesh's coastline is eroding. Published in February 2024, the Shoreline Change Atlas indicated severe losses concentrated in delta districts like Kakinada and West Godavari, while local experts noted direct wave impacts along Visakhapatnam roads.
articles.description: Nearly 31% (318.96 km) of Andhra Pradesh’s coastline is eroding, with about 91.6 km falling into the ‘high erosion’ category. While the losses are concentrated in the delta districts of Kakinada, West Godavari, and Krishna, the coastal port district of Visakhapatnam is also facing the issue. Paul Nicodemus explores how decades of port development, changing wave patterns, and cyclones have contributed to the erosion of the City of Destiny’s beaches

articles.headline: Rahul Gandhi criticizes Prime Minister following trilateral meeting in Shenzhen
articles.title: Trump-Xi-Putin trilateral: Compromised PM can never sit at this table, says Rahul Gandhi
articles.summary: Former Indian National Congress chief Rahul Gandhi stated that a compromised leader could not participate in high-level international diplomacy, referencing a trilateral meeting involving United States President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping, and Russian President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen. The three leaders agreed on November 19, 2026, to pursue United Nations reforms, increase oil supplies, and address nuclear risks.
articles.description: Rahul Gandhi calls India a “side player” in the Iran war, expresses surprise over Pakistan’s role in negotiator

articles.headline: US panel says India targets minorities in voter roll revisions
articles.title: U.S. religious freedom panel says ‘India targeting minorities in voter roll revisions’
articles.summary: India escalated the targeting of religious minorities during a voter list revision that removed 130 million names nationwide, according to the United States Commission on International Religious Freedom. Panel chair Asif Mahmood stated on November 19, 2026, that Muslim citizens are disproportionately affected by the deletions. The Election Commission of India maintained it was removing ineligible voters, while the Ministry of External Affairs dismissed the USCIRF criticism as biased.
articles.description: USCIRF is a bipartisan body of ⁠the U.S. government that monitors religious freedom around the world and makes policy recommendations, which are not binding

articles.headline: Resident doctors in Srinagar launch indefinite strike over stipends
articles.title: Resident doctors at Government Medical College in Srinagar go on indefinite strike
articles.summary: Postgraduate and senior resident doctors at Government Medical College in Srinagar began an indefinite strike on November 20, 2026. The All India Medical Students Association urged the government to implement immediate stipend enhancements, parity with other regions, and maternity leave benefits. Protesters also called for Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha to intervene and facilitate a recognised resident doctors association.
articles.description: AIMSA's key demands include immediate stipend enhancement and parity for postgraduate, senior resident, DNB and MDS doctors across Jammu and Kashmir, besides implementation of maternity leave benefits in accordance with applicable high court directions

articles.headline: Union Petroleum Minister Hardeep Singh Puri meets petrol pump dealers on margins
articles.title: Petrol Pump dealers say govt assured looking into dealer margin hike after meeting with OilMin
articles.summary: Union Petroleum Minister Hardeep Singh Puri held discussions with petrol pump dealers in New Delhi regarding dealer margins and non-fuel revenue streams. Representatives noted that previous lockdowns created financial burdens. The Ministry indicated that any commission revisions will be handled in consultation with oil-marketing companies to support distributors facing ongoing global economic disruptions.
articles.description: In response to a query from The Hindu, Oil Minister Hardeep Puri had mentioned that LPG distributors and petrol pump operators were an important part of India’s response to global turmoil from the last four years.

articles.headline: Keralam home minister urges Centre to amend juvenile justice laws
articles.title: Keralam urges Centre to amend Juvenile Justice Act amid rise in violent offences by minors
articles.summary: Keralam Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala petitioned Union Ministers Amit Shah and Annpurna Devi to amend the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015, citing a rise in violent youth offences. Mr Chennithala stated the law is insensitive to crime victims, attributing the surge to digital media and substance abuse. The Kerala High Court earlier suggested lowering the age threshold from 18 to 16 years.
articles.description: In letters to Union Minister for Home Affairs Amit Shah and Union Minister for Women and Child Development Annpurna Devi, Ramesh Chennithala states existing legislation fails to adequately address plight of crime victims

articles.headline: Muslim population projected to surpass Christians globally by 2035
articles.title: Islam set to be the largest religion by 2035: Where will most Muslims live?
articles.summary: Muslims are projected to outnumber Christians globally by 2035, driven by higher fertility rates according to Pew Research Center data. Between 2020 and 2070, the global Muslim population is expected to rise by 80 percent to 3.64 billion. Pakistan is projected to overtake Indonesia with the largest Muslim population, while India and Nigeria will also see significant growth.
articles.description: Pew Research projects Muslim population in Pakistan will overtake Indonesia by 2070, with India next and Nigeria third.

articles.headline: Enforcement Directorate summons Rajya Sabha member Satnam Singh Sandhu
articles.title: Enforcement Directorate summons RS MP Sandhu
articles.summary: The Enforcement Directorate summoned nominated Rajya Sabha member Satnam Singh Sandhu for questioning on November 25, 2026, regarding a multi-crore fraud probe involving Vuenow. Officials stated entities linked to Mr Sandhu received funds from the group, though he has no direct role in the case. The agency previously arrested three individuals, including Vuenow CEO Sukhwinder Singh Kharour.
articles.description: According to officials, Mr. Sandhu has been summoned to verify the nature and purpose of these transactions and does not have a direct role in the case

articles.headline: Indian foreign secretary meets Nepal prime minister in Kathmandu
articles.title: Foreign Secretary Misri sets stage for Nepal PM’s upcoming India visit
articles.summary: Indian Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri met Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah in Kathmandu on November 5, 2026, to discuss initiatives ahead of the Nepali leader's upcoming visit to New Delhi. Mr Misri also held talks with Nepali foreign and finance ministers regarding bilateral cooperation, hydropower, and border management. Nepali leaders thanked India for humanitarian aid following the Bhotekoshi floods.
articles.description: The Nepali leaders expressed “gratitude for India’s swift and substantial humanitarian and technical assistance in the aftermath of the Bhotekoshi floods”, a joint press release stated

articles.headline: US pursues AI hub project in the Philippines amid local protests
articles.title: Trump’s latest land grab is an AI hub in the Philippines
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump is advancing plans to develop a 1,620-hectare industrial hub for semiconductor manufacturing and data centers in the Philippines. While government officials anticipate economic growth, human rights advocates and Indigenous residents are protesting the project due to anticipated land displacement and environmental concerns. Officials from both nations aim to sign a framework agreement soon.
articles.description: President Donald Trump was greeted by no less than five beauty queens when he landed in the Philippines on Tuesday, according to local news outlet Rappler. As he stepped onto the tarmac, a child handed him small US and Philippine flags. A band played "YMCA," a staple at Trump rallies, as more girls in traditional […]

articles.headline: Report highlights funding gaps in India's corporate social responsibility spending
articles.title: India’s CSR spending leaves gaps in health, water security, innovation: Report
articles.summary: An analysis by Sattva Consulting and India Data Insights revealed that India's corporate social responsibility funding concentrates heavily on education and healthcare, creating critical gaps in areas like non-communicable diseases, groundwater resilience, and innovation. Annual corporate spending reached 40,794 crore rupees in the 2025 financial year, though experts urge better allocation toward underfunded developmental challenges.
articles.description: Non-communicable diseases (NCDs), for instance, account for 60% of deaths in India, up from 45% in 2004-06. Yet, nearly 62% of identifiable NCD funding goes towards cancer, while cardiovascular diseases receive around 12%, despite accounting for over half of NCD deaths, says a study by a City-based global impact consulting firm

articles.headline: Four killed as Russian strikes hit Ukraine’s Odesa
articles.title: Four killed as Russian strikes hit Ukraine’s Odesa
articles.description: At least four people have been killed and thirteen more injured after Russian strikes hit Ukraine’s port city of Odesa.

articles.headline: Nvidia maintains financial momentum following leadership transition
articles.title: Nvidia’s rise, visualized
articles.summary: Nvidia reported record financial results and projected 130 billion dollars in revenue for the upcoming quarter during an earnings call led by interim Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress. Following the resignation of co-founder Jensen Huang, company executives stated that business operations will remain unchanged and that all excess free cash flow will be returned to shareholders.
articles.description: If someone handed you $8,300 every second, what would you do? That's how much pure profit Nvidia now makes. By the time you finish reading this paragraph, Nvidia will likely have cleared $45,000 and change. It's easy to look at Nvidia, a company that just lost its visionary founder CEO due to a series of […]

articles.headline: Bengaluru captures nearly half of national venture funding according to report
articles.title: Bengaluru is India’s AI, start-up capital; city captures 47% of national venture funding: Report
articles.summary: Bengaluru has captured 47% of all venture funding raised by Indian start-ups since 2010, totaling roughly $85 billion, according to the Bengaluru Innovation Report 2026. Released on November 18, 2026, by Karnataka Minister Priyank M. Kharge, the report highlights the city as a major deep-tech and artificial intelligence hub, housing 57 unicorns valued at $211 billion and leading the nation with 212 soonicorns.
articles.description: The city is now the world’s fifth-largest unicorn hub, the largest outside the U.S., Europe, China, and London,with 57 unicorns valued at $211 billion, representing 55.3% of the combined value of all Indian unicorns

articles.headline: U.S. deportees face abuse and extortion by guards in South Sudan
articles.title: U.S. deportees in South Sudan went hungry as guards pocketed money from relatives, families say
articles.summary: Migrants deported by the United States to South Sudan have endured severe deprivation and extortion by guards who pocketed thousands of dollars sent by detainees families, according to relatives and lawyers. While the South Sudan Foreign Ministry denied the allegations, deportees described living in squalor and facing violence, highlighting the consequences of U.S. immigration policies involving countries struggling with poverty and corruption.
articles.description: Guards have solicited and received thousands of dollars from detainees' families, who were told the money would be used to improve conditions for their loved ones

articles.headline: Israeli settler kills Palestinian grandmother in occupied West Bank
articles.title: Israeli settler kills Palestinian grandmother in occupied West Bank
articles.description: A Palestinian grandmother was killed by an Israeli settler in the occupied West Bank.

articles.headline: Lawmakers push for legal protections against online harms before year end
articles.title: Tech lawsuits defined 2026 — and lawmakers want more
articles.summary: U.S. lawmakers are pressing for legislation to allow public lawsuits against deepfake creators and platforms enforcing forced arbitration. During a Senate Judiciary subcommittee hearing on November 17, 2026, legislators targeted Roblox over forced arbitration clauses for minors, while advocates like Paris Hilton championed the Defiance Act to enable victims of nonconsensual intimate deepfakes to sue creators for damages.
articles.description: With just a few weeks remaining, lawmakers are trying to pass new protections for victims of online harm before the end of 2026, targeting deepfake creators and online platforms that block users from filing lawsuits. On Tuesday, members of a Senate Judiciary subcommittee hosted a hearing calling for the end of forced arbitration for online […]

articles.headline: Defending champion D. Gukesh faces Javokhir Sindarov in Geneva
articles.title: World Chess Championship: Gukesh faces stern test against in-form Sindarov
articles.summary: Defending champion D. Gukesh will compete against Uzbek grandmaster Javokhir Sindarov in the Salesforce FIDE World Chess Championship starting November 24, 2026, in Geneva. Gukesh enters ranked 26th with a rating of 2710, while Sindarov holds the fourth spot with 2782 points. The 14-game classical match features a USD 2.5 million prize fund and strict rules prohibiting quick draws before 40 moves.
articles.description: While Gukesh secured his place in the title contest by defeating China's Ding Liren in the 2024 World Championship match, Sindarov has arrived after an impressive run that included victories in the World Cup and the Candidates tournament

articles.headline: US Senate approves bipartisan bill accelerating energy infrastructure reviews
articles.title: U.S. Senate approves bill to speed up permitting reviews, Democrats and environmental groups oppose
articles.summary: The United States Senate voted sixty-two to thirty-three on Thursday to approve legislation streamlining environmental reviews for energy projects. Aimed at lowering electricity prices and boosting supplies, the measure faced criticism from Democrats and environmental groups over weakened safeguards. Fifteen Democrats supported the bill, which now advances to the House of Representatives following midterm elections.
articles.description: The legislation’s sweeping changes would shorten the timeline to start big energy projects and make sure data centres pay for the energy they use

articles.headline: Nigerian President Bola Tinubu proposes decriminalising attempted suicide
articles.title: Nigeria moves to end jail terms for attempted suicide
articles.summary: Nigerian President Bola Tinubu has asked parliament to replace criminal penalties for attempted suicide with medical treatment, rehabilitation, and support services. The proposal follows years of advocacy from mental health professionals who argued that prosecuting survivors discourages individuals from seeking help, while Senate President Godswill Akpabio referred the amendment bill to a senate committee for further consideration.
articles.description: Nigeria's proposed reform follows years of calls from psychiatrists and a parallel Senate bill.

articles.headline: Migrant child struggles to belong in Keralam school
articles.title: Beyond admission: The struggle to belong for migrant children in Keralam
articles.summary: Arunima Mandal moved to Keralam from Jharkhand to join her father, who sought a better education for his children. A private aided school initially refused her admission before accepting her on the condition that she repeat Class nine. Balancing household chores and isolated by her circumstances, she navigates the challenges of adjusting to her new academic environment.
articles.description: Migrant children confront admission barriers, language shocks, and social stigma despite State-led schemes in Keralam. Initiatives such as Project Roshni aim to integrate migrant students even without full documents, but many face hunger, isolation, and cultural distances that extend beyond language

articles.headline: Young Germans protest military registration and conscription plans
articles.title: ‘We don’t want our future decided by the military’: Young Germans protest
articles.summary: High school student Phil Werring received a compulsory military registration letter from the Bundeswehr in Berlin, facing fines for non-compliance. Conscription returned under the Military Service Modernisation Act passed in January, raising army expansion targets. Thousands of students planned nationwide protests organized by Gen Z Regelt on Friday, voicing anger over militarization and deteriorating school facilities.
articles.description: Ahead of Friday's nationwide rallies, German teenagers explain why they are resisting conscription.

articles.headline: Israeli forces launch new military operation in central Gaza
articles.title: Israeli forces launch new military operation in central Gaza
articles.description: Israeli forces have launched a new military operation in central Gaza, advancing west of the Yellow Line

articles.headline: Experts analyze potential global economic impacts of artificial intelligence
articles.title: How AI could reshape global growth and productivity
articles.summary: Researchers are examining the potential economic impacts of artificial intelligence, drawing comparisons to historical industrial inventions like the steam engine. A primary focus of this analysis is the anticipated increase in labour productivity. Economists evaluate this through the ratio of economic output to workers employed, which can shift via output growth or employment changes.
articles.description: A key expected impact of AI is an unprecedented rise in labour productivity, as its success as a technological revolution is premised on such an increase; what remains to be seen is how pervasive its impact will be across different sectors of the economy

articles.headline: US maritime agency warned Iran blockade inflated shipping costs
articles.title: US maritime agency warned Iran blockade was adding to rising Gulf premiums
articles.summary: An internal United States Maritime Administration memo revealed concerns that Washington's blockade of Iran increased commercial shipping risks and insurance premiums. Released through a Freedom of Information Act request, the document followed Central Command attacks on vessels in the Strait of Hormuz. War-risk insurance costs surged drastically amid mounting regional conflicts that have disrupted global supply chains since February.
articles.description: US Maritime Administration acknowledged naval blockade's impact on insurance premiums and cargo capacity, memo shows.

articles.headline: Spacecraft BepiColombo approaches final orbit around Mercury after eight-year journey
articles.title: Mysterious Mercury is about to get a visitor - after spacecraft's eight-year epic voyage
articles.summary: The BepiColombo spacecraft, a joint mission by the European Space Agency and the Japanese Space Agency launched in 2018 from French Guiana, is preparing to enter Mercury's orbit after travelling nearly six billion miles. The mission aims to study the planet's extreme temperatures, ice in craters, and mysterious hollows. Once arrived, the two onboard spacecraft will separate to examine the harsh and little-explored inner Solar System planet closely.
articles.description: The mission is set to give us our best ever view of Mercury - the closest planet to the Sun.

articles.headline: Karnataka government restructures Bengaluru City Police into five new commissionerates
articles.title: Bengaluru City Police restructured; five Commissioners and a Chief Commissioner appointed
articles.summary: The Karnataka government restructured the Bengaluru City Police by establishing five independent commissionerates led by inspector-general rank officers and appointing a Chief Commissioner to oversee operations. Additional Director-General of Police R. Hithendra took charge as Chief Commissioner. The administrative overhaul aims to improve law enforcement supervision across the expanding metropolitan jurisdiction.
articles.description: R. Hithendra appointed the new Chief Commissioner of Bengaluru City Police

articles.headline: Militant killed and others apprehended during search operations in Manipur
articles.title: Militant killed in encounter with security forces in Manipur
articles.summary: Security forces killed one militant and apprehended several others belonging to a banned faction during a search operation in the Yurembam area of Imphal West district on November 20, 2026, according to officials. The region has experienced ongoing ethnic conflict between Meitei and Kuki communities since May 2023, resulting in hundreds of fatalities, missing persons, and widespread displacement across local districts.
articles.description: "During the gunfight, a militant belonging to a faction of the proscribed Kangleipak Communist Party was killed," says official

articles.headline: Donald Trump's Board of Peace warns Gaza ceasefire risks collapse
articles.title: What has happened to the $18bn pledged to Trump’s Board of Peace for Gaza?
articles.summary: Donors have pledged eighteen billion dollars through United States President Donald Trump's Board of Peace, but reconstruction in Gaza has not begun and nearly one point four million Palestinians remain in makeshift shelters. According to a report submitted on Tuesday, the board warned the truce could collapse unless immediate steps are taken to carry out the ceasefire deal.
articles.description: Billions have been pledged for Gaza since a 2025 'ceasefire', but rebuilding hasn’t begun and Israeli attacks continue.

articles.headline: Bangladesh deploys paramilitary forces nationwide amid violence over former leader's return
articles.title: Bangladesh deploys paramilitary as unrest grows over Hasina's return
articles.summary: Bangladesh authorities deployed paramilitary troops nationwide following protests, bomb blasts, and arson attacks linked to the planned return of exiled former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina. Clashes between security forces and supporters of the banned Awami League resulted in multiple deaths and widespread property damage across several districts, prompting mass arrests by metropolitan police forces.
articles.description: Police have recorded dozens of crude bomb blasts and incidents of vehicles ​being torched in at least ‌28 districts over the last 10 days, with several police personnel and civilians injured, local media has reported

articles.headline: Ethiopia and Eritrea amass military forces along shared border
articles.title: Ethiopia, Eritrea amass forces along border, heightening war fears: Sources
articles.summary: Conflict monitors report that Ethiopia and Eritrea have deployed troops along their border, raising concerns of a new war. The Armed Conflict Location and Event Data Project (ACLED) noted clashes near Badme since November 12, 2026. While Eritrea denied incursions, the build-up follows deteriorating relations between the two nations since their 2018 peace agreement.
articles.description: The fighting in Tigray has stoked fears of a ​wider conflagration in the Horn of Africa, with Ethiopia’s government also accusing Sudan, which is in the midst of its own civil war, and Egypt of backing the rebels; Eritrea, Sudan, Egypt ⁠all deny doing so

articles.headline: Board of Peace faults Israel and Hamas over Gaza
articles.title: Trump's Board of Peace faults Israel, Hamas for failure to end Gaza war
articles.summary: The oversight body for United States President Donald Trump's Gaza peace plan accused both Israel and Hamas of failing to meet ceasefire commitments in a report released on November 18, 2026. The document warns that stalled progress leaves residents in dire conditions. While Israel cited ongoing security demands, Hamas dismissed the findings as disinformation amidst continued military actions and worsening winter weather conditions across the territory.
articles.description: While the ceasefire has halted major fighting, the wider plan, which calls for Hamas ⁠to disarm, Israeli troops to withdraw and reconstruction to begin, has effectively stalled since soon after it came into effect last year

articles.headline: Democrats nominate Hakeem Jeffries for next U.S. House speaker
articles.title: Democrats nominate Hakeem Jeffries for next U.S. House speaker
articles.summary: House Democrats nominated Hakeem Jeffries on November 18, 2026, to lead them in the upcoming Congress. Jeffries secured 251 votes despite opposition from eleven members, including a group of progressives seeking policy commitments. He is expected to become the first Black House speaker when the new Congress convenes in January, succeeding current Republican leadership.
articles.description: Despite some opposition, Jeffries is expected to be elected speaker, a powerful position that puts him second in line to the Presidency, when the new Congress ‌convenes in early January

articles.headline: European Union urges developing nations to deploy existing climate funds rather than increase targets
articles.title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged
articles.summary: Vulnerable African nations like Uganda and Malawi face severe droughts and floods but struggle to secure funding because they have not submitted National Adaptation Plans. At the COP31 summit in Turkey, the African Group of Negotiators pushed to triple adaptation finance, but European Union officials argued the priority must be deploying already committed funds effectively. Developing countries globally require billions annually, yet current support falls significantly short of these rising climate needs.
articles.description: African countries at the UN climate summit in Turkey are demanding more funding from developed nations to help them cope with climate change.

articles.headline: Contaminated petrol damages vehicles and deepens financial struggles in Yemen
articles.title: Contaminated petrol leaves Yemeni drivers struggling to make ends meet
articles.summary: Drivers in Sanaa face mounting vehicle repairs and rising fuel prices due to contaminated petrol circulating through local markets. While the Sanaa-based Yemen Petroleum Company attributed the issue to damaged storage facilities from airstrikes, critics and analysts cite import restrictions forcing reliance on substandard fuel. The crisis exacerbates economic hardships amid a decade-long conflict.
articles.description: Drivers in Houthi-controlled areas face rising fuel prices and costly repairs as contaminated petrol damages their cars.

articles.headline: Boston University researchers develop non-verbal video game to study perception in autistic adolescents
articles.title: How do autistic people parse information? A video game can help say
articles.summary: Investigators at Boston University adapted a rodent sensory test into an online video game to assess perception among autistic adolescents without requiring verbal communication. Published on November 19, 2026, the remote tool bypasses language barriers and regional translation needs, potentially expanding clinical research access for participants residing outside major metropolitan specialist centres.
articles.description: Researchers have developed a non-verbal online game that adolescents across the autism spectrum can learn and play; it holds special promise for India by bypassing the need to translate complex clinical instructions into regional languages and allowing clinicians to reach autistic individuals far beyond the major metros

articles.headline: India crude oil import bill rises to 19.5 billion dollars
articles.title: India’s Oct. crude import bill soars 87.5% to $19.5-bn amid West Asia tensions, volumes up 11%
articles.summary: India's crude oil import bill increased 87.5 percent to 19.5 billion dollars in October 2026, driven by higher international prices and an 11 percent rise in volume. According to the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell, geopolitical tensions in West Asia inflated costs. Increased petroleum product export revenues provided a partial buffer against the rising expenditure.
articles.description: While higher petroleum product exports offer a partial natural hedge, sustained increases in crude and gas prices could intensify pressure on the country’s import bill.

articles.headline: Gem and jewellery council urges vigilance over gold scam
articles.title: Jewellers’ body GJC calls for vigilance as an alleged ‘gold scam’ surfaces
articles.summary: The All India Gem and Jewellery Domestic Council has advised industry members and buyers to maintain caution without panicking following reports that Rhenium and Iridium-based alloys are being used to fraudulently increase gold weight. Council Chairman Rajesh Rokde stated that the Bureau of Indian Standards is treating the matter seriously, while urging jewellers to strengthen quality checks and consumers to verify hallmark details using the official BIS Care App.
articles.description: This comes amid recent media reports regarding certain materials, commonly referred to as Rhenium and Iridium-based alloys, allegedly being used by scamsters to increase the weight of gold without a proportional increase in purity

articles.headline: Security officer pushing minister in Bihar sparks political controversy
articles.title: Video of Bihar CM’s security ‘pushing’ Nishant sparks row
articles.summary: A political dispute emerged in Bihar on Thursday following a viral video from Vaishali district showing a security officer purportedly pushing State Health Minister Nishant Kumar. The incident occurred during an inspection for an upcoming prime ministerial visit. While the opposition blamed the ruling National Democratic Alliance, the Special Security Group attributed the occurrence to human error.
articles.description: Alliance partner Janata Dal (United) objected strongly, saying the Assembly mandate was in Nitish Kumar’s name. The party demanded action, calling it an insult to Nishant and all its workers

articles.headline: Canada’s PM calls out ‘lying’ Putin for downplaying sanctions
articles.title: Canada’s PM calls out ‘lying’ Putin for downplaying sanctions
articles.description: Carney accuses Putin of ‘lying’ after the Russian leader dismissed Western sanctions as a ‘thing of the past’.

articles.headline: Government extends validity of pollution certificates for newer vehicles
articles.title: Why has the Centre extended PUCC validity to three years for newer vehicles?
articles.summary: The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways has modified regulations surrounding Pollution Under Control Certificates by connecting mandatory emission testing frequency directly to vehicle age and emission standards. Under the revised norms, specific newer Bharat Stage VI vehicles are granted a certificate validity of up to three years, thereby reducing the regular frequency of required vehicle pollution checks across the country.
articles.description: Amendments to sub-rule (7) of Rule 115 of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989, were notified on November 13, 2026, and came into effect from the date of notification

articles.headline: Justice Yashwant Varma argues removal proceedings are infructuous after resignation
articles.title: Removal proceedings against me infructuous after resignation: Justice Varma tells Lok Sabha Secretariat
articles.summary: Justice Yashwant Varma stated in a September 10 letter to Lok Sabha Secretary General Utpal Kumar Singh that his removal proceedings became infructuous following his resignation. Responding to an inquiry committee report that found three corruption-related charges against him proven, Mr. Varma maintained his innocence and asserted that his resignation does not admit any allegations.
articles.description: In a letter circulated among MPs on November 19, Justice Varma stated that the proceedings directed toward his removal did not survive his resignation

articles.headline: Canada’s beloved Tim Hortons brews ire over ‘excessive’ Israeli data deal
articles.title: Canada’s beloved Tim Hortons brews ire over ‘excessive’ Israeli data deal
articles.description: Advocates raised concerns about the Tim Horton’s app and consumer privacy and data-sharing.

articles.headline: FlightGlobal reduces active Rafale count in Indian Air Force inventory
articles.title: IAF’s ‘active Rafale count cut to 32’ by FlightGlobal; Defence Ministry disputes claim
articles.summary: British aviation publication FlightGlobal lowered the number of active Rafale fighter jets in the Indian Air Force inventory from 35 to 32 in its World Air Forces directory. Ministry of Defence officials disputed the assessment, stating the data did not originate from the Indian military. India previously procured 36 Rafale fighters from France and recently issued a tender seeking support for the entire fleet.
articles.description: 36 Rafale fighters were purchased from France; FlightGlobal in late 2025 listed 35 aircraft as active, while the latest edition has reduced the number to 32

articles.headline: Viswanathan Anand advises D. Gukesh to enjoy chess before world title defence
articles.title: World Chess Championship: Worry less, enjoy chess more, Anand’s message to Gukesh
articles.summary: Former world chess champion Viswanathan Anand advised Indian player D. Gukesh to relax and enjoy the game ahead of his title defence against Uzbek challenger Javokhir Sindarov in Geneva. Gukesh experienced a dip in form and ranking following a series of disappointing tournament results. Anand also noted that compatriot R. Vaishali will gain confidence from her recent performances ahead of her upcoming championship match.
articles.description: At 20, Gukesh and Sindarov are the youngest participants in a world championship match in chess history

articles.headline: Chipmakers report strong demand despite frontier AI training pauses
articles.title: Remember the frontier AI pause? Chip companies don’t either
articles.summary: Nvidia and AMD reported record quarterly revenue, showing that brief pauses in frontier AI model training have not dampened demand for computing hardware. Nvidia's data center revenue rose 110 percent to 107.6 billion dollars, while AMD saw data center sales nearly double. Experts suggest that growing demand for AI inference is sustaining the chip market.
articles.description: This summer, OpenAI paused its largest planned frontier training run after its AI agents accidentally hacked Hugging Face and early evidence suggested that its next model could independently find and exploit security flaws. In September, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for slowing advances in the most powerful AI models, warning that they could be used […]

articles.headline: EU Copernicus reports high carbon emissions from Indonesian fires in 2026
articles.title: Indonesian fire emissions third highest on record this year, says EU’s Copernicus
articles.summary: Wildfires in Indonesia generated nearly 200 million metric tonnes of carbon emissions by November 15, 2026, according to the European Union Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service. The figure represents the third-highest annual volume on record, driven by dry El Niño conditions and land clearing. The fires damaged an estimated 8.9 million hectares of land across the Southeast Asian archipelago during the season.
articles.description: This year’s fires in Indonesia produced nearly 200 million metric tonnes of carbon emissions ​by November 15, the European Union’s climate monitoring service ‌said

articles.headline: Colombian citizens protest tax reforms amid debates on US military cooperation
articles.title: Thousands protest Colombia’s tax plans amid row over US military role
articles.summary: Thousands of Colombians protested in Bogota and other cities against proposed tax reforms and rising living costs under President Abelardo de la Espriella. Demonstrators opposed plans to lower the income tax threshold and increase healthcare contributions. Meanwhile, the government denied rejecting a proposal for joint military operations with the United States following discussions with United States Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.
articles.description: Trade unions, students and opposition groups demonstrated in Bogota and other major cities on Thursday.

articles.headline: Brazilian president visits ailing Amazon leader Raoni as government recognizes ancestral land
articles.title: Lula visits ailing Chief Raoni as Brazil recognises Indigenous land
articles.summary: Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva traveled to Peixoto de Azevedo to meet the ninety-four-year-old Indigenous defender who is receiving palliative care. During the visit, the Ministry of Justice declared the Kapot Nhinore Indigenous Territory as permanent possession for the Mebengokre and Yudja peoples. The newly recognized region covers approximately three hundred sixty-two thousand hectares and faces opposition from rural producers.
articles.description: Lula honours Raoni in Mato Grosso, celebrating his legacy and advancing protection for Kayapo and Yudja ancestral lands.

articles.headline: US Navy official claims single transit insurance in Strait of Hormuz costs $64m
articles.title: US official says Hormuz insurance hits $64m: Is the strait really open?
articles.summary: Acting United States Navy Secretary Hung Cao stated during a Senate Armed Services Committee hearing on Tuesday that war-risk insurance for commercial ships crossing the Strait of Hormuz has reached $64m per transit. The claim remains unverified and contrasts with lower estimates from maritime analysts, as traffic through the vital energy route stays heavily reduced following military strikes by the United States and Israel on Iran.
articles.description: Hung Cao says shipping insurance costs have soared to $64m for a single transit, challenging claims the strait is open.

articles.headline: Israeli forces kill three Palestinians during military operation in central Gaza
articles.title: Three killed as Israel launches first ground push since ‘ceasefire’ began
articles.summary: Israeli military forces launched a new operation in central Gaza on Wednesday, killing three Palestinians according to hospital officials. Al Jazeera correspondents reported tanks operating near Salah al-Din Street and an air strike targeting al-Mughraqa. Hamas condemned the action as a flagrant violation of the ceasefire, while the Israeli army stated the operation aimed to eliminate threats near the Yellow Line.
articles.description: Many Palestinians started to flee refugee camps as the Israeli offensive got underway.

articles.headline: Srikakulam records heavy rainfall as Cyclonic Storm Akvan approaches
articles.title: Very heavy rain lashes Srikakulam as Akvan moves closer to coast
articles.summary: Sixteen weather stations in Srikakulam district recorded over 100 millimetres of rainfall between November 19 and 20, 2026, as Cyclonic Storm Akvan approached the North Andhra-South Odisha coast. The India Meteorological Department reported that Ichchapuram mandal received 153.25 millimetres. Gale winds reached 100 kilometres per hour near the center as the landfall process began near Gopalpur.
articles.description: The major rainfall activity has been concentrated in the district of Srikakulam alone, while a few stations in Vizianagaram, Anakapalli, Kakinada, Visakhapatnam, have recorded light showers

articles.headline: Iranian forces target military bases in Bahrain and Kuwait amid regional tensions
articles.title: ‘Status quo’ between US and Iran could break out into war, analysts warn
articles.summary: Iranian forces targeted military bases in Bahrain and Kuwait after United States strikes hit southern Iran following shipping attacks in the Strait of Hormuz. Analysts warned the unstable situation could escalate into full-scale war. Tehran demanded the US lift its naval blockade, while mediators attempted to bridge gaps amid an ongoing impasse over economic sanctions and regional security.
articles.description: Iran and the US have continued to exchange strikes in recent days, but all-out war has so far been avoided.

articles.headline: Rahul Gandhi criticizes Indian economy during speech at Columbia University
articles.title: India sitting on 'economic disaster': Rahul Gandhi at Columbia University
articles.summary: Addressing students and faculty at Columbia University in New York on November 17, 2026, Indian opposition politician Rahul Gandhi warned that the nation faces a severe economic crisis characterized by widespread unemployment, a failing education sector, and a damaged manufacturing foundation. The Congress party leader argued that small businesses and agriculture are vital for job creation, while alleging that current private investment is overly concentrated among a select few corporate groups.
articles.description: At Columbia University, Congress leader questions fairness of electoral process, speaks on manufacturing decline; links U.S. midterm setback to erosion of American power

articles.headline: Madhya Pradesh scraps two-child policy for government employees
articles.title: Madhya Pradesh scraps two-child policy for Govt employees after 25 years
articles.summary: The Madhya Pradesh Cabinet approved scrapping the twenty-five-year-old two-child restriction policy for government employees and job applicants, citing declining fertility rates. Chief Minister Mohan Yadav announced the decision on November 18, 2026, at a meeting in Mandsaur district. Officials stated the rule caused difficulties and that ongoing disciplinary proceedings regarding child counts will terminate immediately, aligning with broader demographic debates on falling birth rates.
articles.description: The policy had been introduced in 2001 by the Congress government led by the then Chief Minister Digvijaya Singh as measure to check population rise

articles.headline: Law firm Kirkland and Ellis gave millions in free services
articles.title: Democrats say law firm gave $11.8m in free services to Trump administration
articles.summary: Democratic lawmakers in the United States stated that an investigation revealed law firm Kirkland and Ellis provided at least 11.8 million dollars in free legal work to President Donald Trump's administration. Representative Jamie Raskin and Senators Richard Blumenthal and Adam Schiff released the findings on November 20, 2026, calling the sum evidence of official coercion. The firm previously entered settlements with the administration following employment practice investigations.
articles.description: Three top Democrats called Trump's dealings with law firms a case of 'official coercion' and pledged investigations.

articles.headline: Severe fuel shortages cause chaos and violence in Malawi
articles.title: ‘Completely messed up everything’: Malawi’s fuel crisis causes chaos
articles.summary: Persistent fuel shortages across Malawi have sparked violence and long queues at filling stations as motorists struggle to secure dwindling supplies. Motorists spend hours waiting for deliveries, while illegal black market sales flourish despite high prices and safety risks. The Human Rights Defenders Coalition planned nationwide demonstrations on November 17, 2026, demanding the energy minister's resignation over the crisis before police postponed the protests due to security constraints.
articles.description: Motorists and businesses struggle as shortages disrupt daily life.

articles.headline: Justice Nagarathna says high offices do not ensure equality
articles.title: Women in high public office doesn’t mean equality throughout society: Justice Nagarathna
articles.summary: Supreme Court Justice B.V. Nagarathna stated that women holding high public office does not prove that societal equality has been achieved. Delivering the Cornelia Sorabji Memorial Lecture at the University of Oxford on November 18, 2026, she emphasized that substantive equality requires addressing intersecting structural disadvantages like caste, class, and unpaid domestic labor. She noted that formal legislation alone cannot guarantee safety, education, or inheritance rights for all women.
articles.description: The Supreme Court judge says a woman may hold a senior position while other women remain excluded from education, employment, property, or effective legal remedies

articles.headline: Nvidia stops shipping advanced artificial intelligence processors to China
articles.title: Nvidia isn’t selling any more AI chips to China
articles.summary: Nvidia halted shipments of its advanced Hopper H200 artificial intelligence chips to China despite previous White House approval. Interim chief executive officer Colette Kress confirmed the shift during an earnings call on Tuesday without providing specific reasons. The pivot follows former chief executive Jensen Huang stepping down amid a scandal and reports of hundreds of thousands of chips stuck in Hong Kong due to import delays.
articles.description: Nvidia has stopped sending its advanced AI chips to China despite the approval it received from the White House to do so in December last year. The announcement was made by interim Nvidia CEO Colette Kress during an earnings call on Tuesday, marking a notable shift for the company that, under former CEO Jensen Huang, […]

articles.headline: Omar Abdullah criticises Centre over delay in Jammu and Kashmir statehood
articles.title: Don't keep us in the dark; don't humiliate us: CM Omar Abdullah to Centre on Jammu and Kashmir Statehood
articles.summary: Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah criticised the Bharatiya Janata Party-led Centre on Wednesday for failing to restore statehood after more than two years in office. Addressing a rally in Poonch district, Abdullah questioned whether the delay was intentional and accused central authorities of unfairly blaming the elected government for security failures outside its control.
articles.description: Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah said the repeated promise of Statehood at an "appropriate time" has become meaningless

articles.headline: Haiti police say 34 gang members killed in capital raid
articles.title: Haiti police say 34 gang members killed in capital raid
articles.description: Haitian police say at least 34 gang members were killed in an operation in the capital city of Port-au-Prince.

articles.headline: Cyclone Akvan shifts track toward Andhra Pradesh and Odisha
articles.title: Cyclone Akvan veers north and may cross anywhere from Narsapur to Puri, 10 Andhra districts on rain alert
articles.summary: Severe cyclonic storm Akvan changed its trajectory toward north coastal Andhra Pradesh and Odisha on Wednesday, prompting the India Meteorological Department to issue heavy rainfall alerts across ten districts. Forecasting models show unprecedented uncertainty regarding the exact landfall point between Narsapur and Puri, while the storm has weakened due to cooler sea waters and atmospheric factors.
articles.description: Extremely heavy rain is likely in Srikakulam, Vizianagaram, Visakhapatnam, ASR, Anakapalli and Kakinada districts on November 19 and 20

articles.headline: Canada embraces artificial intelligence data centres as United States faces public pushback
articles.title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back
articles.summary: Canadian industry leaders and officials are positioning the country as a hub for artificial intelligence data centres as American communities increasingly reject local developments. Alberta has emerged as the centre of this boom, backed by abundant natural gas and government support for projects like Kevin O'Leary's Wonder Valley. However, rising local opposition, water usage concerns, and recent protests in Nova Scotia indicate that public resistance is beginning to surface across Canada.
articles.description: Shark Tank's Kevin O'Leary is among the big investors looking to Canada as a data centre development destination, while his US project faces local opposition.

articles.headline: International Court of Justice to deliver verdict in Rohingya genocide case
articles.title: ICJ to rule on Rohingya genocide case: What to expect
articles.summary: The International Court of Justice in The Hague will deliver its final verdict on Thursday regarding a landmark case filed by The Gambia accusing Myanmar of genocide against the Rohingya minority. Initiated seven years ago with backing from the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation, the case stems from a 2017 military crackdown that forced over 740,000 Rohingya to flee into Bangladesh.
articles.description: The ICJ rules on The Gambia’s genocide case against Myanmar. Here’s what’s at stake for the Rohingya.

articles.headline: Four bodies recovered after migrant boat capsizes off coast of Senegal
articles.title: Four bodies recovered after Senegal boat capsizes amid migration surge
articles.summary: Four bodies were recovered after a migrant boat carrying at least fifty people struck a rock and capsized near Yenne, Senegal, as search operations continue for survivors. According to Horizons Sans Frontieres President Boubacar Seye, the tragic incident coincides with a significant surge in Atlantic migration attempts toward Spain's Canary Islands, prompting growing concern from United Nations agencies and local authorities over rising fatalities along the dangerous maritime route.
articles.description: Search for survivors continues near Yenne as migrant arrivals in Spain's Canary Islands surge by nearly two-thirds.

articles.headline: Donald Trump grants posthumous presidential pardon to baseball player Pete Rose
articles.title: Trump posthumously pardons US baseball legend Pete Rose
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump issued a posthumous and symbolic presidential pardon to late baseball player Pete Rose on Thursday. Rose, who accumulated a record 4,256 career hits playing for Major League Baseball, pleaded guilty to tax evasion in 1990 and received a lifetime ban for gambling. Although reinstated last year, the pardon does not alter his Hall of Fame eligibility.
articles.description: Rose, who died in 2024, was given a lifetime ban from the sport for betting on games but was reinstated last year.

articles.headline: Natural gas explosion kills six people in Tbilisi apartment building
articles.title: Six killed in suspected gas explosion at Georgia apartment building
articles.summary: Six individuals died when a suspected natural gas explosion caused a partial collapse of a residential building in Tbilisi on Thursday morning. Emergency workers rescued a three-year-old girl and an eleven-year-old boy from the wreckage in the Ponichala district. Georgian authorities launched a criminal investigation into safety regulation violations, while the mayor announced temporary relocations for affected families.
articles.description: Georgian Interior Minister Sulkhan Tamazashvili said rescuers had recovered six bodies from the wreckage.

articles.headline: Mahua Moitra accuses BJP supporters of attacking her convoy
articles.title: Mahua Moitra alleges attack on her convoy by BJP supporters
articles.summary: All India Trinamool Congress parliamentarian Mahua Moitra alleged that political opponents targeted her vehicle with stones and eggs in Nadia district. Writing on social media on November 19, 2026, the legislator claimed local law enforcement colluded with approximately ninety members of the opposing party to disrupt her scheduled programme. There was no immediate official response from police or accused groups regarding the incident.
articles.description: BJP leaders said the alleged attack was Ms. Moitra’s attempt to gain attention and conduct self-promotion through social media live videos

articles.headline: Clashes erupt at Medical College in Kolkata following principal gherao
articles.title: Kolkata Medical College violence: West Bengal government, Left student’s unions at loggerheads
articles.summary: Tensions escalated at the Medical College in Kolkata on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, after junior doctors gheraoed the principal and outsiders subsequently attacked protesting students and damaged property. The demonstration followed show-cause notices issued to eight junior doctors who protested during the Chorbagan stampede. The Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad denied involvement in the clashes, while Health Minister Sharadwat Mukherjee criticized the demonstrating medical personnel.
articles.description: Action must be taken against such “dimagi naxals” who have conducted such activities inside the campus, said State Health Minister Sharadwat Mukherjee

articles.headline: Centre seeks more time for Air India crash investigation report
articles.title: AAIB probe report into AI 171 crash at ‘fag end’, Centre tells Supreme Court
articles.summary: The Indian government requested two or three additional weeks to release the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau report regarding the June 12, 2025, Air India Flight 171 crash. The incident killed 241 people at Ahmedabad Airport. Petitioners, including a pilots' body, have criticized the delay and alleged conflicts of interest within the investigation team.
articles.description: The crash at the Ahmedabad Airport killed 12 crew members and 229 passengers on June 12, 2025

articles.headline: Rajasthan Chief Minister Bhajan Lal Sharma approaches three-year term
articles.title: Nearing 3 years as Rajasthan CM, Bhajan Lal Sharma seeks to assert his authority
articles.summary: Nearly three years after Bhajan Lal Sharma assumed office in December 2023 as Rajasthan Chief Minister, Congress State President Govind Singh Dotasara has shifted his criticism from labeling him a remote-controlled leader to accusing him of dismantling the Bharatiya Janata Party within the state. Mr. Sharma was initially selected as a first-time MLA by the central party leadership, drawing early skepticism from political opponents.
articles.description: Having entered office with virtually no administrative experience, his tenure has been a continuous tightrope walk between balancing the demands of the party’s central leadership and build authority of his own within the State.

articles.headline: Apple is hiring engineers to build an AI agent
articles.title: Apple is hiring engineers to build its own AI agent
articles.summary: Apple is actively recruiting engineers to develop a new artificial intelligence assistant capable of executing multi-step tasks across web browsers, applications, and command lines. According to Bloomberg, the initiative involves collaboration between the Siri, user interface frameworks, and foundation models divisions. This development follows recent software updates that expand developer access to Siri integration.
articles.description: Apple is working on its own AI agent that can perform a range of tasks for you, including browsing the web, working across apps, writing code, and calling services. That's according to a now-removed job listing spotted by Bloomberg, which said Apple is looking for an engineer to lead the creation of an agentic AI […]

articles.headline: Democrat Mary Peltola wins Alaska Senate race following extended vote count
articles.title: Democrats win Alaska Senate race two weeks after midterms counting began
articles.summary: Democratic candidate Mary Peltola secured victory in Alaska's closely contested Senate race after two full weeks of ballot tabulation following the November 3 midterm elections. The win grants Democrats their fifty-sixth seat in the upper house and finalizes their control of the United States Congress. The election faced controversy over alleged spoiler candidate tactics and subsequent legal challenges that were ultimately dismissed by federal and state courts.
articles.description: Confirmation of Mary Peltola's victory caps of the party's rout of the Republicans in the midterms Senate election.

articles.headline: Rajasthan High Court declines interim stay on corruption probe against IAS officer
articles.title: Rajasthan High Court denies interim stay in IAS officer corruption probe
articles.summary: The Rajasthan High Court refused an interim stay on Thursday regarding an investigation into senior Indian Administrative Service officer Shikhar Agarwal. The Anti-Corruption Bureau alleged Agarwal abused his position to provide undue benefits to a private firm in exchange for luxury villas. The court directed the state government to respond to the petition within three weeks.
articles.description: The ACB has alleged that IAS officer Agarwal gave benefits such as relaxations in resort construction conditions, approvals without verification of certificates, and special concessional packages to the firm

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh approves first semiconductor plant near Visakhapatnam
articles.title: Andhra’s first semiconductor plant to come up near Visakhapatnam with ₹2,387 crore investment
articles.summary: Advanced System In Package Technologies Private Limited will establish an outsourced semiconductor assembly and test facility in Tarluvada with a ₹2,387 crore investment. Approved under the India Semiconductor Mission, the project aims to create 1,000 jobs. The state government is providing land and infrastructure support to facilitate this high-technology manufacturing venture in the region.
articles.description: The chip assembly and testing unit at Tarluvada is the State’s first project under the India Semiconductor Mission and will create 1,000 jobs

articles.headline: Deutsche Bank chairman supports CEO following leak of internal records
articles.title: Deutsche Bank chair backs CEO after reports expose past lapses; Trump calls tax leak ‘illegal’
articles.summary: Deutsche Bank Chairman Alexander Wynaendts expressed support for Chief Executive Officer Christian Sewing on Tuesday after leaked internal records renewed scrutiny of past client dealings with Russian oligarchs, Donald Trump and Jeffrey Epstein. The disclosures caused bank shares to fall by up to six percent, prompting German Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil to call for an official investigation into the historic failures.
articles.description: Reports cite 15 million leaked records reviewed by more than 200 journalists; German Finance Minister calls for authorities to investigate

articles.headline: Nvidia experiences stock volatility amid former CEO departure
articles.title: A brief history of Nvidia’s recent stock fluctuations
articles.summary: Nvidia shares dropped significantly following the resignation of former chief executive Jensen Huang amid reports of personal misconduct and an independent board investigation. Interim chief executive Colette Kress reported strong financial results for the third quarter with total revenue reaching $115.8 billion. Meanwhile, the company announced that Huang will not be reinstated and is currently searching for a permanent replacement.
articles.description: "We've got this," Colette Kress, interim CEO of Nvidia, said Tuesday night as she closed out the embattled chip company's third quarter earnings call. By Thursday, the company's stock price was hovering at around $150 per share, a nearly 40 percent drop from its all-time high on October 6th, and wiping out a brief post-earnings […]

articles.headline: Karnataka Cabinet orders confiscation of book accused of insulting Basavanna
articles.title: Karnataka Cabinet okays confiscation of book that ‘insults’ Basavanna and ‘distorts’ his philosophy
articles.summary: The Karnataka Cabinet decided on Thursday to confiscate copies of the book Basava Mantapa by author Ravi Hanj following complaints that it distorts the philosophy of Basavanna. Deputy Chief Minister G. Parameshwara announced that legal action will also be taken against publisher Vishveshwar Bhat, as the government seeks to address concerns raised by the Basava Samiti.
articles.description: Basava Samiti has accused U.S.-based author Ravi Hanj of hurting the sentiments of followers of the 12th century social reformer Basavanna in his book ‘Basava Mantapa’

articles.headline: Haitian police report thirty-four suspected gang members killed
articles.title: Haiti police say at least 34 suspected gang members killed in raid
articles.summary: Haitian national police announced that at least 34 suspected gang members were killed during a security operation in the Martissant neighbourhood of Port-au-Prince. Officers conducted the raid alongside an anti-gang task force including personnel from private security firm Vectus Global. The strategic neighbourhood has remained under gang control since 2021, severely disrupting local transport and commerce.
articles.description: Police say the raid targeted the Martissant area, located on a key route out of Port-au-Prince held by gangs since 2021.

articles.headline: Democrat Mary Peltola wins Alaska Senate seat in midterm elections
articles.title: Why Democrat Mary Peltola’s US Senate win in Alaska matters
articles.summary: Democrat Mary Peltola secured a United States Senate seat in Alaska by defeating two-term Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan. According to The Associated Press count, Peltola achieved 50.1 percent of first-choice votes against Sullivan's 45.8 percent, avoiding further rounds in the state's ranked-choice voting system. The victory expands Democratic control of the Senate to 56 seats and marks the first Democratic Senate win in Alaska in over a decade.
articles.description: Peltola’s Alaska win gives Democrats 56 Senate seats and a buffer in Republican states ahead of the 2028 elections.

articles.headline: US President Donald Trump arrives in China for bilateral meetings
articles.title: As Trump arrives in China, low expectations for breakthroughs in rivalry
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump arrived in Shenzhen for his third meeting with Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit. Analysts anticipate few major breakthroughs as the two leaders focus on stabilising bilateral ties amid ongoing trade tensions and recent controversies. The current trade truce between Washington and Beijing is scheduled to expire on January 10, 2027.
articles.description: Analysts expect few concrete outcomes from talks between the leaders on the sidelines of the APEC summit.

articles.headline: International Court of Justice delivers landmark Rohingya judgment
articles.title: The Rohingya question: International solidarity, accountability and the missing road home
articles.summary: The International Court of Justice delivered a landmark judgment regarding the Rohingya community on November 19, 2026, returning the crisis to international attention. A former United Nations official reflected on decades of diplomatic challenges, highlighting that legal recognition is only one part of a much larger struggle. The situation remains deeply rooted in historical, political, and postcolonial disputes surrounding identity and citizenship.
articles.description: The fundamental question remains: how does a community that has been systematically marginalised, displaced and denied its identity reclaim its place in the country it considers home?

articles.headline: West Bengal districts issue alerts for cyclone Akvan
articles.title: Several Bengal districts under alert as cyclone Akvan likely to bring heavy rainfall
articles.summary: Several districts in southern West Bengal, including Kolkata, issued heavy rainfall alerts as cyclonic storm Akvan approaches the coast. According to the India Meteorological Department, the storm was located over the east-central Bay of Bengal on November 19, 2026, and is expected to make landfall between Narsipatnam and Puri. Authorities have cancelled 19 train services and advised fishermen to avoid deep sea areas.
articles.description: Squally winds of 40–50 km/h, gusting to 60 km/h, along and off the West Bengal coast will prevail till Friday noon and ease afterward, with very rough sea conditions, says IMD

articles.headline: Jasprit Bumrah receives widespread acclaim from pundits and peers for exceptional bowling performances.
articles.title: Bumrah — the postman who seldom fails to deliver
articles.summary: India national cricket team fast bowler Jasprit Bumrah has earned global recognition for his exceptional accuracy and skill on the field. Analysts and senior athletes frequently praise his unique bowling action and consistent wicket-taking ability. Discovered by former India coach John Wright, the athlete now requires careful workload management by the national board to preserve his physical condition for major international tournaments.
articles.description: Plucked out from anonymity despite an action that could so easily have put the traditionalists off, he took little time to establish himself as a premier paceman; his unique skill-sets allowed him to flourish anywhere in the world, on any kind of track because he can take the pitch out of the equation effortlessly

articles.headline: Ten killed in Pakistan as bus crashes into gas tanker
articles.title: Ten killed in Pakistan as bus crashes into gas tanker
articles.description: Ten people were killed and at least 27 more injured after a passenger bus collided with an LPG tanker in Pakistan.

articles.headline: Rohingya genocide survivor: ‘perpetrators will have to face consequences’
articles.title: Rohingya genocide survivor: ‘perpetrators will have to face consequences’
articles.description: The International Court of Justice has ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya.

articles.headline: Salvadoran troops expand military operations against armed gangs in Haiti
articles.title: Why are Bukele’s Salvadoran troops in Haiti and what have they achieved?
articles.summary: President Nayib Bukele of El Salvador has deployed approximately 2,500 soldiers to Port-au-Prince following the October kidnapping of four aviation technicians. The military presence has grown into a major offensive alongside local forces to combat armed groups controlling the capital. While desperate residents praise the intervention for addressing severe security crises, monitors report rising casualties and warn of potential risks to civilians.
articles.description: With crowds rallying behind El Salvador's deployment in Haiti, analysts question whether civilians are any safer.

articles.headline: Delhi court orders framing of charges against 14 accused
articles.title: NEET paper leak case: Delhi court orders framing of charges against 14 accused
articles.summary: A Delhi special court directed the formal framing of charges against fourteen individuals on November 18, 2026, in connection with the National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test undergraduate paper leak scandal. Judge Ajay Gupta scheduled the next hearing for November 21, with daily trial proceedings mandated to begin on November 25 following extensive investigations by the Central Bureau of Investigation.
articles.description: The Judge said the court will start the trial on a day-to-day basis from November 25

articles.headline: West Bengal police file FIR against two former state ministers
articles.title: FIR against two former Bengal Ministers over sexual assault charges
articles.summary: Authorities lodged a First Information Report at Baguiati Police Station against former ministers Indranil Sen and Bratya Basu. Social activist Rajib Sarkar filed the case on behalf of department employees alleging sexual assault, rape, and corruption. The accused previously served in the Trinamool Congress government led by then Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee.
articles.description: Five former Ministers, who had been part of Mamata Banerjee’s cabinet, have been arrested since the BJP government came to power in May 2026

articles.headline: How vaccine fears fuelled a major measles comeback in the US
articles.title: How vaccine fears fuelled a major measles comeback in the US
articles.description: Measles is making a comeback in the US as vaccination rates fall.

articles.headline: US judge allows defamation lawsuit by Trump against media companies
articles.title: Trump’s case against NYT and Penguin Random House may proceed: Judge
articles.summary: United States District Judge Steven Merryday ruled that a defamation lawsuit filed by President Donald Trump against The New York Times and Penguin Random House may proceed. The legal action targets articles and a book concerning Trump's business background and 2024 election campaign. Defendants denied the allegations, arguing the case lacks legal merit.
articles.description: The lawsuit cited a book about Trump by two NYT reporters and what it said were 'false, malicious, defamatory' articles.

articles.headline: Cyclonic storm Akvan strengthens off coast of Andhra Pradesh
articles.title: Akvan strengthens into severe cyclonic storm, but further intensification not likely
articles.summary: The India Meteorological Department reported that Cyclonic Storm Akvan intensified into a severe system located approximately five hundred eighty kilometers east of Chennai on November 18, 2026. Weather specialists indicated that the system is projected to cross the coastline between Nellore and Visakhapatnam with sustained wind speeds reaching up to one hundred ten kilometers per hour, prompting regional forecasts for isolated thunderstorms and squally weather conditions.
articles.description: The system may cross the A.P. coast between Nellore and Visakhapatnam as a Severe Cyclonic Storm on November 20, and not as a Very Severe Cyclonic Storm as earlier predicted

articles.headline: India and Japan review defence and strategic ties in Tokyo
articles.title: India, Japan set to review defence ties as Rajnath, Jaishankar arrive in Tokyo
articles.summary: Indian Defence Minister Rajnath Singh and External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar arrived in Tokyo to co-chair the fourth 2+2 ministerial dialogue with Japanese counterparts Shinjiro Koizumi and Toshimitsu Motegi. According to the Ministry of External Affairs, the discussions focus on maritime security, defence technology, and regional stability in the Indo-Pacific following the recent Quad summit.
articles.description: The two-day visit comes a day after the Quad leaders' summit in Manila, Philippines and as India hosts a joint humanitarian assistance and disaster relief (HADR) exercise involving the four member countries

articles.headline: Supreme Court clarifies countdown timeline after individual arrest
articles.title: When does the 24-hour countdown begin after arrest? Supreme Court answers
articles.summary: The Supreme Court of India ruled on November 5, 2026, that the constitutional twenty-four-hour magistrate production timeline begins at the exact moment of initial detention rather than formal arrest. Justices Ujjal Bhuyan and Atul S. Chandurkar examined Article 22 clause 2 of the Constitution to establish this legal precedent regarding personal liberty and custody limits.
articles.description: The Supreme Court ruled that the 24-hour custody limit under Article 22(2) of the Indian Constitution begins when a person’s liberty is curtailed during detention, not from the formal arrest

articles.headline: Pakistani man sentenced to prison for 2024 plot to kill Donald Trump
articles.title: Pakistani man convicted of plotting to kill Trump is sentenced to over 27 years in prison
articles.summary: A federal court in Brooklyn sentenced 48-year-old Asif Merchant to 330 months in prison for attempting to commit transnational terrorism and murder for hire. According to the United States Department of Justice, the Pakistani national plotted in 2024 to assassinate President Donald Trump and other prominent politicians at the behest of Iran in retaliation for the 2020 killing of Qassem Soleimani.
